text: At first use I thought this was a great charger. But after further use it’s just ok. It works. The package included the charger, charging cord for charger and pouch. There is a small flip out tray that conveniently holds your phone while charging. The charger arrived charged at 83%. If you have any of the newer smart devices you know they do not work with the old chargers. So this one being a fast charger is a plus. It did charge my phone rather quickly, but when I went to recharge the charger it took over 8 hours to charge. As far as it being portable is is kind of heavy. So would not carry well in a purse. It’s also larger than normal so may not fit in your pockets. It may be nice to keep handy in a car. Overall I don’t know if I got a bad one. With it taking so long to recharge, but that was a definite turn off for me.

I just got this phone yesterday. I was pretty successful setting it up the way I wanted it. However, a couple phone setting dont work?? It gives you the opportunity to set a reminder sound if you miss a call or text message. I have it set for 3 minutes. Well it doesnt Work!! That is 1 of my favorite settings because lets face it, we are not holding are phones all day, so we ARE going to miss messages & calls. VERY DISSAPOINTED!! I had a Galaxy ON5 & absolutely Loved that phone. It did Everything!!! By the time I try & return this phone, wait for another, its just not feasible. Tried to Upgrade but this Galaxy A10E is NOT a Better phone. My first Galazy phone that is disappointing!

This mount is stiffer and therefore more secure as far as bouncing around than a standard clip on, plastic GPS mount. But it is harder to attach and is only friction mounted; no clip to attach fully and more securely to the vent. However the metal cross bar at the bottom does help keep the GPS from vibrating while driving. But it's very expensive; about 3-4x the cost of a plastic pronged mount. The ball is higher on the mount than it initially appears, so you need to pay more attention to where it's mounted on your vent so as not to block your radio or other controls. I had to mount this as low as possible on my vents or else the GPS was so high it blocked my radio. You will need plenty of finger strength to mount it securely--twisting the knob requires a LOT of force. That is the ONLY way to get a secure mount. You can't use a wrench since the knob is plastic and you will damage it. Even so, friction only goes so far--on a recent road trip (paved roads) after some minor bumps the entire mount fell off onto my console. A hassle, needless to say. I bought two of these; I won't be buying any more.

I orginally purchased this phone as a backup for my boyfriend. He had drop his other phone in water, twice, and I knew it was just a matter of time before he needed a new one. He works from home most of the time, so he really only needs something just in case. He mostly texts but when he does make a call its pretty good. Camera is descent too. Battery life is good, charges quick. Other than that, it's not the greatest phone. The keyboard is too close together causing him to constantly type out ddouble ifff not tttrible llettersss(-you see how that might be annoying)The send button is also too close causing him to send blank messages at times. Now, not sure if this following issue has more to do with service plan(safelink) or the phone but I'm leaning more toward the phone. Text messages don't always come through immediately. I've text him saying I'm on my way home and I walk in the door 20 mins later and he is only getting it then. Happens more often then it should and that's not very reliable. He's been with safelink for years, with different phones, and that's never been a problem before. Another thing he doesn't like is that you cannot set specific texts alert for specific people only ringtones which seems odd nowadays. For what it is, it's OK. Don't expect a lot here, it's simple just to get a message across, some of the time.

The screen itself feels solid, and went on pretty easily. We will have to wait to see how it holds up with time though. I don't care much for the black border, but it doesn't really take away from any screen area I use. Maybe just slivers around the sides, but that isn't too important to me. I also don't like the lack of equipment included. There is not a card to smooth out the screen like other products have. There is also only one wet cloth for two screens, and no drying cloth. I am being really nit-picky and they don't matter much to me, but those have been included in most other screen protectors I have bought in the past.

I bought this as recommended by the Amazon Kindle specialists because my Kindle Fire was not responding to touches when I wanted to highlight items and such. I was told that this product would take care of the problem. Maybe it does, but I now have bubbles on the screen. I read the directions, watched all the videos on the website, and I still couldn't put this on without ending up with bubbles. I'm waiting to see whether it is worth leaving it on the Fire (if it works better despite the bubbles), but I am not pleased or impressed with this product. For the record, the package comes with two sheets so that if you goof or one sheet needs to be replaced you can use the 2nd. I ended up using both sheets. The 2nd one definitely came out better than the first, but I'm still not happy with it. It seems that I have simply replaced one issue with another. I haven't yet tried to watch a movie on the screen, but the bubbles aren't showing up when I am reading, so I am hoping that the bubbles are either small enough to not make a difference or that they won't show up at all when the device is in use. I am still dissatisfied but it looks like the product will do what it is meant to do-for awhile, anyway.

First, love this brand, have purchased before. Has survived multiple drops daily from weak grip, and the phone inside has remained undamaged. This is good, it's mostly why I continue to purchase. I need a thinner touch screen because sometimes my fingers aren't picked up by the phone, and it's always a struggle to find a good case that can pair with a good screen protector. So this is good too. Due to sick season I needed to sanitize my device more which I guess removed the glue that keeps the plastic connected to the case (which is doubly kept in place between case and phone) but sometimes will partially pop out in a fall. This is not good. Doesn't matter how much, or what I use, to wipe down the screen, or how many times I wash my hands, it doesn't keep fingerprints off either. And heaven forbid if I have a phone call, my clean cheek has more oil than a mcdonalds according to the phone case screen. Overall it's a solid case, and I guess does its job protecting my phone from all my fingerprints (ew), but difficult to keep spotless.

I am no "newbie" to putting on screen protectors. I would actually consider myself to be pretty good. But these are getting pretty frustrated. I have now gone threw all 3 screen protectors and every time gotten dust underneath. after each one i took even more time to get ore precise and had my process and technique down to a science (so i thought). and no luck still SOO much dust underneath. I don't know where it's coming from... i am looking into glare of the light and using the sticker to get every SPECK of dust off the glass, then screen protector goes on, and BOOM somehow there are like 10 specks of dust that got trapped. I blame the THICK backing of the screen protector. It's not the thin film that comes off all easy, it's a thick piece of plastic, and i feel like the when that comes off, it fans dust onto the sticky backing of the screen protector... only think i can think of. I have never had this much trouble with screen protectors before... UGH

Awesome case, easy to attach. However...I'm currently questioning if it was suppose to come with a screen protector, as there was none in the box. Oddly enough, it include the cleaning cloth and a small card to assist in applying said non-existent screen protector ;) Any-who, this wasn't a problem since I had already purchased a 2-pack of protectors which arrived at the same time as the case, so everything worked out quite dandy. :D Oh yes, I'm suppose to be reviewing the case... Well, simply put: Pros: Easy to apply Sturdy Has 2 layers of protection (soft internal case and rigid external) Looks awesome Cons: Erm....it wasn't free? I'm quite satisfied, to say the least. 5-stars Update: Well, it was a great case for a while. Unfortunately this case leaves a huge blind spot the screen (as with most cases.) After using the case on my SII for about 3 months, it fell off my desk (about 3 feet) and the lcd screen (the only one that really matters) was destroyed. I thought it might be a fluke, so I gave the case to a friend who had an SII when I upgraded to the S3. Sadly, about a month later he dropped his phone on a sidewalk while walking, and guess what? Broken lcd. A shame, really. Otterbox is a good brand, this case however, needs some tweaking.

Cover was received already full of finger marks and a scratch right in the middle of the back cover. The cover fits the iPhone well. The small cover cutout for the back camera is difficult to to put in place. The iPhone’s back is very sleek, which makes it prone to slide in smooth surface. The back NOHON cover mimics that all too well, I mean, it does not add any type of protection to avoid all that sliding and falling, as other covers due. I understand that it might be by design, but the main reason for a cover is to add protection, no? Otherwise, why have the cover?

Too heavy, bulky. Only works with a few Samsung phones. Biggest gripe is that the controls are up on the headset itself (no remote control) which means that you have to keep holding your arm up. This is fine for ten minutes of just playing around, but gets extremely tedious and eventually painful after an hour or more. The Google Daydream View is much better, and even though it at the time (December 2016) is only compatible with the Google Pixel and Pixel XL more phones, from a number of manufacturers, are on the way. Unlike the Samsung Gear VR will only ever be compatible with a small number of Samsung phones.

*Not sure why the product is labeled as iPhone 14 Plus on my review, but the review is for the iPhone 14 Pro* I purchased this screen protector directly from Zagg so that I would have a screen protector for my iPhone 14 Pro as soon as it arrived. The order from Zagg was placed on September 10th, 2022. I’m hoping they’ll be updating the design to fit the 14 Pro in the near future, but if you’re getting the first batch, please be aware that the camera cutout is just a touch low compared to the Dynamic Island camera. It might not be a big deal to everyone, but it drove me crazy, so I bought another brand on Amazon. If having things lined up perfectly is a deal breaker for you, this product probably isn’t the right one (for the time being - today is September 17th, 2022). Also, it does come with an install kit, so with the install kit, the fit is incorrect. You might be able to move it up slightly to fit without using the install guide, but I didn’t have an opportunity to try that.

I purchased 3 Zizo Bolt cases. One was for my work phone - a Galaxy S8. The others are for two family phones - both LG G7 ThinQs. These cases are solid and feel like they offer superior protection to most other cases I have owned for other phones. I think the styling is top notch, and the color options offer something for everyone. The screen protective glass is also top quality and easy to put on without air bubbles. I would prefer a slide in holster, but that is personal preference. The clip-in holster is functional and works well. All that said, there is a major problem with the kickstand. The piece that connects between the back of the kickstand and back of the case is horribly designed. The piece itself is fragile, and it does not slide well. This combination results in easily broken kickstands. It broke on my S8 case the first time I opened it. I forgot to warn my son about this, and it broke on his G7 case the first time he opened it. This could easily have been a 5 star review, but when something is of such low quality that it breaks on first use, it ruins the product for me. My kickstand has not broken on my G7 yet, but this is only because I have been hyper careful when opening it. If you are looking for a case to simply protect your phone, and you do not want, need, or use a kickstand, then get this case. If a functional kickstand is important to you, then get something else.

After reviewing that the glass protectors don’t really work on these Apple watches I figured I could get this protector instead. Pros 1. Size: Doesn’t add any size to your watch. 2. Multiple Protectors: Nice that their is two just in case one doesn’t work out. 3. Price: Price is pretty reasonable. 4. Cut-Outs: Precise and I have no issues. 5. Touchscreen: Works as if the protector isn’t even on it. Cons 1. Sweat- As you can see by the pictures, the sweat gets right underneath it. It sucks. Only way of course you can clean it, is by removing the bands and then the protector. So if your gonna work out, be cautious. Once I noticed the issue with the sweat, I decided to just return the package. Great protection but if sweat is a possible thing everyday with wearing the watch, can’t deal with it. If this review helped you, then click the Helpful link right below.

It is a good value and it does replace the stocks glass however be aware that the glass can actually come in the kit with some smudges. Look very closely under a bright light and carefully clean the glass on both sides with the cleaning kit supplied. The first glass installation had to be reminded due to bad blurred glass right out of the packaging. It was not my fingerprints on it. Fortunately the second glass is supplied and after removing the first one and cleaning the second one thoroughly all is well now on the camera now. This kit is recommended but be smart and use much caution on the installation process.

The first night, my watch failed to charge. It WAS charging when I initially place it, so I don't know if it got bumped out of place or what. I suspect this is the case because placing the phone on the charger in the dark from bed was a ROYAL pain. The 2nd night, all devices charged properly. However, I am a go-to-bed-and-read person. When looking for a charger stand for my trio of Apple products, I preferred one that allowed the watch to sit in Nightstand position. This fit the bill. I didn't consider what a pain it would be to reach from prone position in bed to where my charger sits, and accurately hit the little lightening prong for the phone. After fighting with it for a couple of nights, I've given up and am returning. I located one that is magsafe - MUCH easier to "hit the target" when reaching to place on the charger.

The application of the first IQ Shield protector did not go well. Although I watched the video and followed its instructions, particles of dirt remained after application. These did not "heal" within a couple of days. After describing this to the seller a complete replacement screen protector package was sent to me. This time (contrary to the sellers advice) I scrubbed the glass screen with isopropyl alcohol and then used a commercial compressed gas "duster". I then applied the device as described in the video. Doing so required careful attention to its position, aided by an LED flashlight- the screen position is not easy to see, as it is of course transparent. The presence of the detergent liquid made re-positioning easy. Despite careful use of the supplied squeegee about a dozen bubbles remained. Within 24 hours these were gone. The result is cosmetically and functionally good. The application process required more care than I expected. The OnePlus 3 comes with a flexible screen protector already applied, but it is rather inadequate. It is possible that removing it before applying the IQ Shield leaves a residue that requires scrubbing.

This mount has some great qualities and some annoying ones. First, the great: it's super easy to mount and the bracket stays in place no problem. The grips on the side and the included rubber flex bands hold the phone very securely. I have no worries about my phone's security/safety when I'm out on a ride. Now the not so great: This mount is designed to be adjustable/rotatable, but, it's kind of not. The ring on the back side of the mount doesn't seem to get tight enough. The slightest bump and the mount tilts up or down out of view. As far as rotating, it does rotate. It will rotate a full 360 degrees and looks great...as long as your not moving. As soon as I start riding the phone auto-rotates back to portrait and won't stay in landscape. All-in-all it's a good mount that holds the phone very securely but doesn't perform some of the functions as promised.

First, I was in love with this stitch phone cover when I bought it, I mean it is so cute who wouldn't, but do not let his cuteness get you to buy this product. The first time I used the wrist strap, the strap came unscrewed and my phone fell on the sidewalk and the screen broke. The straps do not stay on so wouldn't use. Then his ears started ripping and his body started detaching from the case and you guessed it the return period was up so I am stuck with a falling apart case, I can not use nor return.

I've had the case for about two days now, and though I thought it was great the first few hours, I'm not so hot about it now. The case screen is... odd. It's too far from the phone screen, but it's not too bad when you have a glass protector between the case and the screen. But as soon as you put it in your pocket, the air presses from the inside and sticks to your phone screen, making that annoying puddle-like effect. I found that if you push on the sides, the air returns and it's not that big of a deal, but it's still very annoying to have to do it every time you pull it from your pocket. I haven't tried the belt clip for longer than a few minutes, but I didn't like how it covered the lock and volume buttons. I also noticed that it was made out of brittle plastic, a bit lower quality then one would want in a phone case. It was also kind of hard to snap the two pieces back together once I got the phone in. What I hate most, is if I choose to keep the case on, I'd have to deal with the charging and headphone flaps. They're much harder to keep open than most cases, and they hinder plugging your phone in and keeping it charging. It puts pressure on the underside of your charger and pushes it out of the port. Which sucks, but I'm very clumsy, so I'm going to make it work.

A few things here. A. The actual housing for the airtag is nice with quality feeling metal, however, it doesn’t fit the airtag on both sides. One side feels like the fit is nice and snug while the other side feels like they didn’t make an attempt. I think they just manufacture the same part and include two of them when the shape of the airtag is not the same on both sides. B. The ‘leather’ that connects the airtag holder and the keychain wore out already and fell apart. I was able to fix this but eliminating it completely. I just simply undid the screws holding what little bit of the fake leather to the keychain but and put my key ring through the airtag holder. Just don’t have a clip. C. The magnets holding the holder together and kinda weak. If you just leave your keys in your bag or backpack all the time like I do you’ll be fine. But if you take them in and out and in a lot there is a possibility that the magnets can give out if you hold the keys by the airtag. Not a reason to not buy this, but something to be aware of. I would buy again if I needed more airtags and I wish it was in more colors but the aluminum feels good and overall of a good value. Don’t pay more than $10.

Easy to install, air bubbles were easy to remove, and it fits well. My only complaint is, unlike every other screen protector I’ve ever had, if you chip or crack this one then it will continue to come apart in shards. As you can see by the picture, they’re large and continue to break off 2 weeks after I originally dropped and cracked my screen. My previous screen protector tou could remove from the phone and crumple it in your hand with out as much as a glitter of glass. I wouldn’t purchase again, because I don’t like having to replace my screen protector for minor chips or cracks. Otherwise, it’s cheap and comes with 4 screens so that’s cool.

The screen protector does its job! My husband has been through two of these as have I. The screenprotector cracked but it saved the screen on my phone. I do think that the screen protector cracks too easily. It will crack with minor bumps to the screen protector. There is a small circle at the bottom of the screenprotector that is supposed to be more sensitive to the fingerprint scanner, however I have had to redo my fingerprints a few times to get it to work consistently. It is very frustrating. I have had no issues with the protector for the camera lens other back of the phone. I do like that it came with 2 front screen protectors as well as 2 camera protectors. All-in-all, not bad for the price.

This is a cute wallet. It does exactly what it is supposed to do. I just have two problems with it. 1. It is definitely NOT cowhide which is what it is advertised to be and what I wanted. 2. The wristlet portion is separate and connects to the phone and not to the wallet. If you don't care for leather than this is a great little wallet. Everything stays put. The magnet is strong and does a great job keeping the phone in place. You can definitely get a phone wallet that is of equal or even better quality for a cheaper price. I hope they change the description to accurately describe what you are truly purchasing.

This is a case, with a holster. The case has two parts: (1) a soft rubber inner case that fits around the 5X snugly and I think provides good impact protection, (2) a hard plastic outer case, into which the inner case fits. As a CASE for the 5X, I'd give it 5 stars. It makes the 5X easier to hold and likely provides good protection. For my use, I got this product looking for a holster, more than a case. I've used holsters a lot in the past, so have some expectations. Like the best holster I've used before, this one slides the phone in, phone face toward hip. It has some sort of felt-like material to protect screen and reduce friction as you take it in and out of the holster. As a holster, I'd have to give this product 4 stars. The reason is that the soft rubber inner case, rubs against the holster. It is particularly noticeable when pulling the phone out. Then, the hole for the charging port at the bottom of the phone stretches as it rubs against the felt. It feels like only a matter of time before it breaks. And I believe that the soft rubber part of the case might be increasing friction as it's pulled out of the case, making it somewhat more difficult to get. Not a "quick draw" holster. The price was good, and the product well constructed, but I'd ask designers to reduce friction in the holster, and do something different around the 5X charging port.

Worked great for about 6 or 8 months and then started to wear down. The front always got dusty and cloudy so the front facing camera was almost useless and I would have to take it apart to wipe the back facing camera often. Pros 1. Waterproof 2. Slim (for a waterproof case) 3. Feels good swiping your screen Cons 1. Makes your front facing camera useless 2. Can get dusty on the rear camera very easily 3. Had complaints from people that they couldn't hear me on the phone 4. Water started to get in after 6 or 8 months, so I had to ditch the case.

The case has arrived today along with another I purchased from a different company and although this one has a pocket deep enough to store items along with your phone, it is difficult for a Galaxy Note 5. The phone portion holds the Note 5 well but leaves no room for the headphones to just be inserted at the bottom through the three little holes. I have inserted a picture of what one of the holes looks like after one attempt of plugging in my headphones. I found that I need to put my phone in almost all the way, then insert the headphone plug and then push my phone all the way in otherwise it cannot be done when the phone is fully placed into the holder. There is a headphone hole at the bottom as seen in the picture but it leads into the pocket portion of the case rather than the phone portion. Poor design choice. The holders velcro is very strong but too short and feels like I'm squeezing the life out of my arm when wearing it on my upper arm. I lift weights so my biceps are larger than most ladies and I have to wear the armband on my forearm. It was the phone armband with more bells and whistles than the other cheaper one I bought and yet the cheaper one managed to be much more efficient.

I wanted to like this phone but unfortunately didn't. On one hand it is very affordable, has a nice design and finish on the back cover, supports dual SIM and comes with basically stock Android 10 with no bloatware, 64GB internal memory and 4GB RAM, pretty good specs. On the other hand, it is too big. That might be just me though, and other people might probably see this as a pro. Also, the screen doesn't have the best resolution (720p), which paired with the big size, makes everything look a bit blurry. The fingerprint reader on the back was also difficult to use and most of the time it wouldn't recognize my fingerprint even though I set it up twice as if they were 2 different fingers. Face unlock was slow and also would often fail. I ended up selling the phone and got a new Moto X4, which is a 2017 model but much more enjoyable to use.

Nice phone case. Love the card holder with mirror. It secured very well, but i didnt get to use it long. The one draw back of this case, in my opinion, is the ribbed back design of it. Because of the texture it makes it very difficult to place a ring on the back of the case, or a pop socket. I had a ring on mine thinking that it would hold and it didn't, the ring came off of the case and my phone fell into the water. My fault though, I should've known the texture on the back couldn't hold that accessory.

Update - 3 months later the ring fell off the back. :’( Now I have no ring to hold my phone. Not sure what to get now. ————— Just got my phone case today and I love it! I actually bought one for my iPhone X and just went to my orders so I could order the exact same kind for my iPhone 11 Pro. The only drawback of this case is it doesn’t allow Qi charging. I have to take it off for that. But the case is actually really easy to get off, yet it stays on really well. My old case (same brand) didn’t show any signs of stretching out despite my nervous habit of pushing the case off and back on again over and over on one corner. I love the ring on the back! I can hold my phone securely in my hand without fear of dropping it. It’s an added safety measure when I’m walking around with it, or lying in bed and I fall asleep (it doesn’t fall on the floor). I like the color addition also. It will probably fade over time as my silver X case dad along the edges, but that’s ok. It’s been my favorite case so far.

After a couple of months, this case still does its job. It protects my IPhone 11 and charges the battery whenever I run it low. Recently, though, it started disconnecting itself when I have it plugged in to my car using Apple Car Play. I took my phone out of this case and plugged it in directly and had no Car Play issues. When I called the company, the rep said he was surprised my iPhone 11 worked with Car Play at all as it usually won’t, especially after an update. In other words, the case is fine. It’s not supposed to work with Apple Car play. They apparently expect you to remove your phone from their case every time you plug in to use Apple Car Play. I said they should mention that in their Amazon description.

The OtterBox for the iPhone 5 came with a screen protector. As others have noted, it is extremely difficult to install the screen protector, and then wrap the box around it without pulling the screen protector away from the screen. And, you only get one try before the 'glue' that holds the protector against the screen fails, and the protector is no longer of any use. At that point it is either buy another screen protector, or do without. I bought another brand and it held fine when I put the OtterBox in place, which means that OtterBox COULD HAVE included a protector that would hold.

Ok i would give it 3.5 if I could. The good points are: - Good story, the whole thing with leaving and coming back .. and how the world viewed the whole thing while superman was away is cool, also the almost dying stuff .. it's so close to the comic books way of story telling - The action is great - visually it's very good - stayed true to the original series in terms of atmosphere, and general mood The Bad Points: -The dude is too much of a pretty boy to be Superman, he would make a great Superman son .. or a good younger superman brother .. who's playful and not as solemn as his older brother .. the Superman .. he's also too soft - loius is too knock-out georgous in an eye-candy type of way, not in the assertive, attractive, go-getter, feisty reporter type of way. The finger strap is made of thin rubber and the metal thing doesn't slide down too easy. I hope it's durable. I thought the color would be a bit more shiny or bold but still pretty. You can feel the grooves of the designs. Update Sep. 14th : The stand is not real metal and it broke today. I thought it could easily go back in but then the hinges broke cause it's plastic. The color on back is getting scratched off. I hope the rubber fiber grip part stays secure

The screen protector seems solid, had to watch the video in the link supplied with the instruction to understand what's what exactly in order to understand the written instructions. In addition, the stickers that are suppose to be used to hold the screen protector in place before removing the adhesive side sticker just don't hold in place and keep falling off, which resulted in me having to manually re-position the protector again, which in turned means I ended up with a few small bubbles that I can't get rid of. Also, the bubble remover plastic card is flimsy at best, it folds almost like paper. Otherwise, the protector itself seems of good quality, haven't been using it long though, just an hour or two so far.

The band is ok (for the price, I didn't expect it to be great but I've bought other bands from other brands for similar prices that exceeded my expectations). It is stiff out of the box (as expected). Installing it wasn't a breeze. I bought the 22mm band for my Galaxy watch 3 45mm and it was a very tight fit between the lugs. The spring bars were the issue (the quick release bars wouldn't retract completely, making install more difficult than it should be). I had to try a few times and wiggle the band around to get it to lock in (unlike other 22mm bands I own). I was also scared the bars would scratch the lugs (luckily, it didn't). The strap also felt cheap to touch (it was "genuine leather" after all, and not top grain or full grain leather). Again, I own cheaper bands that actually feel better to touch. Durability is a question mark since I owned it for all of two days.

I’ve been using a plastic SIM card holder with pockets the last few years. With usage the pockets stretched just enough that they no longer held the SIM cards securely. The SIM cards easily fell out. So I purchased this SIM card holder. The good: SIM cards are easily inserted into the pocket. The SIM cards are very well secured in place and there is no way that they will fall out. The not so good: It’s VERY difficult to remove the SIM cards if you don’t have long fingernails. I’m a guy and I keep my nails trimmed. So I find it difficult to get my nail under the top edge in order to pull out a SIM card. I find it easier to carry a small set of tweezers with me to pull on the top of the SIM while flexing the holder in order to expose the top of the SIM card. It’s better than my old plastic one because the SIM cards will never fall out once they have been slid into the pocket.

Does its job. I tested it with the phone and tablet (both Samsung Galaxy). With the phone I started with the charger at 60% and phone at 33%. After half hour charger at 36% (-24%), phone at 58% (+25%). so the rate of charge /discharge about the same. and 25% in 30 minutes isn't bad. With the tablet i started with the charger at 100%. After 45 minutes the charger dropped to 61% (-39%) but the tablet only gained 18% charge. So at about half the rate, and only 18% after 45 minutes. For all the techies out there that will say dahh... the Tablet battery is probably twice the capacity of the charger but about the same as the phone. The answer is probably yes. Still the overall charging rate is fairly slow. Regardless, in a pinch while traveling and away from a wall these will work their magic and keep you alive and connected. More so with a phone than a tablet. Please be careful though with the charger, when plugged in to the phone or tablet, they can be used, but the charger is thicker than the device, so when you place it on any surface, you may be applying torque on the USB-C connector and port and can damage one or both.

I really like this case and I’m only giving this case two stars because it takes on whatever smell it’s around. I know this is super weird but it’s true! And it’s so gross! The gym that I climb at uses old tires on the ground under the routes and I set my phone on the ground for ONE route and I picked it up and it smelt AWFUL. This hasn’t happened with anything else I’ve brought there and set on the ground (water bottles, sandals, hair binders, other phone cases) Like worse then the room itself smells. I went to the bathroom, took the case off and cleaned it off with soap and it got a little better. I also got an oil change and just the fumes of the oil change while I was sitting in my car made the phone smell. I still use it because I paid for it and it is a nice case in every other respect, but it’s super weird. Maybe you don’t you have these weirdly specific problems that I have, it won’t be an issue but just a warning.

I'm really disappointed that these are not fast charging cables despite being listed as fast chargers. I bought both this Micro USB and the USB C versions of these cables as I have a mixed environment. I really needed these micro USB to USB A charging cables for charging a Samsung Tablet. I really like right angle cables so this was an added bonus. Unfortunately, after trying all 3 of the micro USB to USB A cables, none of them are fast charging. I checked them using the Accubattery app and one is dead (0% charging speed), one is 3%/hr and one is 4%/hr. My last remaining fast charging cable (5 years old) charges at 23%/hr and a basic non-fast charging cable from a 1 dollar store charges at 4%/hr (all tested the same way and using the same devices). So these cables are not fast charging and were not worth the cost as they are no better than a $1 cable. With the slow charging, these cables are also incapable of charging my micro USB power banks. Conversely, the similar USB C version cables are fast charging and will charge my phone and a USB power bank in a reasonably short period of time.

Good in concept, but not for every vehicle. The specifications note that it will fit most models of phones, but they don't mention anything about the car. I drive a Honda Fit. The steep slope of the windshield and long dashboard does not allow the holder to come anywhere near within arms reach of the phone. I would think this applies to most compact cars with sloping roofs and long dashboards (IE: Fit, Prius, Beetle, etc). I had to mount it to the top of the windshield but, because of the long flexible extension arm, the phone bounces wildly while driving.

I actually liked this case a lot its was a perfect fit for the iphone 5, the grip is great and besides for looking really cute its a hard case so when you drop your phone it secures it and protects it from breaking. I just have one issue which is why I don't use the case anymore: The home button is rubber which sticks out but its really hard to push down and it was hurting my thumb, so I cut off the rubber piece not knowing that you cant even reach the real home button at all (because of the plastic case circling around it). So I just have it sitting in my drawer. But over all if you have a super strength thumb. I say go for it.

I've purchased both versions of this case (clear and opaque) and describe them separately below... ~ CLEAR VERSION ~ As far as phone cases go, this is as minimalist as you can get. Don't expect much protection if your phone falls on concrete. It's probably more appropriate for falls on indoor flooring, such as vinyl or carpet. With that said, this case looks great on the S6 edge and fits perfectly. My only real complaint is how scratch-prone it is. I noticed scratches immediately after installing this case, caused by the phone's aluminum edges rubbing against it. If you have a Black Sapphire S6 edge, these scratches are quite visible. ~ OPAQUE VERSION ~ There are numerous differences between this and the clear-backed case. First, the plastic in this version is a bit thicker and sturdier than the clear case. The lips around the edges are a bit more pronounced, wrapping around the phone a little more. There is also a padded surface on the interior, protecting the glass back of your S6 edge. All of this amounts to better protection against drops, while maintaining a very thin profile. It doesn't look as good as the clear-backed version, but withstands scratches better and doesn't show dust that may get in between the case and phone. I would recommend this version of the case over the clear cover. Note: Both versions of this case do a good job at protecting the camera-bulge and screen when placed on a flat surface.

This case is not exactly as I expected. It's pretty much like the silicone covers -- slim and flexible. I wanted to have a little more proctection (or at least a case that feels like it will protect my phone just a bit more). The product is simple enough, but I dislike the very glossy top and bottom portions of the cover. I know there a few photos on the page, but I feel it is more glossy than the photo can capture. Unfortunately, I didn't even try it out on my phone to see how well it fits, so I can't comment on that; I have returned the product.

I LOVE the Jawbone line of headsets and have been using them since version 1. I have been using this this current version of the ERA for a while now and after researching what its competitors have to offer ordered another (2) ERA Silver Streaks. One with charger, one without. I handle it this way because the the ONLY downside to these headsets is their battery life and thus the purchase of two and the charging case. I rotate them back and forth on busy days! Deplete the battery on the first, throw it in the charger and use the 2nd while the first is charging. It works great. This particular ERA however came DOA (dead on arrival) out of the box so I had to send it back. This is why the bad rating. And, I went right back out and ordered another to take its place. They really are that good! Someone at Jawbone needs to wake up and begin development and marketing of this headset again as it is fantastic in its current state and with some specific improvements could be the leader in this area for many years to come. Most non-technical people aren't familiar with the Jawbone line and if made aware of how good they are/were, they would tear it up!

I've not purchased many items on amazon until recently, so my navigation skills when trying to find products were a little rusty. I ordered the wrong size (I think) because it definitely didn't fit my phone. I spoke with the seller, and they weren't very nice about me wanting a refund or exchange. All in all, it was a very hard case, seemed durable, and when I decided all I wanted from it was the peacock...it was SO HARD to pull off. So if you want it to stay on the case, I don't think there will be a problem.

It does what it is supposed to do and it is exactly what they designed it for. Although there are some plastic parts that do concern me if it falls on that area. I haven't test dropped it because I don't want to ruin my iPhone 5c. The only issue I had was that my package was opened and sealed with clear tape. It may have been the USPS out of concern, but it was strange and unprofessional of them. Update: After using for a few months now. It's does have it's pros and cons (more pros than cons). Pro: does protect the iPhone 5C pretty well since it's made part rubber and plastic. It does come with a little piece of plastic on the back to hold it up (like for watching videos) and protects it the screen if I leave it with the screen down. (about a 1-2 cm from the flat surface). Cons: Unfortunately the only con is that it gets difficult to use the IOS menus like using that swipe from the bottom up (or notifications with the swipe from up to down) to show icons such as the airplane mode/wi-fi/bluetooth/etc. Therefore, it does make it difficult to reach things that are on the corner or sides of the screen.

I really wanted to give this 5 stars, but after having it 2 weeks the clasp began to loosen and it comes open all the time now. Yesterday I was wearing it to work but when I got to work it wasn’t on my wrist, I spent the whole morning searching the parking lot, my car...I looked everywhere and couldn’t find it. When I got home I was so upset that I had lost my $400 Apple Watch after only having it a month. Luckily when I walked into my bedroom is was laying on the floor. The clasp must have come open when I put my jacket on and slipped then off. Wish the company sent multiple clasp with the band because the band itself is so beautiful and it is really nice leather, I can see it lasting a very long time. But with it not being dependable I won’t be using it amymore.

Ok, this is a followup of my original review. I initially had an issue with bottom port covers not staying closed. I took off the case and put it back on twice and have finally gotten it to where the bottom ports stay closed. The key is to make sure you put the phone in bottom first, press all around the phone to front of case, then insert that into the rubber bottom first. It's been 1/2 hr now and the port covers haven't gradually worked their way open. On a side note, this case will not work with the moshi iglaze tempered glass screen protector on the phone.

its pretty hard to use the fingerprint reader with this case on, especially if you have smaller hands. if you wrap the case around the back to hold it you end up covering the reader, so i end up having to hold the other half of the case with my other hand to use the fingerprint reader. annoying as hell, but not impossible. also, the magnetic clasp is not the same as in the photos. instead of one long strip on the front it is two short strips on both sides that cover each other on the side, which feels a little less secure than the longer strip would have felt. i also had to look at the pictures again to figure out how i was supposed to fold the case in order to stand it up horizontally for videos, haha. if you have any particularly thick cards in the pockets it will end up a lot harder to balance the phone on top of them like that

This case looks okay, but compared to my iOttie (bought for $9.99) it feels so cheap. With my iOttie, I dropped it on cement at least 20 times with no damage to my phone. This case feels like cheap plastic and I'm very worried that if I drop it, it will not protect my phone. This is just what it feels like, though, so I could be wrong. I'm not going to take the chance though, because it also does not have a good grip on it. The sides are smooth plastic and the back is textured, but not a rubbery material. It feels like it will slide right out of my hands. Colors are fun and as pictured. Simple, but bright. I received this product at a discounted price for my unbiased, honest review. I would not spend more than $5 on this item. If I decide to keep it on my phone longer, and I like it more than I do now, I will update this review.

These fit pretty well. They seal water out nicely, but leave just a slight bit along one edge as an air bubble. I have found no other brand that fit or protects even close to these. That said I do a lot around the house and in the shop and garage , and the first one of these I cracked after I hit it on the sharp exposed point of a screw. My bad. Second one lasted about 6 months, but had three chips and I ordered another before this one failed and exposed the watch. So went to install third, and lo and behold, there was not one in the box. Box was sealed, everything else was in there, just not the actual protector. Amazon will send me a replacement while I ship back the missing part box, but not good. One other point, I tried to have the second one replaced under the lifetime warranty, but conveniently zagg is out of stock on these...and has been for over a month now. I can’t wait anymore.

Edited to add- Customer service is beyond excellent and very apologetic for the quality. They even offered a discount for an improved product. They reached out to me in order to correct the mishap and for that I’m editing my stars from 1 to 3- simply for the customer service. The case for the phone itself is just a tiny bit too small which means it doesn’t wrap all the way around the edges. Super annoying for the detail-oriented types. You can see your phone peeping out around half of the edges. It’s also not wireless charging compatible. I don’t know if they put the magnet in the wrong position in the case or what but it definitely won’t connect. Super disappointed in this product.

Definitely something you would expect for 3$. It came in with a few scratches on the inside of the case, so its definitely not scratches made during delivery, seeing as how theres a foam inside the case. The metal part came with a scratch on it as well. Wallet part cant hold much or else you wont be able to close it. outer blue slot doesn't allow my cards to fit all the way in. The pockets are made out of plastic so I wont be expecting this wallet to last me very long. Overall its a cute wallet, but the quality is just very poor

Case fits nice but don't expect the phone to stay in the case if you drop it on a hard surface. Cover does lift up at times but I like the extra protection it provides for the screen. It does extend past the camera bump but since the bump is so large, case really needs a flap to protect the large bump surface! Whats bad though is the magnet on the inside back prevents the s-pen from working where it sits so you have a large circle of screen that the pen cannot write in nor screen hover!. The magnet really is not even necessary! I almost sent my phone for warranty service when I noticed the loss of pen use near the magnet! All said here, I may keep the case cause its much cheaper than the samsung version. I may just cut out the magnet.

Measured my wrist for this, got the medium, and it ended up being way too big. I have to put it half way up my forearm before it stays in place. And that was AFTER going through thr incredibly frustrating 8 minute procedure of installing the dang thing. This is my fourth fitbit band and it has so far been the WORST to install. Ended up needing my husband's help. The pins are not attached to the band and will very easily slip when trying to insert them onto the device. We got lucky we only lost one in the process as they only gave us a total of three to work with. Overall, I feel like this product could be REALLY good if the sizing was a bit better and the installation wasn't as frustrating. I'm not planning on putting the band back on my versa again because I refuse to go through that experience again. It is pretty soft and the pink color is pretty dang good and accurate.

Very responsive and accurate, good pressure and tilt sensitivity. My only issue is how long it is. It's so long that it makes the weight weird. It's awkward to hold especially for long periods of time and doesn't fit well in a pencil case or anything for pencils and pens really because it is quite a bit longer. I love the magnetic cap though and the fact that the back also works on touch screens so if you just need to tap something real quick you don't need to open it up. I've never used a stylus with the little disk so that has been odd but it doesn't obscure the screen or anything, just feels very different. It's a little heavy because it's metal but I like that because I know it's sturdy even though it's thin and I don't have to worry about having it in my bag or anything like that. The magnetic cap is really the best part to me. It's so sturdy on there I know I'm not going to ever lose that. I use it a lot so I've mostly gotten use to the length and weight but it does cause some extra hand fatigue if you're planning to draw with it.

Update: got the case on my phone and will up to 4 stars. Fitment is good, works really well with a tempered screen protector. The design also is good at keeping tempered screen protectors in place. Side coverage is even better on this model than previous models. For this phone the side bumpers are flush to the face of the screen to add protection from drops. The two caveats is the lack of integrated screen protector (which isn't so bad to match with a tempered screen that won't get dust/debris under it) the other is the fact that the back design will limit protectors for the camera (see pics) I have had this case for other phones and it works really good. The kickstand pops out of the tracks everyone in awhile, but it is great at drop protection. This one doesn't come with an integrated screen, which I wrongly assumed because previous cases had them.

I bought this to use on my motorcycle and the adjustable band (strap) easily rotates and the speaker turns upside down. I have another mount that my cell phone sits in and it has clamps which work perfect (I swapped strap for clamp to utilize my speaker). The device comes with two battery doors (I'm guessing old speaker and newer speaker) that replace the original battery door and attach to the mount. That part is rock solid. Be aware (as I wasn't) that the cover shown is NOT included....That's my fault. As far as customer service and Killer Concepts, major KUDOS as they are responsive and accommodating (past experience with my speaker).

I didn't realize that this was a glass fusion screen protector. It's flexible and easy to apply, but I was wanting a glass screen protector. It doesn't hide fingerprints well at all. I find myself constantly wiping off my screen. The fingerprint sensor has worked 90% of the time without me having to re-register my prints. My touch sensitivity is on. I just have to push a little harder on the sensor. As far as protection goes, it's already cracked just a little from it slipping out of my hands about 3" from the countertop. The sides are coming I p slightly and I have to constantly press down on them. When applying it, there were a ton of bubbles and I spent longer than expected getting them all out. I wouldn't purchase this again, but its not a terrible screen protector.

I didn't give the product the 5 stars it likely deserves as the first one they sent to me the magnetic latch for the front cover of the phone wouldn't "stick." Point of fact, I took small pieces of metal and nothing stuck to the mag that's in the back half of the unit. I returned and received another and it's perfect. Stylish, protective for the entire phone, ease of access to all controls and the Note's Pen. The replacement/return process went very smoothly - good service, however it should have never left the factory floor given it was missing one of the key and needed features...the ability to keep the front cover closed.

I have been using mine since March 2017, and it has worked pretty well. I did have to re-tighten the magnet portion a couple times as It became loose and it would just spin in circles when I attach my phone. I do have a Samsung Note 3 on it, so its pretty heavy. Last week during the first week of October 2017, the arm from the mount to the magnet portion broke. It just snapped off while I was driving. I only drive my car on paved normal roads here in Southern California. I garage my car daily and use sun shades when I park outside. So I did not subject this to extreme temperatures. I do wish it lasted longer.

Haven't had the case for too long, so I can't testify for its ruggedness, but when putting it together, it was so tight, it depressed the power button and wouldn't stop cycling on and off. I had to take it apart twice (which is nearly impossible without damaging it) and try to readjust. Now it is pressing the volume down button so that doesn't work, but it's better than power. It's also so tight that the case seems to want to bust at its seems at the top and bottom and because of this, a little water leaked through in my water test. Nothing substantial. I hope after time it settles in a bit and the buttons become a non-issue.

This phone works okay but there are some quirks with it. I went from a Huawei mate SE to this phone which is about same pricing. This phone has a quirk with making phone calls when a call is started the screen goes black and will not come back on sometimes so you're unable to hang up the calls or to switch to speakerphone. It does have four cameras in the back but the quality of them is not what you would expect. Very slow boot time for having an eight core processor this phone is significantly slower than what my mate was. Screen resolution is also lower. By calling areas also reduced as well as the internet design must not be as good as my previous phone. I've had Nokia phones in the past and they've always been great phones this one is definitely not on par.

Very secure phone case for my iphone 11. Love the color, the back of the phone is clear so you can see what color your phone is which is what I like. There is a stand on the back of the phone which is the best feature. Perfect for watching shows and movies without having to find a place to set your phone. Highly recommend this item. Follow up after few week of using, If you are using magnetic car holder in your car then this is not the one because on the back of this magnetic is very weak, can't hold your phone tight , always fall off.

I have just received my order no more than an hour. I use to hold my phone with my pinky at the bottom. When I saw someone with this I was hopeful the idea of getting one of these would relieve the weight and discomfort from my pinky. It’s very helpful. I have already been using it to hold while I write emails and make calls. My pinky feels strange though, doesn’t know where to go but I’m a fan. Buy it!!! UPDATE: Damn time flies by. It feels like I just bought this the other day. People have written that theirs lasts 6+ months. I’m unhappy, it stuck till last week. Lasted not even three months.

Well it was cheap enough that I'm not willing to take the time to send it back, but it looks like I got one that was used and previously damaged. Doesn't give me much faith in how long this case will last. Other reviews said that the speaker fits so snug it's hard to get it in and out, that's exactly what I was hoping for, however, this one does not fit that tight, I can easily slide the speaker in the case and remove it as well as rotate the speaker within the case without any struggle. All and all it will do, but I am bummed that I payed for something that has quite a bit of wear and tear/ seemingly used.

It is a great-looking phone case and the stand works really well. I was originally given a hand me down of the case and that worked until the stand started becoming loose after a couple years of use. I finally got a replacement and it works just fine. If you are looking for a super protective case because you drop your phone very often, I'd suggest you would go with something else. The case is a little flimsy, but if you aren't outside, or are in an environment where you won't be dropping your phone on rocks all the time, you should get this case

I like this case better than my former L***P**** case. The screen seems much clearer, and I like seeing the back of the phone. The charger and headphone ports are easier to open and close with flexible rubber-like tabs. I also like that it came with a wrist strap. The only drawback is that the knob that switches the ringer on and off doesn’t work most of the time. If you use that button often, this would be super annoying. I’ve only had it for a week, so I can’t comment on its durability, but it seems sturdy enough at the outset.

Why does this exist? Anker has a Nano line of USB C chargers, some of which have identical or better stats than this one, at half the size! So, like I said, this charger is about twice the size of the Nano. The Nano is 20w, while this one is only 18w. This charger outputs 5V 3A; 9V 2A, while the Nano is only slightly different at 5V 3A; 9V 2.22A, for what that's worth. The only other differences of note are that this charger specifies as a PD charger, whereas the Nano uses Anker's own technology/terminology, IQ3. They both, so far, seem to charge the same stuff in the same way (including a Nintendo Switch). The only other difference is the price, where the Nano is actually cheaper! So, again, like I said, I don't get it. Why does this exist?

I received this product on time and without any scratches/tears. First the pros: I love the colors and the style - very chic and looks amazing. I have received nothing but compliments...though I have to say most of them from my daughter's teenage friends! The magnetic clasp appears to be well made and keeps the cover in place even with a couple of cards. It works great as a wristlet and (conceptually) is a great wallet-n-phone combo. Its a fantastic price on amazon Cons: The slots for the credit card/ID are not wide enough to hold a standard card. I am so so bummed by this! Its such a cool design but this is such a major flaw! How in the world could the manufacturer have not accounted for a standard size credit card/drivers license? Also, while the design is cool, it is very impractical to have a conversation with the phone inside the cover! I wish they had made a little hook or something to store a headset - bluetooth or wired. Lastly, just a minor flaw in mine...when it arrived one of the threads was hanging out loose. I cut it with a scissor and fixed that issue. Overall, would I recommend this product - for the price and despite some major flaws, YES!

Pros: Price Ease of installation Fast shipping Comes with 3 shields Cuts down on the glare Does provide screen protection, I dropped the phone at the gym and it banged against one of the machines. There was damage to the screen protector, but the screen itself was fine. Cons: I know I'm comparing this to my Tech Armor experience for my LG G2 but... It doesn't look as good as the tech armor. It makes the screen look a little dingy. It does feel better than the regular protector from illumishield but not as good as the tech armor. Unfortunately, tech armor does not make a screen protector for the OPO.

I would happily give this product 5 starts if it would stick better. It is excellent in that when it comes in to contact with a flat surface, it doesn't budge. I bought the stickers to attach to back of a charging case for the Iphone 6 plus - so my grip would improve. And in the defense of the manufacturers - instructions stated not for curved surfaces. The stickers started lifting within a couple of days on the curved surfaces - but I had to try. I don't think the product would hold up to being put in a pocket - the edges would come undone. My grip is definitely improved - but needs more stick! Felt was a little pricey for the size and amount of stickers included. Also - give me more color options!

We bought this for my 8 year olds iPhone (don’t judge me, it was a hand me down). She’s had it about 8 months and the case is in horrible condition. The plastic screen protector is covered in scratches and the screen on the phone is hard to see. The actual phone is fine though so thats good. Now the plastic screen cover is peeling off the phone! Meaning it is no longer waterproof. My cases take a beating and last (I have a life proof case on my phone). I have to order my daughter a new case now. I won’t be buying this one again though. I want my phone cases to not only protect my phone but to last. I’m not asking too much. While I know my kiddo is hard on her phone (that’s why we have the case on it amiright?!), I still expect the protective case to hold up better. The poor thing didn’t even make it a year! Now it looks like a bodyguard who needs to retire and let healthier bodyguards step in. I would say it’s "old" and needs to retire but the cause isn’t even a year old! If you need a cheap case and aren’t hard on your phone this is a cheap option. Seriously though, if you’re not hard on your phone you must be a wizard and I’m impressed. This case will work for you. Regular people like me (who are sadly not wizards) need a case that will protect our phones from our clumsy human selves.

** Since pencil could not be charged when cover is on I cut a small piece of the cover off to see if it would charge and it does now. So now cover does not need to be taken off to charge. I do like the pencil however it will not charge while the cover is on. I debated whether to return or keep. I kept it because even though the cover needs to be be taken off to charged I really liked how the cover made it easier to grip pencil. The first time taking cover off was a little tricky but the more you do it the easier it is

Gorgeous phone case, albeit the color is slightly darker in person than in the photo. Definitely not baby blue. Case is made of 3 layers: inner hard plastic, middle glitter sheet, and outer soft bendable plastic with a slight silicone grippy texture. Sturdy enough to prevent scratches and dents. Not sure if it provides any shock protection should you drop your phone though. The one CON and biggest concern, however, is the case does not fully fit the iPhone 12 Pro max. While no buttons/ports are blocked, the vertical edges of the phone are not fully covered and seem to be on the verge of slipping out. Because of the unprotected edges, I’m not sure if my phone screen is touching the table when I put it faced down. This causes two concerns: 1) will my phone drop out randomly at some point, and 2) will my phone screen shatter when I drop it and it happens to land faced down? Summary: Although beautiful and sturdy, there is a huge safety risk with this phone case. I would advise against buying this if you are a frequent phone dropper.

This case does what it is intended to do. However if you have a cell phone mount in your car that holds your phone in place while you drive, I Highly DO NOT RECOMMENDED YOU BUY THIS CASE. I cannot count the number of times my phone has fallen off the magnet because the little metal kickstand in the back is to weak. It's definitely annoying and I will be returning it back for sure. If you don't have a car mount and this is not a concern to you then this case will work perfectly fine for what you need it for and that's clearly to protect the camera lenses.

Pros: Quick Arrival, body of phone in great condition, screen initially looked good, great battery life. Cons: Permanent Screen Protector (I believe liquid glass), no fingerprint recognition, occasional touchscreen sensitivity or delay, wireless charging issues The long of it: This was probably my fault for not reading carefully enough or not really understanding what liquid glass is, since I've never used it. I cannot get the phone to read my fingerprint or wireless charge which I think is due to the "permanent screen protector". At least my online forum reading has lead me to this conclusion. I've never had these issues before and I've never had a phone with this kind of screen protector. Additionally, when putting my phone case on, I pushed hard on the top corner and the screen protector cracked. Not the screen. Just the hard plastic-ish screen protector. The screen is actually un-cracked but now the screen protector is peeling back further and further a tiny little bit at a time. I mean tiny and I have to pick away little pieces and it appears as though there is now a long crack on the upper left corner but, again, the actual screen is fine underneath but everything I can find is telling me there is no 'safe' way to remove this kind of screen protector so I'll just deal with it. However, knowing what I know now, I would not recommend using this kind of screen protector. The screen looks cracked and the phone repair place said they would charge me for a full screen replacement since they cannot remove the protector so it doesn't feel like it protected anything because it 'cracked' so easily while putting on a phone protection case. No service problems with the actual company.

The front screen protector seems to be doing its job nicely since having it for a couple weeks. The back camera cover though is shattered. I just noticed it today and I could not recall ever dropping my phone, so I’m not sure how it’s shattered. It’s not even cracked, there’s a whole piece missing out of it. The only thing I can think of is that I might have hit it against a counter at work since I’m a barista and keep my phone in my apron pocket. I wouldn’t have slammed into a counter super intensely as I’m sure I’d remember the pain, but I’m a little disappointed in just receiving and barely using this product to already having to replace it.

The glass protector came on time and got 2 as promised. The packet that they came in included a whole bunch of things (see picture). Followed the instruction and got the screen protector on without any bubbles on the first try! I didn't really use the bubble pusher thing they gave - it's kind of flimsy and using a credit card/library card is better. The protector doesn't scratch and all the iphone touch functions work as they are supposed to so it's pretty good. But I am still not giving it a 5 star because the protector doesn't actually cover the whole black screen. If I try to line the protector to the left, there is a very noticeable part on the right exposed - vice versa. I just centered the protector so I get a very small amount of uncovered screen portion on both sides (probably less than 1mm on each side, but it's still noticeable). It's not ideal and the makers should probably adjust the production settings or remeasure their design... but I'll live with it. I need a screen protector since i'm not the most gentle iPhone user. But I can definitely see some more sensitive eyes becoming really annoyed at this gap.

I bought this phone because of the qwerty keyboard. I love that, it is easy to text quickly. The music player is great. Other than those two things, there is little that I like about this phone. There are NO cases out there, except cheapy ones that break quickly. I even went to the Sony sight and nothing. There is absolutely NO memory on this phone, I installed 2 apps and that is all that can be store on the phone. There are numerous preloaded apps that I rarely use but can not get off. This is an international phone and I did not realize that. The Navegador does not work and the phone is super slow. Sometimes the text box will not work and I have to wait a few minutes to text. It is very slow in transition and when switching between an app and text, forces close or you have to wait. I would not buy this phone again.

I needed a replacement stylus for my Motorola Moto G Stylus 5G (2021) phone. These work just fine with my phone. However I have a couple of minor issues. 1.) Sometimes the stylus gets stuck in my phone & can be difficult to pull out (and I'm afraid I might break it accidentally when trying to pull the stuck stylus out of phone). And 2.) The color of stylus button has turned from green to a tarnished gray-ish green color, which is only a cosmetic issue. Both of these issues have me questioning if these are actually in fact oem styluses, I suspect that they're not, but for the price, quantity (came in a 2-pack) & the fact that they work ok as replacement stylus for my phone; I honestly can't complain...well other than the getting stuck in phone occasionally that is. I do hope they'll fix this sticking issue in the future. I have recommended these to other friends & family with the same phone.

I have been using the PhoneDevil (matte finish) on my iPhone screen for almost a month now. Overall, I have been satisfied, but not fully impressed. The good: The Feel - I really like the texture of the protector. My finger glides across it with very little friction. The anti-glare works pretty well. The bad: My screen protector got a small scratch in the first week. This surprised me, as I don't remember scraping my phone on anything that would have done this, but it happened. The scratch isn't that noticable, but if you look for it you can see it. That is the only scratch that it has after a month, so it seems fairly durable. But yes, it apparently will scratch under the right conditions. The matte effect has a negative side effect of slightly blurring the screen. I have always been a big fan of matte finishes on TVs, computer monitors, etc. for reduced glare, so I got the matte finish for my iPhone. However, when you are holding the screen about a foot away from your face the blurring effect from the matte finish is much more noticeable. Not terrible, but noticeable. The application/installation went fairly smooth, except I have a couple very small, hardly noticeable bubbles around the home button and the hole for the ear speaker. I tried to rub them out, but they wouldn't go away. I finally decided that getting rid of them was more trouble than it was worth, and decided to leave it as is. In conclusion, the matte finish is very effective at stopping glare, but does have a slight blurring effect. The protector has a good feel, but is not indestructible (is anything?) And the application went fairly smooth, but wasn't perfect. Overall, I give it 4 stars.

I've had this case for 6 months now and beyond the irritations others have addressed here it's been fine. Just last week however the little door that pops open for the charger to go in, has stopped closing. Unlike another who posted that he opens his only once a day to charge at night, I plug my phone into my car via the charger sometimes a couple times a day as well as charging at night. I've ordered another brand case that is not waterproof. The strange on/off switch, the poor sound for people on the other end of the line, and the need to use proprietary headphone and charger jacks, were all tolerable knowing that the phone was so well protected. Now that I know it's not, I'm changing to a different case.

I wanted the thinnest possible case for my iphone and gave this a try. It's definitely on the thinner side, but not as thin as I'd hoped. But it still does the job of protecting my phone and giving it some friction, because iphones are very slippery without any cases. The magsafe magnet is nice and strong and never had an issue with my magsafe wallet falling off yet. However, the one big drawback is that I started to see the case yellowing and it only has been 2 months since I've used it. It's not TOO much of a big deal as I have my magsafe wallet on it and covers most of the back, but I have yet to see a clear case that doesn't yellow over time no matter what the state in this price range. If you want a budget clear case that protects your phone, this may be it for you. If you are looking for an even thinner case or better protection, I'd look for something else.

This "Dream Catcher" cover is really beautiful; however, I did not realize it was going to weigh twice what the cover I had on the phone weighed. Also, you can see pictures of the bottom end of the phone where you plug in the power cord and where the speakers are, and you can see a picture of the top end where you can plug in ear phones; however there is not a clear picture of the volume button, nor the on/off switch. My old cover had all these things cut out so everything was open. This cover has the volume and on/off switches covered. It took me two hours to try and cut out the holes for the volume and on/off switch on my phone (you might want them covered, I don't.) I wasn't sure the switches would work after I cut these out but it is working and I am happy enough to keep it. I hope this helps others. May God Bless

Just put it on my Samsung Relay yesterday. After 24 hours there are LARGE bubbles/imperfections under the shield. The instructions say to use liquid dish soap. The video on YouTube that an insert in the packaging insists that you watch prior to installation (STOP in big red letters) shows the installation using a dishwasher rinse aid. Not the same thing at all. For the price you would think that they would have included a bottle of the spray that has been included with EVERY OTHER protective shield that I have ever bought. But no, they have you make your own. Which probably led to the large bubbles/imperfections. Pros: It fits the Samsung Relay and it has a lifetime warranty (which I will be taking advantage of, bet on it). Cons: Confusing instructions, lack of pre-made solution.

The screen works great, but the tools that were included are a joke. The suction cup is almost comically useless and the triangle pick is way too thick but somehow also too malleable to be useful. It's almost impossible to remove the old screen with the tools provided. The only way I was able to swing it was to push out hard from the small window where the ribbon is run through with both my fingers and cracked the screen even more. I would recommend a set of professional tools instead. The videos online are super helpful and I would recommend watching them a few times before buying. It took me about an hour and half with these tools but it'd probably been 30 minutes with a better tool to remove the case and the screen

Quality of material is great. I really like the comfort and feel of this product compared to the default foam padding that came with HTC Vive. The material of the product also looks great on the HTC Vive. The function of the product is also excellent, It does help bring your eye distance closer reducing the goggle effect of VR and opening up more of your peripheral vision to the headset. However, the craftsmanship of this product is not long lasting. I had this product for 10 months and the glued seams along the edges that keep the foam material inside began separating and falling apart. I like the quality of the material of this product but, feel they should have sewn the edges of the material instead of using a material glue that apparently doesn't last more than 1 year of use. If the manufacturer corrects the way the material is held together will be a great product. If not, I would try other options out there for VR Covers or if this is your only option contact your local seamstress to fix the product.

After installing the screen protector (took less than 30 seconds), I noticed that it does not completely cover the screen of my S23+. This ends up working for me as it does not interfere with the case that I have. I have experienced an issue with the soft film screen protectors that cover the whole screen and as a result, when using a case, it will eventually cause the protector to start peeling up. As far as the impact to the fingerprint sensitivity, I do have the setting turned on to increase fingerprint sensitivity but I still notice the sensor being slightly impacted by the protector.

I really like the way the screen protector applied I was able to get it right the first time with no air bubbles. My problem was with the edges on both sides. It is meant to curve over the edge of the curved screen, but these edges kept lifting up. They would appear to be adhering fine but a few minutes later they would be lifted. After pushing them down with the card and sealing them so many times I pretty much gave up, because by then dust particles had gotten under the edges and they weren't going to stick smoothly anyway

Pros: USB C connector, holds a large phone (Note 8), charges quickly (or as reported by Android), works well even with a case (I have an Otterbox with both rubber and plastic layers), auto-close arms, leather (or leather-like) pad, USB cable included, two different mounting options, support leg for the clamp option, indicator lights, open/close buttons and indicator lights on both sides. Cons: No car adapter included, suction cup is pre-coated for stickiness - which will leave residue that can be difficult to remove. The lack of a power adapter will leave your charging speed highly dependent on your adapter. You need to supply your own QC3. 0 charger for optimal charging. (I took pictures, but it looks like Amazon has enough - they took off the option to add more.)

*** Update 2/1/2014 *** I contacted Otterbox directly about my problems with the product. After a couple of photos were sent to them they promptly mailed me a replacement. My hope is that the replacement is stronger in the areas I've mentioned below. Thanks OtterBox for prompt service. *********************** I've had a few previous OtterBox cases before and have been pretty happy with them. However, this case could use some improvements with the hard plastic external case. I've had this case/phone since July 2013 and I have never dropped my phone to date and generally keep great care of my phone however I have a few spots where the hard plastic has broken which to me gives this item a 2 star review. The areas below have broken from daily, normal use. Never dropped and the case has only been assembled and never taken off. 1) The very thin plastic strip that is near the audio jack. 2) The very thin plastic at the charging port 3) and finally today, a random piece near the rear speaker (thus prompting of my negative review today) Break area 1 and 2 from above case need either thicker wall sections or the case should be redesigned or a different plastic compound chosen as it seems the plastic is too brittle. The rubber, inside case, has no issues and fits snugly. My history with these cases I had come to expect another winner in the durable case category but the hard plastic shell seems frail and damaged with even daily use.

I always purchased griffin survivor case for my phones. However, this case which is supposed to be the toughest on survivor line sucks. They did away with the screen protectors and just raised edges. Not a fan of. I rather have the case with the built in screen protector. Case was ridiculously tough to snap on. One before you would slide the cover down which was so much better. I’m not a fan of this case. Older survivor cases where far better. I will not be sticking with this case. Griffin just lost a long-standing customer with these new cases!
