Easy to put on and a little high if you have small hands but overall still comfortable.

The case looks great and provides ample lip protection for the face of the phone. I like the rubber incasing used in conjunction with the hard bumper cover, for extra shock protection. I have received many compliments on this case! My only complaint is the rubber incasing stains really easily and the stains do not come out. I have tried using soap and water, alcohol, Lysol wipes and stain removers to clean this case; however, nothing has worked. Therefore, I would think twice before slipping this case in your jeans pocket and to make sure your hands are clean when carrying.

I had one and really loved it. It has so many cool features and it sound great for streaming media and playing music stored on the device. People even said they heard me very clearly - the noise canceling is incredible (as long as it's a consistent sound like a washing machine or traffic.) BUT DANG IT, something has gone wrong - the last two that I've had have taken a sharp downturn in performance after about 10 months. I don't know if they are selling refurbished units as some people have suggested, or if this is planned obsolescence.. But I'm not happy about a 10 month life cycle.

I purchased this hoping the screen protector had been redesigned since most other reviewers complained. At first I felt the gap and simply pushed harder, but after a day or two I decided to remove the built in protector and purchase a separate one to then place the case over that. The protector I purchased was a tech guard ballistic glass edge to edge, which is a really nice screen protector. However, with it going edge to edge the Otterbox case prevents flush contact at corners and middle connectors so when the screen is off you see a small bubble. When the screen is on you do not notice it at all. My recommendation if you do choose this Otterbox is to purchase a good screen protector that only covers screen, remove the old protector, not by cutting but just pushing it out, then remove glue with a glue remover, and in the end you will have paid slightly more money but overall you will have great protection for you phone. The Defender series for my Iphone 5S is waterproof while this one is no where near being that. It protects my Iphone 6 plus about the same as the Otterbox on my Ipad Air. Also, the belt clip is really tight and I was afraid I'd break it by turning it, but it turned fine. To use it as a stand I prefer both landscape and portrait orientations and the clip works well.

I bought this cable a year ago, and really liked the sturdiness of it and the 6 ft length. I started noticing after about 8 months of use, that it would occasionally not be recognized on my iphone 6 and would not charge it. I would remove the cable and plug it in a couple times and the it would start to charge. About 2 weeks ago, it has stopped charging at all, my phone does not recognize it , neither does my wife's phone or our ipads. It is disappointing that the life span of the cable is so short. The cable looks to be in great condition from the outside - no fraying or noticeable breaks, but I guess the wires inside have broken. I decided to buy a different cable to replace this - hopefully one that has a longer life span.

Update: I couldn't live without the application button so I contacted the seller and they are sending out a replacement part. They were really quick to respond. Now with the new replacement part the applications key works but callers cannot hear me unless I use the speaker phone. After looking the phone over 1000 times I decided to just reinstall the chip with the broken applications key since I would rather be heard on my phone without my conversation being broadcasted. The part fit great on my Verizon Note 4 and came in faster then expected. The applications button did not work on the new charging port though, which is a downer, but I really needed to replace the microphone in order to talk so I did not send it back. Other than that this part was as expected.

The battery is garbage. I've used this phone for about a year now (a review shouldn't be done in a day or week of receiving, imo). They have made it similar to the "fruit product" including the flaws. As a business its much more profitable to rip us off and not make batteries easily replaceable, but I must say that I am tempted to switch to another brand after over 10 years of loyalty to samsung. I have unplugged this from the charger (which is a constant struggle to make a good connection) for 30 minutes now and already my percentage has dropped to 92%. For a $1000 phone I find this unacceptable.

I love everything about this phone case /wallet EXCEPT the top snap doesn't snap. I don't know if it's a factory defect or what but the little button that goes in the snap is barely sticking out to catch which is very disappointing so that's why it got 4 stars. I wanted to order another in the wine color but will pass on that because of the defect. Magnet seems to hold the phone fine but it's still new. I have read some of the other reviews that say the magnetic gave out...we shall see but for now it works for me.

UPDATE!!! Had to lower stars as life expectancy isnt that great...After about 2-3 mos the edges or as one did under the “notch” starts lifting!!! Great protection while they lasted though!!! Bubble free, easy and simple No rainbow type effects, smooth, maybe its just me but the fingerprints arent as bad either. Heck of a deal!! Major props to the company. Just wish they lasted longer First. This is a heck of a deal. Highly recommend for the value and the packaging as well. This was clearly thought out and just glad i picked this one. Crazy fast on delivery too. Will install tonight and well for 3 of them. I doubt i can go wrong. And the glass is 9H and u can feel it Thanks

I would have loved this phone case BUT... there is one major flaw. The phone screen sticks up over the case with no bumbers or protection. I have only had this case a short time and I have had to replace the tempered glass screen protector 5 times!!! It's ridiculous! Every time the phone drops the screen cracks. They need to make the case deeper for protection. In my previous case the edges were raised and I never cracked the screen! When you look at the case from the side you can see your screen sticking up higher than the case. I've kept it to long now to return it so I suppose I now need to buy another case. I'm so disappointed as the wallet and open front are so wonderful. But my phone is not safe using it

This charger does work, but the mounting devices are very flimsy and jiggle around if your car vibrates at all. It doesn't hold phones very well if they are in a case. They won't fall out and they will charge, but they do stick out awkwardly. The vent mount doesn't fit with my vents, which is a shame. The suction cup works fine, but fails in hot or cold weather just like every other suction cup in the world. The cable is also quite short, which is fine if you mount on the vents in the center console, but if you want or need to locate your phone elsewhere, you will have to buy a separate usb cable.

I bought the white color so that it would match the face of my iPhone (yeah I'm crazy like that). Set up was a breeze. There are easy, step by step instructions that come over in your ear for quick pairing. The calls are clear most of the time. That issue could easily be the call area that I'm in at the time. What I really love are the different sized ear buds with the loop on the end. It molds to the cartilage of your ear for firmer positioning. I prefer this over the hard plastic piece that goes over your year. I also love the ability to pair to multiple devices/phones at the same time (you just can't switch calls on devices) The one thing I don't like is that it pairs with EVERYTHING; my games, phone calls, videos I watch on Facebook, etc. I wish there was a setting to only pair phone calls.

Pros: * Works with all sorts of devices (most likely including future ones). I feel MUCH better about having this than an Apple lightning dock. * You can pick the phone up off the stand with one hand, without touching the stand (can't say that about some docks). * The angle is perfect * The iPhone 6S Plus, for example, can have lightning and headphone cables connected and still sit (albeit slightly off-center) on the stand in portrait orientation. * The mic and speaker are not blocked or muffled when the phone is placed in portrait orientation against the back, because the size of the rubber pads in the two arms are just big enough to hold the phone gently and not big enough to interfere with audio. Cons: * Slightly rough texture (not sure if it's the metal or the paint) doesn't quite match the look and feel of Apple's products (Apple's MacBooks and peripherals are much smoother; see photo). It doesn't look bad, but I think it doesn't quite look as good as it could (or should for the price I paid for it in Japan, about $45). If there was another product like this -- universal, with cable management, and that holds the phone at a good angle -- but with a bit better appearance, I'd return this for that. * The inner upper edge of the two arms that hold the bottom of the phone are sharp, and if you're not careful, you'll scratch your screen!

Neither of the two Phillips screwdriver bits provided were adequately small for the iphone screws. I almost stripped the heads and/or the screwdriver bit before I realized I wasn't turning the screw. This interruption was both frustrating and disappointing. I was able to continue the battery replacement only after obtaining the proper size Phillips screwdriver. Another rude awakening: the replacement process all of the videos show, looks deceptively easy. It isn't! Unless you're a brain surgeon, or equivalent in eyesight and steadiness and dexterity and have a lot of patience, don't try any smart phone repair. One minor muscle spasm and the microscopic size screw you're trying to position is gone forever! As I just finished replacing the battery, it's too short of a time to comment on the quality of the battery.

Extremely minimalist case. If you aren't looking for much protection but an amazing look and feel then this case is perfect. I use it strictly indoors. I have both the smoke and the blue both look amazing. Now the case does add extra grip which is nice even more than a skin. The down side is that it barely covers the buttons. This case would be perfect if it had a little bit more meat not to much just a little. Also because of the bottom cut outs the bottom middle lip easily comes down revealing the unprotected glass. But the corns stay on so the case doesn't completely come off. No other case manufacturers I've seen come close to the look and feel of these. They are absolutely stunning and feel great in the hand.

1 Star off for the price as there are many SIMILAR cases a lot cheaper on eBay and Amazon. That being said the fit and feel are excellent. The quality shows. Using this on a MINI 13 (wife's) and the credit card holder is VERY tight. Adding three cards requires a mallet to get them in. Maybe on the larger phones where there is more room to stretch it would be better. TIGHT is better than LOOSE though. Nice thin design. She had a similar case for her 12 MINI ($10!) from here which they don't make for the 13 Mini and while it held cards better (had an elastic stretch band) it was a thicker (it was that fake leather stuff). If this case was $15-$17 it would be a winner. At $25 it's a nice case. Of course the price dropped a little bit by coupon on the very day my "pre-order" for this case showed up in the mail direct from seller, now Amazon has it for 2 day delivery. If you're willing to spend $25 (at the time of this posting) go for it, you'll like it.

The case looks Ok, it fits the phone well but it's not very slip resistant. That the main reason I bought it. I have a case on my old 3gs that will stick to most surfaces. It doesn't slide out of my shirt pocket or off the arm of the leather couch. I can put the phone o my chest to use the speaker phone and stays put. This new case does none of those things. The material is not high friction and the gold stripes are flush with the rubber surface. Another thing I noticed is the opening for the power cord and earphone jack are pretty small. The power cord won't always connect without fiddling with the case and I have an MP3 adapter for my truck that won't fit at all. I'm going to have to enlage the hole. I would not buy it again. I'll be looking for a case with a very high​ friction case.

This is very daunting right out of the box, as the "instructions" really just tell you how to lock the light stand in position. But, it's less confusing than it first appears! The phone holder had me confused but it's just a spring mechanism. The remote had me REALLY confused but it's just a Bluetooth pairing that my phone found really easily (much easier than literally anything I've ever tried to pair before). The stand is pretty sturdy & the telescoping arm is quite stable in just about any position. The lights have 3 different shades of white, varying from cool to warm, and 3 levels of brightness, controlled by buttons attached to the cord. There's a compartment on the bottom that looks like it's for batteries, but it's just for storing the cord & remote. I really hate the cord! It's not particularly long, and does not come with anything to plug into - it's just a USB connection & you have to supply your own power hub. Which would have been fine a few years ago, but now that every gadget is switching to USB-C, I actually could not find an old USB hub! I tried plugging it into the USB port in my desktop computer, but computer did NOT like that & shut it off immediately every time I tried to turn it on. Finally my husband was able to dig out an old USB wall hub to plug it into, but that greatly restricts where you can take photos because the cord isn't very long. Needs to either switch inputs to USB-C so it will work with current chargers & hubs, or include it's own wall hub.

The screen protector seemed really great at fist, the camera lenses protector works good but need improvement and most importantly the privacy screen works! The issues I have with this set up is the camera lenses protector does not sit flush on the phone body so there is a gap all around the lenses and pocket lint and dust gets stuck under it and it sticks to the adhesive. Looks gross after a week. The privacy screen also has a huge issue that you can barely type a text out since it doesn’t have a good sensitivity connection to your phone glass screen it miss spelled almost every word I typed. It got to the point I ripped it off and threw it away after it miss spelled an important text I wrote. Keep looking maybe a better quality one will be out there

Difficult to apply, requiring rather excessive force on the edges; though the result is a tight fight, such pressure could have resulted in scratches or possibly a bent phone. Clear case unfortunately is a fingerprint magnet; also, the entire right side of the case has unnecessary and indiscreet text such as "Air Cushon Technology" and "PWR", in addition to the logo through which the company promotes itself. Edges do provide a good bumper for protection, but are also rather thick and almost magnified due to the prism effect of rounded crystal. I have a platinum gold S6, whose sleekness is subsequently somewhat offset by the cover. If you want a super slim case, there are other options out there.

I'm not about to do a drop test to test the durability. Nor do I want to jinx it now. It was very easy to put on the phone. I'm using the built in screen protector and it works very well. Something that may be an issue for you, that can't be help is when you're trying to push something to the edge of the screen (like moving a shortcut to another screen) you have to grab the object by the edge and push it over because the protection ridge surrounding the front screen prevents your finger from contacting the left most part of the digitizer that senses pressure from your finger. For me that's a non issue and probably for you too. Another minor issue is the fingerprint reader. Coming from a pixel phone, where the finger reader worked 99% of the time, with this case on, sometimes it requires a 2nd try out of 5 tries that work the first time without issues. It might just need some getting use to.

I have tried multiple brands of screen protectors and try to clean the screen as well as possible, but after 2 weeks bubbles start forming and impossible to get them out. The Apple screen protector seemed to adhere the best but cost 50$. A nuisance spammer kept calling me right after I had just bought my phone. The default apple settings are vibrate and ring the jerk kept calling while I was trying to sleep and the phone vibrated off the table onto the floor. The actual screen looked broken but luckily it was just the Apple screen protector so don't actually know how long that protector would have adhered, but 50$ is a lot for a tiny piece of glass.

This case needs some more work. This is the second slide one I have and neither work well. To be honest, I would not put a credit card in the slide out for fear that the slide out would drop off. When you go to put it on your phone, you have to carefully keep the slide portion attached to the rest of the same colored portion and put your phone in. Then you have to carefully attached the slide portion to the front of the case without any parts falling out. Otherwise, you will have to unassembled and reassemble again.

Nice design to keep the mount unobtrusive but it only mounts to a relatively horizontal surface like the top of a dashboard. It won't adhere to all surfaces (at least not well) especially leather, but does include an adhesive disc that you can permanently mount and then suction to the disc. Not sure who would permanently adhere the disc to their dash, but it's an option. The only real issue I had once I found a place to mount it is the weight of my iPhone 13 ProMax and the Apple MagSafe case. The cantilever design of this mount can't support the weight of the phone and the mounting plate on the slippery case allows the phone so slip and rotate/slide when hitting bumps. I wish the charger plugged into the back of the charger instead of the side for a cleaner look, but with the phone on it you can't see it. Overall it's nice but be sure you have a good place to mount it. The arm pivots down, but not up so it can't be suctioned onto a vertical portion of the dash.

The phone seems to work well enough from what I can tell. It is in brand new condition and seems like it'll be a good phone for the person I ordered it for. Sadly, the sim card that came with the phone was not the sim card that it should've come with. The numbers did not match up, and thus, the phone could not be completely activated. I did call Straight Talk, and they agreed to send a new sim card free of charge. When the new sim card gets here, I will be sure to edit this post with more details about the phone, it's reliability, and features. ***Update*** While the phone does work well, and there have been no complaints about any of it's features; it simply has no memory space. The phone came with a Micro SD card, but somehow there is still no space for anything, to the point that the owner of the phone had to store her contacts on her gmail. It hardly gets any signal in the same places that her old Straight Talk phone had great signal. We're not sure if different towers are being used because it says Tracfone when you turn it on; or it the antenna in it is just far weaker than other current phones. Unfortunately, because of this limited space issue, she is unable to download anything, and thus can't play the games she once loved. For a smartphone, apps are essential, so this is rather disappointing. All in all, if you want it as a phone and live in the big city or something, it may work for you. If you're not directly under towers, and you want to use this phone for apps and pictures, I wouldn't.

Love it ,love it , love it . Beautifull ,more then I expected for this price ,no slippery ,as some commented,and flower staued on ,so far. But there is a big issue ,the case does not have a hall for the sensor,atleast the one I was mailed ,so when the case is on and you are talking to someone ,the screen would not lock, so you touch the screen with your face and press all kind of buttons,so you can only use it on speaker or with earphones. But l I got a drill and made the hall myself ,it took me about 1 min. I would give 5 stars ,if not the problem with the missing hall

Fits the S3 mini quite nicely, it really doesn't add bulkiness to the phone. Its clarity level is good and plays nicely with the pebble blue model (the one I own). I like that you can put the phone facing down without worrying about it getting scratched, because the case lifts it about 1 mm. It's definitely not designed to be removed often, so keep that in mind. My only quarrel is that mine seems to be pre-owned... not really sure why, but the back of my case shows some ware and small cracks... That aside, it's a good case and I would recommend it to others.

I’ve only had for a week, using with Ghostek Convert case. Pros: -Easy to install, good adhesion. -Loop is easy to use, feels secure. -Lays flat, phone still fits in pocket. Cons: -Kickstand is not very stable. It will collapse if surface that phone is on is bumped or moved. -Kickstand is already loose, after a few days. -Issues with phone charging wirelessly. I’ve tested on multiple chargers, I have more luck getting it to work with flat chargers vs. standing. If I’d purchased as a loop/ holder, this would be great. But, I was expecting the two advertised features below to work better: • Adjustable Stand for Video Watching • Detachable Making it Wireless Charging Compatible Returning this item, may be good for some, not for me.

I was excited to get this phone, it replaced my T721. It is in a beautiful case and plenty of features like the camara, bluetooth, etc. However, the phone is not very responsive. Also I sometimes have had trouble with the front display going crazy and just showing random junk, and sometimes the screen doesn't come on when I open it. So I called Motorola about it, if I want it looked at I need to send it to them and they will return it to me in (get this) 4-6 weeks. Which pretty much makes the warrenty useless for my purposes. So if you gotta have a nice looking phone this fits the bill but think twice if you are on your phone a lot.

Not having my screen exposed to everything is a load off my mind. This was my 1st time ever installing one of these types of protectors, and I managed to do it with minimal bubbles, and the ones there were were easily worked out. It looks like there's nothing on the screen at all. It's slightly interfered with the fingerprint reader, making it take longer and giving an error sometimes, so I just set up another one with the protector on and all is well. The touch screen works flawlessly. There's no offset, and my finger slides smoothly over it. The lens protector for the camera is where the problems arise. Even though there is a cut out for the flash, the glass still seems to catch it and it ruins the pictures, rendering the lens protector unusable. This is unacceptable. If it's doing it on my S20Fe, it's doing it on all of them and this had to have been known before the product was released. Maybe I'll try giving it another go and offsetting it from The Flash as much as possible, but it seems kind of janky. Seems pretty clear how it's supposed to sit over the camera.

I thought this was a set that had holders of different dimensions that would fit both Tablets and an iPhone.Turns out it's only meant for a cell phone. They are so tiny. It seems to fit the iPhone 11, and it does not fall over. They look gimmicky, not sturdy from the looks of it, not very aesthetically pleasing.. I can see how it can be useful if someone wanted to use their cell phone to do a zoom meeting or watch videos, but the question is why do you need so many of them in different somewhat ugly colors. Perhaps, if a family has a few people with phones, it might come in handy to have a different color for every family member. In any case, me no likey...

IT HAS GLITTER ON IT. I know they were trying to make it look like the phone's back but ya it did'nt work. The nexus has the pixel sparkling thing that not just makes it pretty but makes cool as well but this cover has glitter nothing more nothing less. As a man I find it too girly. I am gonna give the cover a try and put it on for a while but what I know is that if any of my friends notice it they are definitely gonna make fun of me. if you're a girl go for it. It would be great for you but if your a typical man find yourself something that doesnt sparkle.

I bought this phone yesterday, and I am going to try to exchange it today for a sidekick. I love the large lettering on the screen, decent lighting, and I love the keyboard. But the TOUCH SCREEN IS TOO SENSITIVE! I often end up opening applications I dont want. Most frustrating is when scrolling thru the PHONE CONTACT LIST. It slides pass the contact I want, and I have to flick backwards and then it passes my selected contact again. Unlike my RAZR phone, there is no screen alert to tell me I have a voicemail message waiting. The phone will give one chime once when a voicemail message is left, but that's it. Nothing appears on the screen. If you're away from your phone, you dont even realize that you missed a phone call, unless you just happed to check your voicemail function. I DONT LIKE HAVING TO UNLOCK THE PHONE EVERYTIME I WANT TO ACCESS. IF I'M AWAY MORE THAN TWO MINUTES, IT LOCKS AND THEN I HAVE TO UNLOCK AGAIN BEFORE I CAN DO ANYTHING. I'm going to exchange it for a phone with a scroll ball, so that I can have better control when scrolling down my phone comntact list.

Really unable to evaluate the product quality its self. However, the ScandiTech response is great! I advised ScandiTech of my unsuccessful attempts to separate the front and back of my wife's iPhone 5 to replace the battery, and that in trying to do so, closely following their instructions, the screen was damaged. They immediately issued a full refund of the purchase price as well as the shipping. While they could only recommend taking the phone to an authorized repair facility to see if it could be repaired, they at least promptly refunded my money for their product. I WOULD CAUTION EVERYONE TO MAKE SURE THEY KNOW WHAT THEY ARE DOING BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO REPLACE A BATTERY IN AN iPHONE 5. As a result of my efforts to use this product, my wife now has a new phone!

I was really excited about this product. I have wanted a mirror screen for awhile but I did not think (duh) about the reflective part. You can't see in direct sunlight. I had the brightness turned all the way up on my phone. Which, by the way causes your battery to run down faster. And, I still could not see very well outdoors. It would give me a headache trying to text or read emails outdoors and my text were completely wrong b/c I could not see what I was typing. It was worth the price, to get over my urge to have one and I have 2 more...

I've used it for almost two years so I think I know what's good and not. The battery life is outstanding. Really reliable and it lasts for quite a while, i.e. when you travel and don't overuse it, you can for sure rely on it! Camera is nice and ok, nothing outstanding but solid! I like the the extra button for it and how fast you can have it open, double tap the power button and the camera is on. That's very helpful. The keyboard is horrible. After two years, I still make mistakes because it doesn't feel natural and the autocorrect is only ok. The worst part is swiping with one finger. The keyboard doesn't learn you pattern and suggests the WORST words that are low frequency, no one every uses, and have no context at all. I have no idea how you can program a keyboard this bad, seriously!!! There's a few other things that I don't understand why the phone is doing it that way but after almost two years, I'm at the point where I'm happy if it breaks so I can get a new one.

Update: The charger heats up quite a bit while charging. This causes the magnetic ring to move/slide on the phone to where it is no longer lined up to charge or the phone just falls off completely. This morning I woke up the phone falling on the floor. The magnetic ring is still on the charger… what a shame because otherwise I would have loved this. Initial review: This is perfect! I can charge my watch and phone in one place and I don’t have to keep tabs of the cords anymore. The magnetic ring was easy to put on the phone and the magnet is surprisingly strong. It did take a little to get used to placing the phone exactly in the right place for it to hold but once you get it lined up, the phone isn’t going anywhere. Hopefully this lasts longer than my previous wireless chargers. I’ll update after I’ve been using it for awhile.

MP-MALL Screen Protector for Samsung Galaxy S8, [Tempered Glass] [Full Cover] I've had several glass screen guards in the past, and this was to replace one that had cracked after 2 years of use. It is unbelievably easy to apply. The video is clear and the guide provided makes it almost impossible to put the glass in the wrong position. It took seconds and I had no dust or bubbles to remove - although the video gives good instructions on how to do this. Sensitivity is the same as it was with my previous guard so no worries there. Hope this quality continues with use. EDIT AFTER 2 WEEKS: OK, sensitivity became an issue in the middle of the screen, typing the 'top' line of the keyboard needs a good tap, but who needs to use the 'e' anyway? And then it started to crack. Phone has not been dropped, but the screen started with a half inch crack a few days ago which has now snaked its way up and down the long edge. Suspect it won't last much longer.

Less than two months after installing this, it has chipped or fractured on the edge at five points. Cracks radiate out from those points into the rest of the screen. This was a replacement for my previous screen protector, same model, which after about a year was too cracked up to use. It does protect the screen underneath, but I can see I’ll need a new one in a few months and I will be trying something else. I don’t keep my iPhone in a case - this is the only protection I put on it - but I don’t treat it harshly either. I mostly just keep it in my front pants pocket. It might work better for someone with a case or someone who keeps their phone in a purse or holster.

Edit: the seller did refund me the price of my purchase, so I'm editing to add a star and let you know that their customer service is really good. I very much appreciated their help. Original Review: I bought this because of all the reviews saying it's a fast charger, but now I'm wondering if I got the same product as those people! This thing is charging at a snail's pace. And what's worse, I tried to use it, and it's dropped from 20% to 3% WHILE PLUGGED IN. I don't know what charger other people got, but I didn't get the some one apparently.

I like it a lot, just haven't had it long enough to judge how protective it will be. I'm using it with a Tech Armor ballistic glass screen protector, so the rounded glass on the front is still slightly exposed. I wouldn't mind just a bit more bumper on the front bumper. Cut outs on the back for the logo and camera are deep and fit precisely, and so should protect both from coming into contact with anything that could scratch them. The buttons are easy to use and I had no problem fitting Bose earbuds into the headphone jack for a snug fit. It is hard to get to the ringer/silent toggle switch: I have slender fingers and can use my nail, but people with larger hands or mobility issues may want to try before buying. The kickstand is fine. Mine snaps into place when not in use, the angle is perfect, and it does not slide around/down (I have two glass tables and no issue). As many have written, it would be nice to see a metal kickstand. I'd suggest a rubber tip, metal or plastic, to keep it just that much more securely stable when in use.

UPDATE 8/16/16: CASE RANDOMLY DIED, WOULD NOT TAKE A CHARGE NOR CHARGE MY PHONE WITH CASE OFF. MOPHIE CHARGING USB CABLE WAS EVEN BROKE TO. IT IS GETTING WARRENTIED. I am in no way pair or promoted to review this. I am a average consumer. Lets start out by saying this case is phenomenal.the battery charging aspect is very good. The case is very solid, its a bit thick compared to the bare naked phone but thats a given if you have to have a battery case. The only cons of this case are that 1. It can feel a bit slippery at times, and 2 for the money i would like to see a few more options or variety such as a fancier style case and a more rugged style case.

I was able to review the Hybrid Bumper Case for iPhone 6 from Case and More. It came with a screen protector, that isn't that great of a quality, so with this price you really are just paying for the case. I like this case because it's see thru. I like the look of my husbands phone and so does he, so he likes the see thru cases to see the phone.. I marked it down a star and a half because the screen protector scratched really easily and the closures for the plug ins, didn't close all the way. The back of the case wasn't very smooth, it was kind of scratchy. This case does seem to protect the phone very well and I don't think all of these cases will still have all the same issues that mine did. I still think 3.5 stars is a great rating for a cell phone case, since there are tons out there that are really pricey and they have gotten lower ratings. Even with a 3.5 rating, I do recommend this case!

The clip to retain the phone sucks. I had my phone for over 3 months without any protection. Never dropped it. I went and got this for peace of mind. The case around the phone is excellent, and it should be to withstand the constant dropping that the clip does. In one day my phone got dropped out of the clip 4 times. My wife has a Otterbox for her Samsung, and her clip has 5 points for retaining the phone in place. This only has the 4 corners. If you're looking to have this because of the combination of a clip with protection...you are going to be disappointed. I read reviews on this before I bought, and unfortunately they all started with how good the case is, and unless you clicked more didn't get to see the clip sucked. So, I started mine with the clip sucks.

** I am tossing this and trying another brand. I can not get my screen to respond with it on. Have purchased SuperShieldz for all our Samsung phones in the past. The most recent purchase for a Samsung J7 Crown, fits as it should leaving only a small area uncovered around edge. HOWEVER, the screen is not as responsive as it could and should be. I find myself swiping multiple times and hitting keys at least twice. I will use this for now but it is a problem. Will definitely consider another brand next purchase or sooner if this keeps up.

when this charger works it works great it fast charges my galaxy. But there are many times I have to pull it out and put it back in or when it will slow charge my phone for no reason. I'm not sure why I get intermittent issues with it but I've tried this charger in 3 cars now and it does the same thing in the different vehicles. It's pretty frustrating to plug your phone in, have it say its charging and then after my 45-minute commute have my phone only gain 2% battery. I have also tried it with 3 phones and the symptoms cross phones so I know its an issue with the charger.

The item definitely adds a good layer of protection for my Moto X2, but does not provide completely coverage on the screen. However, I would estimate about 2 mm on 4 sides that are missing protection when this item is applied to the center of the screen. I can see the reason why this was the design because the Moto X2 screen is slight curved on the edges. Thus, if you have a non-flexible piece of glass, it won't hug the side. I guess the manufacturer should've tried to address this problem in their design instead of making the actual piece smaller than the screen. I am taking this off and tossing it once I get another order of screen protector.

So this is my second one, the first I bought 2 years ago for my iPhone 7 and I love it. The first one was very grippy and even sticks to my pocket keeping it from sliding out. I decided to get another for my new iPhone 8 and it's a completely different feeling case. The fit is nice but it's not grippy at al, in fact it's pretty slick feeling. I see recent reviews from people talking about how grippy they are, but the one I just got is not. Holding the old one and the new one together it's like night and day. Not sure I even want to use the new one.

I'm not sure if I got a defective unit or what. I am no electrician, nor do I have the tools to empirically test it. I got it cause by its measurements and my laptop's it should be able to charge the laptop, though potentially not at the same time as charging my phone. It can charge my laptop with several different cables that I've tried. Additionally, it can charge my phone if I used the cable that came with the phone to connect it. However, if I try to use amazon's official C-to-C (6ft) cable to charge my phone, it will only pulse charge and the phone will attempt to use battery share mode even with nothing to share with. It will charge, battery share, not charge, charge, battery share, not charge repeatedly each cycle over the course of about 1-2 seconds. I think the issue actually lies with some sort of interaction between anker's cable and this new charging block. Because the cable has worked flawlessly with my last anker charging block for a couple years now (and still does). I will be returning this block. If Anker thinks this is simply a defective unit (either the cable or the block) they are welcome to send me a new one and if it works as intended, I'll gladly pay for it.

Pen worked great. Tip Broke, needed to order more, it only comes with one backup. It came with an instruction sheet and a comment that says to contact them if you need anything. 24/7 support. Guess what? There is no phone number, no website address, no email, no nothing. Tried to find them on the internet. Zip, Nada, Zilch! I guess when this tip goes I will have to buy a new pen. It will be from another company that does have a phone number. 2nd tip broke when I accidentally dropped the pencil. I will look for a different pencil with more durable tips, or one that offers an easy way to buy more tips for less than $10 per tip.

This product worked great for the first 2 weeks and then it started being really unreliable. Some mornings I wake up and it’s fully charged, and then some mornings it hasn’t charged at all! I make sure it’s placed exactly on the charger so that the blue charging light indicator is on, but then in the morning, the phone is dead. I’ve already thrown all the packaging away, too, so I can’t return it. UPDATE: I reached out to the company and they immediately responded. I received a replacement within 1 week, and so far, this one is working great! They definitely get 5 on customer service!

If this was just a selfie tripod, I'd be fine with it. That would make this a nice product to purchase. But the failure of the add on features kind of disappointed me. 1. The remote only worked once with my iPhone 13 and that was after I charged said remote. 2. The LED light only helps when RIGHT next to you. IF you have that light at selfie distance, it wouldn't matter too much. The tripod is sturdy and easy to set up. IF it stopped at just the tripod, I'd be over the moon about it. Models like it and use it my studio for BTS. But this totally fails with the additional features.

Not sure how environmentally friendly this product really is. Nothing on the case itself or inside the packaging confirms that this case is compostable or made from plants (unlike pela Case, see second image for reference to my first compostable phone case that lasted me over 4 years and was my favorite case ever). I couldn’t find a good deal with them this time around so I decided to try this case but unfortunately did not look at the reviews which showed the horrible non environmentally friendly packaging- plastic and styrofoam abound. What on earth is the point of avoiding a plastic case if it comes wrapped in frickin plastic?! Do NOT buy this case if you care about the environment. I’m not even sure how accurate their claims about the case being plant based are… it doesn’t have the same rubbery feel as the pela case, it truly feels more plastic but I suppose that’s the TPU.

The matte finish was beautiful, but this thing is IMPOSSIBLE to install neatly. No matter what I did, the edges would not stick where the phone screen curves. I tried waiting several hours to stick it again, I tried blowing it with the hair dryer (they recommend this on the website) but nada. Cannot be done. Also, I didn't realize that this is the type of screen protector you cannot use a phone case with! The second I put on a phone case, the edges bubbled up. I tried tucking the edges under with a credit card but within minutes they would simply bubble up again. I ended up taking it off and getting a small one that isn't edge to edge simply so I can use a case. That being said, I can see how the protector could have been ideal, if you don't want to use a case at all, and you can get the edges to stick.

This cable was purchased as a replacement cable for an original one that I accidentally left on an airplane. I actually purchased two of the MIFI hotspots at once. The second unit still has the original cable. Noticing how light this cable is compared with the OEM version, I took a closer look. Fortunately, this cable does not trigger the warning message the MIFI gives when a incompatible cable is attached, but the cable is noticeably thinner and seemingly far less durable than the original. Perhaps it will miraculously still charge the device within the same time frame,. but that is yet to be seen. Still, its obvious that the cable will not last as long as the original version. The product certainly underlies the mantra that “you get what you pay for.” Image attached.

There were great intentions with the design of the product to help aid in seamless installation. However I had a less then optimal product sent to me which resulted in a poor adhesion. The other issue is the back camera protector does not easily fit with a normal case. I had to put the case on first then try to jam the back camera protectors in after, so I had to waste one whole cover because I adhered one without the case the first go around. Learn from my mistakes. Ensure your case has some wiggle room around the rear camera if you go with this protector.

I ordered this case and a couple others for my IPhone 7 since I was nervous that they might not fit right. The fit is perfect, no room left to wiggle and the phone can be taken out easily enough. It came exactly as expected. It seems to be of good quality, though I will say it's a bit stiff where it's supposed to bend. I'm sure that will change over time. This isn't my favorite style of case I've decided, but all in all, I can't really complain. If I encounter any issues I will update my review. Product shipped and was at my house in less than 48 hours. UPDATE: it's only been about 3 days that I've been using this case and the stitches are starting to pop out. Not pleased.

This seems like it would be a very nice, handy charger and it was. The problem is that the 3 regular USB ports stopped working completely. The 3 USB-C Ports are still working. The seller did not respond to a message that I sent via Amazon not sure why. I’m lucky that it stopped working a few days prior to the return period which is today 1-31-2023. I’ve requested a replacement since it did it’s job well on a recent trip and I’m hoping it’s just a fluke that this one is defective. We shall see. The replacement won’t be here until March 5th, which sucks, but what can I do? I guess I should have just requested a refund. I gave it 4 stars for power and travel as when it worked it worked well and it’s small enough to travel with in a backpack or the wife’s purse.

It is hard to find a phone case for a working person now a days. My phone is in and out of my pocket, im in and out of holes for inspecting all day, sand gets in my pockets. What is the point in have a screen protector with holes in it. There is holes for the speakers and the cameras, which allows sand in which scratches everything. The s pen isn't even covered. Its like they just gave up on the case and just left the pen to fall out and more sand in under the case to scratch my phone. I work with alot of engineers and just because it looks good on paper doesn't mean it works in the real world. Don't buy this case its just cheap and full of holes.

PROS... I’ve dropped my iPhone 7 Plus onto concrete off a short table several times and this case protected it each time. Does a very good job of keeping my driver’s license and credit cards stashed away and handy in the folding flap. CONS... The magnets that hold the folding flap secure to the case, which keeps your credit cards in place, wreak havoc on the internal component in the iPhone that senses direction. If you have a compass app, you’ll have to remove your iPhone from this case in order to use ANY compass app you might have. The leather on the sides is (for lack of a better word) “beefy” making it somewhat tricky to plug in an iPhone charging cable and have the end piece inserted into the iPhone to actually make it charge. Credit cards go way too deep into the pockets and the slots are very tight making it very difficult to extract credit cards, driver's license, ID cards and any other type of card you will be sliding into the slots. LAST NOTES... This case on my iPhone is 5 months old now as I write this review. Other cases I’ve had on my iPhone 7 Plus were nearly worn out and unusable at 5 months, but this case is very durable and shows absolutely no wear or deterioration at this point.

I had initially wrote a positive review for this product but after a few weeks the screen protector began to lift on one edge. I attempted to get a warranty replacement and was asked to send photos of the edge lifting. I followed through on that request but unfortunately the pictures have a difficult time showing it. The only thing the image could show is the Halo effect which is common with these protectors due to the 2D Display of the Turbo. Due to this I was told I couldn't get a warranty replacement which disappointed me but I didn't want to worry about it too much. I ordered 2 more protectors and attempted to put them both on but I am now going without a protector. I installed the protectors perfectly but the Halo effect was 10x worse than my original protector. It stretched onto my display which I am not too happy to see each time I use my phone. Again, perfect install with a centered application with 0 specs of dust. If you can deal with the halo effect this is fine. Unfortunately, I'm not too big on this myself. I've mentioned to iVoler that if they would cut down the glass slightly on all edges that this issue would no longer exist. The question is will they do it or will they keep this design?

The case fits perfectly and provides a good protection to the device, sure. The material matched the white bezel on the Moto X 1st gen, so it looks good too. Unlike some other cases, this one covers the power and volume switches also, so you may take a while to get used to it. The one thing that I did not like was the way this case got dirty. I was in a dusty region for a couple of weeks and my fingers picked up dirt and grime - and these were transferred to the case. I can make out the places where my fingers touched the case, and the material around the switches looks dirty too. The real problem now is that the dirt won't come off! I have tried dishwasher detergent and no dice!

I purchased this product (along with a competitor's product which had a different image). This item arrived on time, in perfect condition, and as described. On the plus-side, this phone wallet fully covers and protects the phone. The velcro closure is secure. The colors on the cover of choice are bold and true to image. I very much liked that this had a wrist strap, and thus it was more appealing than other products. It will hold about 2-3 cards easily. On the minus-side, it was a bit "plastic-y" in terms of "feel" compared to the competitor's product. Although I very much liked the availability of "classic art" designs, and the price is great for someone who likes to change phone covers a lot, I think I will just poke a hole in my other one and attach a lanyard. I don't tend to change phone covers. I did keep it as a back-up. -> I am NOT being compensated for my review :)

With this product i guess you get what you pay for. I purchased this case for $5 just because it looked decent. However; Pros: Gives the phone a good grip on your hands. Solid enclosure with rubber around it for extra protection. Looks good and fits perfectly. Cons: Huge! Makes your phone 4x the original thickness. The plastic enclosure feels cheap; there is no shock resistant material (like rubber) on the inside (so if you were to drop the phone it would receive most of the shock internally when transmitted by the plastic of the case. The plastic material feels like it's going to put scratches on my phone if i drop it. The wholes for the charger and audio port are exact fit, so some other chargers won't fit in there, this creates a huge hassle. The trim around the screen comes up a little too high, getting in the way of your fingers if you have to click something around the edges of the screen.

Smart, but VERY stiff leather. Stiff to the point that I struggle to get it to wrap around my wrist. I am assuming that it would slowly form itself to your wrist with heat, sweat, and time, but I haven't tried yet as it is a bit too smart to daily drive. For me, it is back in the box for use with formal wear. It does look great. It is smartly packed, would make a nice gift for a chap who wears a suit most of the time. It fits my large wrist ok. It clips in and removes fine from the fitbit with no additional hardware.

This product arrived on time. I went ahead and installed this and found an air bubble on the top left corner of my screen protector. Because I have OCD and it bugged me so much, I contacted the seller right away. She sent me a replacement that same day. 5 stars for the seller. After my new one came in, I took the old one off and notice that the top left corner isn't flat, that's why I had an air bubble. Went to put the new one on. Found that it was worse then the first one. The sides wouldn't stick right. If I move it to the right the left would lift (air bubble alone the side), if I move it to the left the right would lift. Almost like it was cut to wide and is starting to hit where the s6 screen curves. My first protector was 99.9% perfect, and I should have left it. The 2nd one was about 90%. I ended up just taking everything off. 2 star for the product and 1 extra one for the seller. I did end up giving the seller a 5 star seller review on her page.

I like the case, feels sturdy and not as bulky as others I tried. Have experienced the hard to press buttons, and other issues mentioned by others; but, what bothers me the most is, it seems the case designers are left handed, as the case must be fit on your left side to make it adequate for using the phone properly (without having to switch hands, or flip the phone.) I am right handed, and frankly, get tired of having to rotate the phone every time I try to use it - just for that reason, looking for another case. Why such a poor option in design? If the lanyard was essential for the product's marketability, the phone enclosure should have been designed with the lanyard holder at the top center of the case, with the indentations for the retaining clip in both lateral sides - that would have made it with a better design, and greater usability for all users - not just for those left handed (what were they thinking?)

I don't feel like I'm too rough with my phone cases and I love this one a lot out of the set I ordered. I have already had 3 gems fall off. Not too surprised as it was at the corners but what is annoying me the most is that the sides are separating from the back if the case. I have only has this case for like 2 weeks and it was my favorite. I'm hoping I can super glue it back down but I'm annoyed I have to do this after only having it for not even a full month yet.

I really liked this bumper when I first got it. Low profile, yet offers really good protection against side impacts against the glass. Much better protection than the plastic back covers that snap over the side. Also comes with scratch resistant film for the face which has been surprisingly effective. 1 year later... The bumper is 2 piece rubber and plastic, the rubber used is pretty tacky and tended to keep it from sliding easily into my pocket. Also it was pretty thin and ended up tearing though the bumper was still useable. The holes for the ear phones and charger did not always accomodate the accessories that I wanted to use. There are better cheaper bumpers out there.

I do like the way this case looks well enough though it looks kind of Fischer Priceish. That said when I got it out of the envelope it was delivered in it felt kind of cheap. I expected the rubber bumper to be softer so to better be able to absorb shock generally experienced in a drop. For the money I guess it isn't a bad case, my expectations were higher though. In the end I feel this case adds more bulk than actual protection. Also the belt clip feels kind of flimsy. I would give it a 2 1/2 star if I could. In the end I will keep it but will probably be putting my phone back in my Spigen case.

Had read that the case requires double sided tape. My case didn't come with any double sided tape but there are magnets in the hinge cover - which I don't see the point in, but whatever. Glass screen protector is not even big enough to cover the whole outside screen. It leaves a gap all the way around so have fun figuring out where to place the glass. Case is slippery and very, very bulky Makes a "cachunk" sound every time your open it due to the hinge cover moving around. Since I already opened it and applied the screen protector, I guess I'll have to keep it but would certainly give it an "C-" and have no particular to purchase any other VRS cases in the future. Will look for another option.

Just received this as the clip on my E-LV case broke after 8 months. This case looks to be a very similar copy of the E-LV, with one big exception - it doesn't have the faux rubber feel on the hard plastic part of the case. (This keeps the phone from sliding around as much when resting on a hard surface, and also grips better in the hand.) The silicone rubber jacket is not quite as thick as the E-LV. The holster plastic is also not as thick. But who knows - maybe it's better than the E-LV in the long run (which has become very hard to get or maybe completely unavailable now). It slides in and out of the holster OK - a little snug. But this may loosen up. Better than being too loose! I'm giving it 4 stars as it seems like it will fit my need and probably protect the phone well, but we shall see . . .

Product broke the second day my wife used it. I couldn't remove or install the phone without possibly breaking the product or the phone buttons so I modified the case by cutting off the thin strips around the phone buttons and it works fine. Also the case doesn't turn the screen on and off when you open and close the cover (only the closure tab is magnetic not the cover). For the price this product protects the phone just fine. I still recommend is product for the price. I'll send a pic on what I cut off when my wife gets home

After using an iPhone 7 for five years (two of those years with a bulky battery case because a small bend in the chassis meant I could not get the battery replaced) I decided to switch back to Android. I hate the facial recognition compared to fingerprint, missed having a headphone jack and needing to use a dongle to connect to my car stereo, and I also felt that it really isn't necessary to spend $700+ on a new iPhone. The iPhone SE is pretty basic for $450 and the $350 Google Pixel 4a seemed like a great choice. Look, you already know that this has a great camera, good screen, good fingerprint sensor, headphone jack, etc. - here is why it's a 3/5 for me. Even with a case, the screen cracked after falling a few feet onto a hard surface after only five weeks of use. Amazon covered a screen repair which was really awesome, but there is no reason this phone should be so fragile even with a hard case. I really don't see this lasting more than maybe two years and I'll likely go back to Apple at that point. Just too many cut corners here.

At first I loved this case. I loved the way it didn’t fall out of my hands. I also loved how the material that was used didn’t effect the pressure needed to press the volume or lock buttons. I am one to not get new cases often so after reading reviews I thought this was going to last me longer than it did. Now I’m around little ones a lot so when they grab my phone with stinky fingers or if I get a little water on my phone, I like taking me case off. Within two months I think I took it off less than 10 times. I heard a little crack and noticed that the case broke on the inside. It didn’t bother me because the case still worked fine. When I took my case off today, the rubber ripped.

The case looks like it would survive an impact very well, and as far as protecting your phone I'm sure this will do the job well. My problem with the phone is the very sharp corners, especially around the headphone jack and the usb-c port. I tend to put a put my left pinky finger under my phones when typing for stability, but the shape of the case on the bottom is quite sharp. It is extremely uncomfortable and leaves two indents in my finger affer only a few minutes. Im not sure why spigen decided not to round off the corners at least a little to make the edges a little less sharp. I've already ordered a replacement case after only a few days of using this case.

While it will charge my Note 8 it can be finicky, so you have to watch it about 10 - 15 seconds after you place the phone to see if the light in the charging plate is going to blink. Which is does about 50% of the time so them you have to unplug the charger, plug it back in, place the phone back on top and wait again. This process is repeated until it doesn't blink. Now 10-15 seconds may not seem like a big deal but it does get annoying not being able to just set my phone on top and go. A couple times I waited the 10 - 15 secs and all seemed fine but when I woke up in the morning the light was blinking and my phone was almost dead. I do not feel a charger should be this much trouble.

Este cobertor para Nokia N95 sería perfecto si la calidad del plástico fuera superior.El celular luce genial, calza perfectamente sin esfuerzos y sin peligro de que raye el teléfono.El problema con este artículo es su fragilidad,a mi me duró tres días y se rasgó en dos lugares, talvés por la presión que ejerce el mismo tel sobre el plástico y eso que nunca se me cayó ni en broma, solo lo andaba en mi bolsillo. Si quieres ver el tel protegido sin perder su glamour te lo recomiendo pero te deseo mejor suerte que yo y preparate a cuidar como y donde lo pones y si se te cae... dile adiós al estuche y Dios quiera que el tel resista el impacto.

After my first back up cam failed because it was not sealed well form rain I found this brand that was well rated. The case is very solid and seems to be well sealed from the elements. I did have a problem with this cam and am happy to report that customer service replaced my cam within the warranty that I had remaining from purchase of Oct 2018. This cam does not have the clear picture night time quality that my previous cam had so hope they will improve this issue in a new model. I have been notified by this Co that there new cam will have lux rating of .005 from .01 that is the cam rating I have now, this should be a BIG improvement! Make sure you find out the lux rating when you are buying a back up cam as it makes a Big different for night time viewing, The lower the better. I will review this cam when I get it...

Just put this case on my phone, it looks and feels promising so far. Can't comment on durability, water/dust proof, etc. But high hopes. Finger print scanner works better than I thought it would. Sound from music playing is a little different cuase of the case but not as muffled as I thought it'd be, but is muffled a bit. Love that it comes with a free replacement lifetime warranty. Either it wasn't mentioned or I blindly missed that part either way it was a nice surprise and love they offer that. Will update after I get back from a month long trip on how it held up.

It works but is not perfect. I received one of the first batches that was too small. I got the email that a new one would be on the way Nov. 2nd like many others. But mine was never shipped until I emailed after waiting and not receiving it. After more waiting I finally received the new ver yesterday and installed today. It's easy to apply, the screen is still responsive, but it's still too small and is obvious. I don't think any of the competitors are much different right now so I'm going to live with it for now.

I bought this for a ONE day hospital stay. I had it fully charged ( I think it was as the instructions aren’t very clear on the whole “flashing” numbers thing. That took 6 hours as the charger was at 34% for some reason when I removed from the box ). So it said 100...fully charged after 6 hours . I was good to go. After my surgery, I went to charge my iphone : it was at 64%. It is now at 97% and the charger; which I had also hoped to charge my iPad ( 57%)...it’s at 34%. It charged only 33% and drained well over half of my battery.: 66%

LOVED this screen protector! It went on fairly easy, with no bubbles, and looked so slick and pristine, UNTIL the next morning when I went to put my case on it and every corner pulled up. After numerous attempts of smoothing the screen protector and carefully putting on the case, it is literally impossible to put it on without pulling up the screen protector. I had the same brand for my s7 edge and it did not go all the way to the edges which prevented the case from pulling up the corners. Unfortunately that is not the case for the s8, as it fits perfectly to each corner. Sounds like a great idea, but doesn't work if you plan on using a case. Super bummer!

Had this for a week. The screen protector is good but I think the gap from the edge of the phone and edge of the screen protector is a bit too big of a gap. The camera lenses cover popped off. I was bending down to grab something, my phone slipped out of hand, phone dropped on the corner of my case and the cover popped out and attracted all the dirt. Tried rinsing it and the dirt won't come off. So to return it I'll have to pack and return everything for them to replace it.... Worth it? Nah.

I have been purchasing Iconflang cases for years. I love the ring that is normally on these cases. To begin, the ring on this case is different than the ones that I’m used to. The ring on this case is different and doesn’t fit as well with my finger. It’s needs to be lower. In addition I prefer the ring that spins around 360 on a swivel base. This ring actually turns around the circumference of a circle that it is mounted to it does not give you as much flexibility for what finger can fit through it. Lastly, it says that the case is translucent I don’t mistake yet for clear. You will not be able to see the back of your phone through this case. I wanted to see the awesome blue color of my phone but this case makes the back look grey or brown.

I bought this case in multiple colors and it was great.. until the pen holder started opening on its own- in my pocket, in my purse, taking it out of my purse. My pen fell out three times. Then, the one I bought for my mom, the face cover started sliding over during use. She also complained that it was too close to the edge of the keyboard so she couldn't type easily. The maroon is the prettiest but the green/blue one isn't really the color. The border is one color, the rest of another. The stand worked, fit the most part, at least. Had to send it back, though, because of the other issues.

I don't know about the others that posted pictures of it going close to the edges. Mine didn't. I have a Spigen Neo Hybrid case and it didn't even cover to the edge of the case. There was a gap between the case and and the screen protector. It states that it covers to the edge up to the curved glass part and that is NOT the case here. My Spigen case covers the curved edge part and didn't even touch the edge of this screen protector. I also couldn't get this applied without bubbles all over the screen. No this is not my first screen protector. I've applied tons. Just due to the fact that it didn't provide enough coverage is more than enough for me not to want this screen protector so I've sent it back. I guess I will have to look further for a decent screen protector. I've revised the review to 4 stars just for the company itself. The product is still only 2 star at best. Right after I posted my review they were very understanding and offered me a full refund no questions asked. I wish more compnies were this accomadating.

I wanted to love this case, especially for the (purple) color. I was immediately disappointed in the quality of material. I was also concerned that the round metal piece on the back would cause more damage than protection if I dropped the phone. My biggest disappointment is not being able to wirelessly charge my phone. Other reviews have indicated they were able to wirelessly charge but the metal piece got really hot. I set my phone on the wireless charger and nothing happened (did not charge). I need a case that allows wireless charging. This case may be suitable for others, but I will be returning it.

After seeing an answered question saying this wireless charger works with a Razer Phone 2 I decided to buy it. While the response isn't wrong it doesn't quite work very well. Razer built their phone with the charging coil built in the lower center portion of the phone so not all wireless chargers will work. Unfortunately for this one the twin coils are set up a bit too high so it fails to make proper connection with the Razer Phone 2 when placed in portrait mode. It WILL charge in landscape mode but the phone is so off centered to do so it tends to tip over. All in all the wireless charger works, it does what it says it'll do, and worked just fine with my roommate's phone so I gave it to him. I'm only docking a single star since it doesn't really work that well with mine. Not really the company's fault but Razer's.

I bought this case to replace a broken one I had of the same. While I was happy to find it I was not pleased at the quality as my earlier model worked. This one looked fine at first but became discolored where I hold it along the rubber strips within 2 wks. It fits my phone fine but the base no longer has hard case across the entire bottom as the original one did (which is why I was replacing it to begin with). My old case still looks better than my new one and the old case is 3 years old. I won't buy it again.

I'm actually kind of disappointed. After so many recommendations I expected more from this product. First off I expected to receive a tempered glass screen protector, but that's party my fault for not understanding the description. Installation was more time consuming than I expected and there was a lot more to it than just "sticking it on there". I followed the directions to the letter and waited for the full 24 hours after application to turn on my phone. Obviously there were micro bubbles everywhere however they did go away after a few days as they suggested. It's been over a week and the screen protector isn't completely flat on the surface on my phone. It has this weird ripple effect across the entire thing. Although hardly noticeable it's more so than tempered glass. Instead of completely forgetting I have a screen protector I now notice it every time I use it... I'll probably end up taking it off and picking up a tempered glass protector from a local store.

Great case, except comes with cutout for headphone jack, when this is for an iPhone 7 plus without a headphone jack. I know they say this is intentional so it can fit the 6 plus... but when I go on Specks website and look at this same case they advertise there "only for 7 plus" with a picture of the bottom with NO cutout for headphones. Makes me wonder why the speck website and amazon listing for the same case is different and why the cases are physically different. I would return the amazon case and buy this case on specks website because I really dislike having the cutout, but it is $20 more on specks website. Disappointed because I love everything else about this case.

The length on the lower strap which contains the "holes" is short. The upper strap that has the "buckle" is pretty long. It seems to me that this should have been the opposite? With the short lower strap length I just barely have enough strap left to tuck inside the buckle for a secure fit. I'm not a fan of this. I ended up ordering another pack from a different company. If the lower strap was longer and left more room to tuck in the strap these would have been awesome. If you have smaller wrists they should be perfect for you. Color, quality and fitment to the watch are all good though.

I just got this phone last week, and it has some nice features. The one I liked mostly is that you can put specific phone numbers on a black list and have the phone send a busy signal when they call you. One other thing is the calendar and to do list. Very practical. Also you can have an alarm set to wake you up only on weekdays. Cool!! Also, what I liked about this phone is that it's a sturdy phone, it feels good in your hand. It's beautiful, but it will get smedged easily with fingerprints. However, battery life is really bad, not what I'm used of with Nokia. Also, the slide mechanism has a major problem. When you slide open the phone, it just doesn't react by unlocking the phone. You have to unlock it manually. It seems this is some kind of magnetic failure of the phone. More users have reported this same problem. You can see these on the Nokia Discussions website. I took the phone back to the store and exchanged it for the N95. But still I like the E66 best because it has some features the N95 does not have. E.g. when in sleep mode you press the selection key you see the time. And the phone is so slim it slips comfortably in your jeans pocket. Try that with the bulky N95... I hope Nokia fixes this slide problem.

I've used several of these cases and like them more than others. However while this replacement looks like my prior purchases, it isn't. The top lip or rim of the holster is too high to be able to slide the phone out of the case. In my prior purchases the top lip is recessed. To be able to use this unit, I had to use a grinding wheel and remove almost all of the top lip of the holster. It now works well, but isn't "beautiful" anymore. Someone made a new molding and never gave it a "usability" test. Back to school for that person!

I am on my 2nd case in 8 months. My things normally take a beating which i why i get cases for everything. This case functions great. I love the wallet style and i like being able to take the phone out for pictures, i take a lot. Or just to have it more compact to fit into my running belt and still be protected be the inner case. The magnets that hold the phone in place are pretty strong. However, it is still possible for it to slide around a bit. In addition the strip work magnet that holds the civet closed gets lots of wear and tear and stars to fall apart quickly

The case fits great and has a good feel. I haven't tried its magnetic backing yet, still waiting for the car magnet mount to attach it to. However, the screen protector is absolutely worthless. When I pulled it out of the packaging, it was already warped. The instructions, as I understood them, were to simply place on the screen and press down in the middle and then it would adhere to the screen. That didn't work. Not the first, second, or third time. So I tried to use a prior protectors spray to see if wet adhesion would work. It held for a few hours, but the edges curled up so they caught on my pocket, or my hand, whenever I went to grab it. Can't return just the screen protector, so I will have to search for a different one to use with the case (which I love).

This applied very easily and cleverly. Make sure you watch the video. Adherence and alignment was great. Unfortunately, the privacy function, which works very well, is achieved using polarized film. So the film is dark, and once applied it is easy to see next to the front facing camera how much darker the screen is. No problem if you just increase brightness. However, if you go outside and wear polarized sunglasses the screen fades to completely black depending on the rotational angle of the phone. Great concept and quality, but does not work for me because I need to see the screen on sunny days.

Installing the case was literally a snap, just start at one corner and push down all around until it snaps in place. The screen protector is a different matter. It has an "applicator" which is a jig that fits in the USB port to hold 3 cutouts on the screen protector sheet that will NOT stay in the port, even after taking the case back off to allow deeper connection. Once I fumbled around a bit with that and finally got it on the phone (only one tiny bubble yay), I discovered that my phone didn't recognize my thumbprint anymore unless I pressed really firmly on the sensor. Registering my prints again seems to have resolved that issue. I think this is going to work out well. I like that it's clear as my phone is lavender and this case allows you to see it. Time will tell how durable it is.

I bought this, but I have 2 problems, 1) the holder does not really hold well on the more rectangular cup hole in my Honda Fit 2008..when my car goes over humps, the stand and my iphone5 jumps out of the cup holder despite me securing it well after turning the knob to make sure it hold tightly. 2) the viewing angle cannot be adjusted???? The current viewing angle, if I put my iphone5 resting on the phone holder, is not very correct! I have to tilt my head to view it clearly. It is confirm that the viewing angle is fix? appreciate any kind soul to help...

I want to like this case. It's exactly what I wanted, feels like an Otterbox case but with built-in screen protection. It does add some bulk to the phone, but the rubber edges make it easier to hold. Unfortunately the fingerprint scanner doesn't work. The first case I ordered had a mark on the screen protector which I thought was interfering with the phone's ability to read my fingerprint. I exchanged it for a another one but my phone still cannot read my fingerprint. I tried scanning three other peoples fingerprints and it still wouldn't read. I adjusted the display modes, brightness, etc and still wouldn't read. I'm not sure how others were able to get there's to work. So if your rely on the fingerprint scanner, just note that with this case, it's a 50/50 chance it will work.

this seems to be made well, for a woman who has a purse to put it in it would work great, for a man trying to use it as a Wallet it just did not work for me it is too thick, however the case that the phone actually slips into has a magnetic backing on it, I kept using that part, it has come in handy several times, I can put the phone on vertical metal surfaces securely to watch videos, talk on the phone or secure my Flashlight . that part alone for me was worth the money .

I bought this case (in carbon fiber black) after having an Otterbox for a long time, and I love it! It's slim, but tough and protective, and the power and volume buttons work very well through the case. The gold color on the edges matches my gold S7 perfectly. My only hesitation so far is that the fit of the case around the sides of the screen is a bit loose. I haven't dropped my phone, but at the case's loosest point, it shows the phone's outer silver edge, so I'm hoping it'll provide enough impact protection if (when) I do drop it. Altogether, great case.

My mother has the Galaxy edge and and it fitted well to her phone. I was surprise that it would protect the curves on the edge because the case was meant for the s6 galaxy.My mother said that she loves the color and loves how it protects. But the only thing she said that she wish could be fixed, is the part were you insert your card. She asked can you make a little hole were she can push the card out from the other side. Once you put your card in it makes it so hard to take out. When she has to take her card or id out, she has to take the whole case off of the phone. The phone case came very fast and when it said it would come. My mother just wish it was a bit more easy to take out your cards , as it is to put them in. I received this item at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review.

I noticed my charger wasn’t working well on a recent long drive. The USB outlet power was so-do, and the pd outlet was outright useless. When I looked closer, I noticed that the PD insert slot had separated from the metal charging ring inside it, and then the button on the end of the power outlet was bent. This outlet hs never done anything but sit in my car, occasionally switching out cables and being pushed in to seat fully. The metal casing is still solid. But evidently you can’t 100% trust the insides to stand up to extended use.

I put this on my macbook about a year ago. It's completely impossible to put on flat (and I say that as someone who's usually pretty good at putting on screen protectors) because it's so stiff, and once the bubbles are in they're pretty much there to stay. It's just so big that there are gonna be bubbles and it's gonna make your screen look like shit no matter what you do, but when I finally took it off my screen was immaculate. Within a couple of days of not having the screen protector on my screen got fingerprints and smudges all over it, I had to actually get a cloth slightly damp and wash them off just to use my computer. So, bottom line is: it works if you're cheap and your goal is preserving the screen/resale value. If you're an artist or something you should probably shell out for a nicer one, though.

I gave this a 3 stars because although I absolutely love the face cover and it looks good with almost any band, not bulky, the sticker does not hold for very long. the sticker on the inside of the face is really the only thing that holds the face cover on the watch other than the side buttons.
