Battery life and sound quality is very good. After several weeks we get voice messages saying power off power on power off power on even while we are on the phone and speaking to someone. We had to start leaving our Bluetooths turned off and turn them back on when we received a call and after a few rings we would be connected to the caller but would still hear power off power on while we were on the call, just not when we were not on a call. That's why we keep it turned off with the switch. This power off.. power on gets very annoying. This doesn't happen all the time, but too often. We will probably purchase different ones next time. We had these before under a different name and had the same problem occasionally, but not as often as these

Having only had this for a very short time, this is the best I can do. It looks nice, the phone fits good, and I like it. Given the price, I can't imagine it lasting very long. Be nice if somebody would market a good quality one that would last over a few months. Even if they had to charge two to three times the price it might be worth it. Alas, but nobody would purchase it since people go through cell phones so frequently. When this one wares out, I'll probably just buy another one assuming my phone lasts longer than the case.

I bought this for my Apple Watch Series 7 because it was stated it would fit. The watch does fit in the band; however, the watch looses functionality. You cannot swipe left or right and the side button will not scroll/spin through functions. I believe this must have something to do with the additional 1mm screen size because my SupCase for my AW5 did the same thing when I put the 7 in it. If you read something that says it works with the Series 5, 6 and 7, it does not. I hate it didn't work because the case seems really nicely designed and is very nice looking. If you have a 5 or 6, I would say buy this but don't if you have a 7.

I bought this to use for my digital art. When I first opened it, I wasn't by my iPad that I do my artwork on, so I doodled with it on my iPhone. It was nice! About the same accuracy as other pens I've used, so pretty good. When I went to use it on my iPad, it was wayyyy different which I found odd. It wouldn't draw clean lines and the accuracy was far off. I realized that it was the screen protector on my ipad, I have a paper like screen protector that seemed to be causing the problem. I have not had this same issue with other pens not working properly on the same ipad and screen protector. So if you're using a screen protector on whatever device you want to use it on, then just be weary.

The USB sockets on these are not positively locking, which means the cable pretty much falls out when left in a vertical position... which is exactly what this is designed for. I bought three of these to mount some ChromeCasts behind TVs in my office. These looked like they would work since I have a very small space to work with, however and all three of them were very loose to the point I instead just bought some power outlets with the USB inserts and installed those. I like the idea of these adapters, but the fact cables just fall out means I would spend too much time pulling the TVs away from the wall to plug stuff back in. Not worth the effort.

The anti-glare qualities of this film work somewhat well. It's a bit hard to get used to it at the beginning since you can see a small gradient separating the actual screen from the viewing angle. The viewing quality indoors is somewhat limited as well since you can see the subtle grainy-ness of the anti-glare qualities. The fit was somewhat off; however that may be due to the type of phone since I have the i9505 and this is meant for the i9500. I wouldn't be able to confirm this issue. But all in all, it mostly fits well. Application tools where on point with all the necessary tools to apply the film; it also came with a small cleaning cloth which is useful. After application, the glide that the film provides between your thumb and the screen is great. The film makes it easier for your thumb to slide well across the screen. All in all : if you don't mind a small grainy-ness filling your screen, then you should have no problem using this protective film. The anti-glare properties of the film are not the best but neither the worst.

For the price, this case does its job. The iPhone 5 fit very well, including button alignment. The case discolors easily, but it is white, maybe the other colors do better. The quality was fine for its price. The fabric tore a bit right where you fold over the case when holding the phone to talk. The fold-over aspect also makes taking photos a bit more challenging as you have to hold the phone so the flap stays out of the way. Also, the case doesn't close well if you have too much in the pockets, but it works great for a credit card, ID, and $20. You definitely don't want a bunch of dollar bills shoved in there. The clip on the strap has given me no trouble and I don't worry about the phone falling out or off. I get a lot of compliments on how it is such a great idea to have the phone, ID, credit card, and a little cash all on one place.

I bought this about 5 months ago, when the HTC Inspire was relatively new and this was the only reasonably priced cover for my phone. I have to say that it does the job of protecting your phone, but it is just not functionally a good cover. First problem: So hard to get out of ones pocket, it is almost irritating to try and get the phone out of your pocket and more times than not I end up pressing ignore or some button I do not want too when attempting to answer a call. Second Problem. The sides that come up to cover the sides of the screen are loose because of it being a stretch fit, that it sometimes inhibits one from being able to do certain functions when using the phone. Example is when playing angry birds, you cant move your finder enough to play the game fully because of this design flaw. Overall, if you are on a budget and do not keep your phone in your pants pocket, then its great, but other than that, I would go with a hard cover instead.

This phone case is nice and looks like it will protect your phone. The looks of the case is more for cosmetics. The sides of the case are very functional, not so much the back. All the grooves and black strips and fake looking bolt head’s don’t do anything. Now the little kickstand is kinda interesting. It spins 360 degrees and kickstand adjust to couple of different angles. The negative to the kickstand, it like the phone is setting on a quarter. The centerpiece is 1/8” thk above the case. It’s going to slide off of whatever you set it on. Point blank, would not have bought it if I had seen it in person. Will not get another if for any reason it breaks. Would not recommend it. I am not returning it because it would be a waist of my time. And probably will still be using it two years from now because I am not going to order anything else.

3 out of 5 because I cannot tell if this case actually fits. It wants to, so badly.. but it pushes up a bit at top as well as the bottom. It is quite snug. I had a case similar to this for my galaxy note 9, which is why I was excited for this one. It had fit the note 9 so perfectly and protected it through many drops. But this one for the note 20 ultra is completely different. It is thin, a bit more flimsy and overall disappointing. It's still cute and I'll use it til I can purchase a more protective case so I can't give less than 3 stars, for cuteness and to be honest the way it fits over the camera is beautiful almost mesh with the cameras. I used a pop socket as well as a ring on the back otherwise it may have looked a bit too "flat". I wouldn't recommend.

At first I thought this was a great product. It went on with no problems, all the bubbles smoothed right out and it looked great. Today is the 3rd day and upon pulling the phone out of my pocket, found the screen protector had pulled off and folded over the last time I put it in my pocket. I have installed many screen protectors on all my cell phones and this has never happened before. Got a 3 pack so trying it again after cleaning/polishing the screen again. If this continues to happen I will be buying a different brand. Again.... screen protector fell off after only 2 days! Have 1 left now. Ok, I am glad to say it is now 12/05 and the 3RD PROTECTOR IS STILL ON MY SCREEN and looking good after several weeks. The only thing I did differently this time was to wash the screen with an LCD screen cleaner and micro fiber cloth before applying it. The instructions don't tell you to wash the screen but after the 1st 2 protectors falling off so fast I decided to follow my own instructions.

For the last several years I have been exclusively using wallet cases. I was previously using the slide out design but opted to try this design and overall am happy with the switch. This case has room for 3 cards which I appreciate. 2 reasons for the 4 star, unable to use wireless charging due to the thickness of the case, especially when there are 3 cards in it. Unable to use apple pay if you also have tap cards in the back of phone. I have only found this to be an issue at some gas stations. I can use apply pay at Target and grocery stores with the cards still in the back without problem

This *IS* a good screen protector. I used the same brand and type for my Samsung Galaxy 5 and it worked great. However, my S5 died after many years of good service and I replaced it with a S10. This screen protector didn't go edge to edge of the display - which was pointed out by several reviewers - but most reviewers said that it was a moot point since the protective case was wide enough to cover the gaps. The Otterbox Defender does not cover the gaps and I have gaps between where the screen protector and the Otterbox case. The screen protector is trying to pop out of the case. In review - great screen protector, but doesn't fit with an Otterbox Defender.

So... Is it just the phone's design or is it also due to IQ Shield's design, possibly workmanship, possibly none, possibly all. This is the third phone in the past 5 years I'm protecting with IQShield. The quality of the material is, and has always been, pretty good. There is an inherent problem with putting a traditional screen protector on this phone since the screens are almost wrapping around the edges. Not only does the screen protector need to cover the curve of the edge of the screen. The case, if you have one, also needs to cut back on the sides to not block the screen. My problem... The sides/edges of the screen protector are coming up and everytime I take it in and out of my pocket, some lint lodges in and prevents it from adhering back to the screen. As screens continue to go edge to edge, this, i'm assuming, is a common problem. Suggested Solution... (Feel free to throw me some royalties on this design) Screen protectors that wrap around to the back the phone, on all four sides. All four sides will ensure that it doesn't come up when taking the phone out of its' case, or in and out of your pocket. It would be a multi-step application... Adhere the front of the phone first. Once it is set in place, remove the plastic backing from the two sides flip it over and wrap the sides around the back. Important that the wraparound runs the full length, top to bottom, of the phone. (optional step) Once that was set in place, remove the plastic backing from the top and bottom and wrap around.

Phone freezes a bit and I need to reboot but that is maybe once a week. I am hopeful that a future update will fix this. Annoying that it doesn't read my face properly when I am wearing my glasses. Not many apps are up to the speed with the facial scan so I need to type in my password every time I check my banking statements. The missing fingerprint button took some time getting used to but once I did, I don't even miss it. The camera is lovely as is the speed. I wish there were more color and size choices, but prob next year.

I bought this in October 2016 for my iPhone 7 and have not taken it off my phone since then. It started to become brown by December and collect dust and grits in the back. Every month I take it out to clean it. In May my phone started to slide around in it. Now it's July and the right side border has started to detach from the back part. I've been hanging onto this case for dear life because I didn't feel like dropping another $9-12 for a new case in less than a year, but the case starting to fall apart more now is compelling me to write this review. I'm wondering if Caseology has a warranty where they replace your case if it falls apart in less than a year. I'll be purchasing elsewhere if I find out that Caseology doesn't. My coworker has a clear iPhone 7 case very similar to this one that she's had for a year and it's still pristine. Though I believe the reason for that is because I put my phone in my pocket way often than she does (she's an older woman who keeps hers in her purse/out of her pocket). Regardless, I'll ask where she got hers.

I ordered this in May 2021 -- I liked all its features, it perfomed admirably until today January 21, when it failed to start up even after I had charged it to 100%. I pressed the ON button and ... nothing ... then ... nothing ... again ... nothing. Black screen, all my programs kaput -- I don't think it's still under warranty. If I bring it in for service it will probably cost me more than the original price. **OK-- UPDATED -- I did a search online and was instructed to press the ON button and the LOW Volume Button at the same time (how did they find out? I wonder how many of these phones had suddenly gone dead like mine) -- I tried this a few times and nothing happened -- but after a few more tries -- my phone came back to life !!! PS-- a customer rep kindly informed me that there is a 1 year Warranty.

UPDATED! Only had it a few days, but it is everything they said it would be. It is thinner and lighter than other more expensive cases I have owned. Very functional kick stand for both portrait and landscape viewing, and when open, you can even put your finger through it for a more secure grip on your phone. I was even able to attach a small thin magnetic plate (high on the kickstand) to attach to my car mount. It works! Weeks later ... I found that, over time, the belt clip does not grip as well, and the side that holds the phone no longer holds it well. The phone now slips out at least 2-3 times/ day.

Although i got this charger as a complimentary product to a phone that i purchases that featured up dead and i ended up returning it, the charger is pretty solid and gave a good charging capacity in a short duration. The only problem with the charger was that it was without a cable which seemed unfair to me and the charger seemed failing to reach full potential which is because the cables are usually made as per the handling capacity of the charger and if i use a cable which supports more or lesser amperage, it will affect the efficiency of both charger and the phone charging capability. So 4.

I recieved the galaxy s20 after having an android active (basically indestructible) series for the last 4 or 5 years. I was worried that my phone would break easily so I wanted a protective case. I went for the command series because it was the middle Otterbox series. The main thing i am not happy with is that there are lips on the top and bottom of the case but not on the sides. This worries me because the case ends lightly below my screen on the sides and will not protect it. the color is also different than pictured. it is a soft baby blue when others show a more blue/green. I can get over the color but not the lack of protection.

Sorry for late review. Seidio makes decent third party accessories for mobile phones and this worked quite well, but only for a while. Bought this for my HTC Evo 4G about 2+ years or so ago. Worked very well for a while, and I loved it. However, it only lasted about maybe a year more or less before the contact on the back of the base wore out and it would no longer keep a solid connection w/ the micro USB cable. Once left it in the charging base overnight, and next morning saw my phone had never charged. I also noticed red light wasn't on, but upon jiggling the cable connector on the base slightly, it came on and phone beeped, indicating it was now charging. Setting it back down on a table however, within a few seconds my phone beeped again, and the charging indicator light went off, Tried different micro USB cables but to no avail. I realized the connector must have gone bad, so I threw it away. This is why I gave it only 4 stars. Otherwise, it did work well for a while and I probably got my money's worth. I am slightly disappointed it didn't last as long as I had expected it to b/c I've bought several products from Seidio before. However, I have a since gotten newer phone but this did suffice for a mobile charging station, if only for a while....

Had it for almost a month and liked alot about it, but eventually had to return it. I was willing to deal with the poor volume on calls-- twice people couldn't hear me (maybe my carrier?), and I had to hold the phone up to about 12 inches from my mouth when using the speaker function to hear the caller. The deal breaker was when the phone started to freeze up and restart for no apparent reason with increasing frequency so I had to send it back, since defects increase over time rather than go away. Maybe it was just the particular phone. I'm disappointed as the phone was one of the few that met my criteria. Now I don't know what unlocked large screen 32gb phone with a removable battery, and all the bands I need for overseas travel, to buy.

I bought this primarily for the photo grip and remote shutter release. The photo grip is sturdy plastic, grips the phone very well (not worried about it falling out) and is comfortable to use. The remote shutter release was easy to pair with my iPhone and worked well (no noticeable lag) when it worked. Unfortunately, the shutter release would randomly switch from releasing the shutter to chaning the volume on my phone, then back again, in the same session. I tried restarting the device, restarting the phone, and "forgetting" the device and then reconnecting - nothing made any difference. Per Amazon's advice, I have contacted the seller and requested a replacement. I will update this review if I receive a replacement. Edit: No word from the company after two days. Decided to return it and buy the ShiftCam ProGrip Starter Kit- much pricier, but hopefully it will work reliably. Edit2: Just heard from the company (3 days to reply - not bad). They said I could return the item, which I already knew I could do. They also offered to reimburse me for a new one (very nice). And they said they are working on the problem, and that they will have a new model out in a few months.

This case is a decent case. The touch sensor works with it which is one reason I got it. The price point was what really sold it for me. My old life proof nuud was destroyed because it was almost 2 years old so I decided to try this one out. This case has some major fundamental flaws. The rubber access ports to the headphones and charging cable are opened by a very small and thin piece of rubber. Mine has broken on both of them, I have had this case for about a month. The main part of this case deforms when dropped so say goodbye to your waterproof ability if you drop it on the edge. lastly, the back covering is a thin plastic which can break easily. All in all I feel as if I do not handle my phone roughly or anything worse than normal wear and tear with a few drops here and there. Those are the only issues I have with this case. Especially the headphone and charging covers, my headphone cover is a major pain to get out now. All in all I probably won't buy this case again when it's time for a new one.

First off, I purchased this about 6 months ago. At first, I couldnt wait for it to come. It seemed like a perfect solution to a "cheaper otterbox". I used this for about 4ish months, and the white got irreversibly dirty. It's yellow, and gross... My biggest issue with it was how... ugly it made the front of my phone look. The front of the case is actually a square (where the camera is), and this really impacts the design. What you paid for is what you ended up getting. About 3 months into using this, the front plastic started to break off and several of the attaching clasps broke off. Also, the silicon near the plug attracts dust like crazy. Overall, it's an okay case. I, however, got so annoyed with it that I decided to buy an otterbox, which I like much better.

For $15, it seems like a good purchase. However, 3 stars fits the bill. It's okay. It won't protect against any sort of edge hit. If your phone's glass would break, it will unless it's a direct hit of something falling on top of it. Then, maybe, and only maybe, would the "ballistic glass" protect your phone. It requires a case that covers all edges, and then you should be fine. Because you are paying less for protection from an impact, and more for something that *really* holds the glass together, and thus prevents cracking. What happened to me was I had a bumper case, and this, and my phone fell from two feet onto pavement and hit the corner, making perfect contact with the phone's glass screen. The ballistic glass cover cracked quite nicely, which shows promise (not sarcasm, it did it's initial job), but the top half of the screen itself cracked with minor lightning bolt cracks coming off everywhere. I'm essentially SOL, and wasted $15 here, let alone on the bumper, let alone the $189 I'll be spending on a new screen and digitizer cause the phone is so new. Good luck, I would buy the "Spigen" or "Ghost Glass by MIME" covers instead, as I've only read good things about those since.

First, the power adapter is poorly designed: it plugs directly into outlet and can block adjacent outlets. Second, it automatically runs as soon as the cover is closed. An activation button would be better. Third, cleaning indicator light could be brighter, it's actually hard to see in sunlit room. Fourth, no signal when cleaning cycle is complete. I've forgotten my phone in there several times because there was no chime./sound that the cleaning cycle was done. So, anything good about this? Yeah, the extra USB connections are nice for charging or whatever. But this is pricier than most other UV cleaners I've seen.

I have owned many otter box cases in the past never the defender. Always the Commuter which works great and does it job well. Although this is more money, I think the Commuter otter box cases are better buy. The Defender case is strong, smooth, feels a little bulky. My problem is the screen protector. it feels weak, plus it lets in dirt or debris in between the phone and itself. Which lead me to always take it apart to clean. I'm afraid after doing that so many time the case clips on the side that hold it together will be weaken and eventually break. Otherwise its good. In conclusion the Defender will protect the phone from a reasonable drop, but the screen protector failed miserably, you not only clean the outside of the screen but you'll need to the case apart to clean the debris in between the screen and the protector.

As my first ever wireless charge, i'm kinda disappointed in the end with this product. It's cheap and it works. Bought it a few months ago and now it's aging slowly. At first, this can charge my Samsung S10+ for about an hour. But all the sudden, now i'm noticing it's charging time is slower and slower. It seems like 2 hours is the sweet spot now.. yikes. Even once, I got 4 HOURS! My advice is to just go buy a better quality one which will be more expensive. This one just has a limited lifespan and I don't think mines is gonna last for a few more months. Makes me piss because i've bought 3 more of these for my family as a Xmas gift too... ugh.

I have bubbles (light spots when viewing a white image) and I have not been able to press them out... very frustrating! This screen protector is a little thick so using the touch ID took some time to get used to because you really have to place your finger into the home button area (not just have your finger lay flush against the phone). This cover so far had the best screen quality compared to others in this price range. Images are a little pixelated and blurry at times, and you will not be able to take advantage of the iphone's retina display. Privacy at a side angle is best when the screen brightness low/dim. However because the protector darkens the screen so much, I am usually forced to use my phone with the brightness on high/max (as a result draining my battery quickly and not able to have the most privacy from the side 30 deg angle).

Sold by Santa Monica Wireless for $64.99 as new, it isn’t. The Motorola RAZR V3 arrived with a battery and wall charger. The picture in this ad does not match the RAZR I received. The front and battery covers are void of the Motorola Signature Emblem. Both covers are crudely painted with a matte black finish. The battery cover did not fit properly. After inserting a battery, its sides were exposed. Having owned an Original RAZR, I know this phone inside and out. The obvious discrepancies led to a more rigorous inspection. Soiled lint in the wrist strap eyelet confirmed my suspension that this unit was used, at best; it is factory refurbished. The phone had a plastic skin as though it was new, but the main screen has the hint of a blemish that hadn’t been thoroughly polished out. Using a RAZR that was purchased off eBay as a ‘Parts Phone’, I replaced the front and battery covers. Now it looks like what is portrayed in the Amazon advertisement. The inside of the phone showed more evidence of an ‘Other Than New’ phone. Front cover screws were slightly corroded and chip shields have marks that are indicative of a TP (testpoint) procedure. On the bright side, the phone works flawlessly, but I sincerely feel I didn’t get what I paid for, and paid too much. Best regards, Nat Ray

I bought this used in February 2013 for my 2 month old daughter (she likes to sleep with an sound app and I couldn't give her my Samsung G3 all the time when we were out). I bought this used for $25 so no worries... but it turned out that the battery life wasn't that great when I used the app/phone (maybe 1/2 the day) so I put it back on Amazon Marketplace to resell. I winded up finding a Samsung Exhibit by Metro PCS for $50 and it was worth paying an additional $25 for it. My bf couldn't believe she was 3 months old and already upgraded! Ha! BTW, my infant daughter cannot make calls. I do not turn it on, so for $25, it's so much better than having an iPod.

I bought this to use with my ThinkPads X380 Yoga. I have 3 Thinkpad X380 Yoga laptops, each is able to do PD USB-C Charging. When I received the unit, I found that sometimes it wouldn't charge the laptop - where it gets stuck at 5.0V-0.0Amps. Sometimes the unit wants to charge the ThinkPad, and will charge at 5.0V-3.0Amps. So something about this unit does not play well with 8th Gen Intel ThinkPads. I emailed support regarding my order and after 2 weeks, I still have not heard any response. I don't know if I got a bad unit or if all units are this way. Since support didn't respond, I have no choice but to return the unit. [Update March 5, 2023] I've updated my rating from 1-Star to 3-Stars, mainly for the customer service I received. Communication through the manufacture's website is non-existent, but communication through Amazon has been a good back and forth. In the end, the charger is still not fully compatible with my ThinkPad X380 Yoga. It has a max charge rate of 15 Watts via USB-C with my laptop.

TLDR: More value over time buying the official apple pencil tip and this tips from this seller. As a college student, the pencil tip could not stand a chance against lecture notes and homework problems. A few weeks into using this and it is time for a replacement. The official apple pencil tip lasts a lot longer and more bang for your buck. Writing with this pencil tip made writing a bit of a struggle since my ipad would no longer write as good and it make it more tedious finding the angle in which to write with this worn out pencil tip which was never a problem with the official apple pencil tip. At this point, I would rather use my worn out official apple pencil tip than the one from this company.

Unfortunately, my dog does not like the mail person or UPS delivery person and tends to tear things up. I ordered another brand screen, had it shipped 1 day, then the dog proceeded to destroy it. This was the second screen I ordered and like others said, one of the ribbons is too long and makes it a little challenge to install. Once you get the first two ribbons connected, the last one is a little long, but was able to connect it. Then install the metal plate to secure them in place. I was a little worried because after a week, the phone started rebooting and shutting off. I updated all the apps and checked out the phone and it seems to be working ok for the last 3-4 days. I have heard issues of aftermarket camera. Time will tell.

Long time Moment lens user primarily for the v2 wide angle and v2 fisheye lens. They both worked great on my iPhone 7 Plus with Moment phone case. When my iPhone 7 Plus mysteriously died I upgraded to the iPhone XR and bought this Moment lens case for it. The lens now require much more force to mount on this case compared to the 7 Plus case. So much so I feel like I'm going to break something. You know that feeling that something just isn't right and you should stop? That's just about how it feels every time I mount a lens on this case. I tried taking the phone out of the case fearing I was rubbing on my phone lens but that doesn't appear to be the case. Even with no phone in the case the lens are still tough to mount. The fisheye now vignettes in the left corners for still photography which it never did on the 7 Plus rendering the fisheye useless to me. Time to search for a new fisheye. The 18 wide angle lens also requires greater force to install on this iPhone XR case but at least it doesn't vignette. The v2 Tele 60 lens behaves the same way mounting it on this case but I'm not a huge fan of that lens due to it's inherent distortion that Moment attempts to pass off as bokeh. The case itself is very similar to my old 7 Plus Moment case. I had always liked the way that felt in my hand and I'm glad that hasn't changed significantly. I'm disappointed with the fisheye vignetting but at least the 18 wide angle v2 still works ok.

So I just got this today and already I am have some issues with it. The sensitivity of the screen protector is not good. There are certain spots on the screen I have to press fairly hard for my touch to register. Secondly, I can already tell the screen protector isn't going to last long. For one it easily migrates up the phone cause the edges of the case to lift it off the surface of the phone. Second, the glue on the edges is not very strong so I can see where it is lifting down the curved edge. Also I have had protectors like this where just a little bit of the adhesive is accessible so it gets filled up with dirt, dust and sand which doesn't do well with living at th beach. Now on the to the case itself. . ... its OK. The edges are not lifted enough so if you are a screen breaker like me don't bother. It won't save you phone. The finger hole in the kickstand is too big and in a weird place for me as I have smaller hands. I already miss my pop socket. I am probably going to be returning which is a shame because I really like the design but the function sucks.

Cute case and I absolutely love the lace but the sad thing is is that after using this case for about two weeks the lace started to fall off on the corners and slowly almost the whole case. A friend of mine told be to paint over it with clear nail polish and thankfully it dried and stayed on but I personally don't think it's worth the trouble. Before I painted over with the clear nail polish I look at the glue that should have held it on there and it look like it might have been dollar store tacky glue.

I bought this to put on my dashboard. While the description and the information on the manufacturer's website says that it "is designed to install to smooth and lightly textured surfaces like a glass windshield or dashboard", it surely does not attach to the latter. My 2013 F-150 has a textured dashboard like most any vehicle these days, but the Airbase won't even attempt to stick to it. It does attach strongly to completely smooth plastics and to the windshield - just don't expect it to do so on a textured dashboard. I am disappointed, as the dashboard is where I'd like to mount this. I wrote the manufacturer about this and their response was as follows: "Thanks for reaching out to Kenu and for your support. We are terribly sorry that your Airbase Magnetic is not sticking to your surface. Please try washing the suction cup with warm water and soap and re-applying. If it still doesn't stick then we will send you a replacement. Thanks so much!" I wrote quite clearly and distinctly that I was having problems with my "lightly textured" dashboard suction, and mentioned their own description stating it would, but the person responding didn't venture there at all, instead writing what appears to be a basic, 'I'm not answering your specific issue' response. The instructions say that you should wash the cup with water and soap when re-attaching the device (i.e., after using it somewhere else), but this is a brand-new straight-from-box device. It didn't work. So beware, if you're wanting to put this on your windshield or any completely smooth surface (as long as it's flat enough to completely cover the suction cup), you will like this unit. Anywhere else, you're going to be out of luck.

Due to the design of this covering, light from the flash gets picked up and deflected onto the camera sensors leaving a quarter of the image washed out. I am going to try and modify it to remove some of the material around the flash to see if that helps. Otherwise I like the case, but it does interfere with wireless charging. I may also modify it by cutting a big chunk out of it where the wireless charging area is to see if that helps. I think it is far too thick in that part for it to work properly and it really doesn't need to be thick there, just on the wrap around edge.

I love how pretty this phone case is. And it at least lasted an okay amount of time. But three or so weeks ago, one side of the case started to separate from the back of it. And a week or week and a half later, the other side and the bottom started to separate from the back of the case. It was pretty much hanging on by a thread. I was worried about its protective capabilities at that point. I also had to sanitize my phone and immediately after wiping the back of the case, a lot of the design started to flake off. Overall it’s not completely terrible but I wouldn’t purchase this case again or others like it or recommend it to people. You’re probably better off looking elsewhere.

I like being able to charge my watch, phone, and AirPods with the same device…but it is definitely a slow charge. Fine for overnight, but not what I would use if I need to get my phone or watch charged quickly. - it does have a USB port for charging non-Apple items, which I like. And you don’t have to use your own Apple Watch charging cord like you do with some other units. Also the blue “charging” lights on the front of the unit are really bright, so not ideal for overnight. I put my fan remote in front of it which blocks about 80%. So overall it does the job and has a couple of nice features, but it is definitely not a powerful unit.

I've tried a lot of these over the years but never can quite find one that works for my car. The ones that are inserted into the air vents end up flopping around or breaking the vent tabs, the ones that sit in the cup holder are fine, except where am I supposed to set my cup? I have one that clamps on the steering wheel but that one gets in my way when I'm turning the wheel, plus its blinding at night with all that brightness right under my nose. The CBLBXYB Rear View Mirror Phone Holder has all the features I like. Its a sturdy car phone mount, rotates 360 degrees and has retractable arms that snap into place with the press of a button. My only problem with it is its size. This thing is big and sturdy but doesn't fit tight on my rear view mirror (my coupe's mirror is a bit more slender than is usual I suppose). Other than the fact that I can't use it, its a good choice! It's certainly worth a try. I like the design; it would probably work great in a large-sized truck or SUV, something with large mirrors. I would say get it -- if it fits your mirror then problem solved, if not just send it back.

I really liked that this was offered as a set of three. However, when it arrived (for my iPhone 8), I realized that: (1) It didn't cover the entire front of my phone, like all of the other screen protectors I've purchased in my life. It wasn't even big enough to cover the entire black screen section, it's just a tiny bit too small. To me, I'm surprised about this and feel that it offers less protection than all of the other screen protectors I've purchased. (2) It was difficult to put on! I had to peel it off 3 times and put it back on because there was a hair caught - now, usually, with screen protectors, they have a front side and a back side that you peel off, so that you're getting all of the fuzz. This only had the back side to peel off, so maybe that had something to do with it. All in all, I would not purchase this again - I don't feel like it really protects my phone because it leaves about half a centimeter unprotected on either side of my phone.

After 6 weeks of light use, the layer of plastic padding on the inner surface of the phone mount is coming unglued from the hard plastic part of the clamp, possibly because I leave it attached to the vent in my car in warm weather, as one usually does. When I try to insert the phone now, the padding layer peels back against the edge of the phone and prevents it from sitting firmly in the clamp. The clamp is very shallow —just deep enough to grip an iPhone 12 in a very thin case— so once the padding starts to peel, the clamp’s grip on the phone becomes unreliable.

Update, about one month in, in the first 4 minutes being submerged, it let water in through the top and flooded the case, would not buy for true IP67 rating needs This phone case was $3 more than my last phone case (which lasted 2 years) upon initial open, the plastic is firmer and the phone fits more precisely into the case. After two weeks, the waterproofing holds up without letting any droplets in, the charge port cover seems more durable than most others I've tried at this price point (its also the first thing that ends up breaking for me) now I can't speak to its durability due to the short window of ownership, it has survived several 3 ft drops onto hardwood floors without any damage to the case or phone.

I find that I'm very "either/or" with this device: either I'm using my iPad and writing my notes electronically, or I have a paper tablet or notebook and am handwriting my notes. This dissonance means I rarely use both sides of this stylus in the same outing. But the stylus is a good one (I already own a [[ASIN:B004VM0SE6 Wacom Tech Corp. Bamboo Stylus for iPad/Tablets]], which is the same as the stylus here) and it's nice to have a pen available if the situation calls for one. The line it draws is a bit fine for my tastes, though. Both the stylus tip and the ball-point cartridge are easily replaceable. The ball-point replacement is a bit pricey, though, so you're likely better off using it primarily as a stylus with "emergency pen" feature.

The charger itself looks pretty neat - fairly good material used not too cheap feeling. Folds flat for easy carrying. Has 2 charging stations. But this charger didn't work too well with my phones. All my phones have cases on them so the magnet didn't work to hod them - phone has to be charged with the charger folded flat. Otherwise, if you rest your phone on the bottom - the charger has no edge to hold a phone, and the charging MagSafe on the back of the phone is not at the top of the phone, but in middle, so you actually have to slide the phone up higher for it to detect the charger. But again the magnet didn't hold. I would think most people would have a case on their phones so this charger won't work holding a phone with a case. And I know I wouldn't be taking the case off my phone just to charge it. Easier to use a USB charging cord then. So this charger isn't for me - has design flaws to be useful for my phones.

Okkkkaay so I got one of these as a gift and it was cute and functional. I really liked it, I had it attached to my Speck case on my iphone 7plus... WELL after just finding out that I could remove and reposition it, I did and it took off the clear coat on my phone case and stuck to the popsocket so now I can't use it anymore because theres a bunch of clear, thin plastic stuck to the popsocket and my phone case is missing a shiny spot. I am super bummed because I really liked this product.

This is beautiful and glitzy glam and fun or EXTRA as my friend calls it. I have dropped my phone in this case multiple times and there has been no damage so I would definitely vouch for its durability along with the fact that none of the rhinestones or crystals have fallen out of the sides. Really the only thing that I'm disappointed by is that the ring on the back has lost its stiffness so there is no like propping my phone up using the ring it just falls over. from the look of it there's no way of tightening it back up.

I found getting the bands on extremely difficult. Even following the advice of others, the pins are too short - so while I could get it in, they wouldn't latch. And because of the make, I cannot swap out the pins. I'm still trying to get one on, and it's been 30 min of trying, breaking nails, using a letter opener to try and push it in, etc. After 45 min of struggle, I gave up. Will be returning. I will say that the bands are made of good quality, so I am disappointed that I can't get them to latch properly.

This is a great hands-free speakerphone for use with Zoom /Teams calls Pros: Battery life is very good and easily lasts a full day of Zoom calls. The Sound quality is excellent with good bass - probably the best I have heard in a true echo-cancelling speakerphone. I don't mind listening to my Spotify tracks on it in between meetings. Cons: The charging cable with a USB-C connector is hardwired to the device and is about 2' long. Why, oh why did they not just provide a USB-C port so I can use my chargers with much longer cables. If I run out of battery, I need to relocate this to within a foot of an outlet, which is super annoying. The other fail is that the mute button on the device fails to synchronize with the mute button on my Zoom desktop application. On my Jabra, if I hit mute on the device, Zoom would mute too (that way other participants can see I'm muted) but with the Poly this does not happen. A third minor issue is that you have to press the power button and hold it for 5-6 seconds to turn it on. Annoying - 2 seconds like with most other devices would have been sufficient.

The case came quickly from the seller. The case is quite stunning and perhaps is what I was looking for, but then, where is the tempered glass screen protection mentioned in both pic 2 and then the Special features section in the description? There isn't one. Suddenly, there is an additional area below the " Add to Cart" that mentions you will need to also order a screen protector. What happened to the part of the description about a screen protector built in? Trust me, I looked and looked before I chose this case over others! I am very disappointed. I found others that had all the necessary protection. TOO BAD and shame on the seller for deceiving me! I gave it a decent review just because the case looked beautiful.

The Invellop blue slider is one of the many 3-rd party accessories out there for the iphone. This iphone case however, was a good price at $7.95. I prefer two-piece sliders much better than snap-on and it's a tight fit so the pieces never fall off. Moreover, my favorite part about the cover is that it is raised so if you drop your phone it should hlep to protect your screen if it falls flat on its face. Are there others like it yes, but can they beat the price of this one, probably not. I recommend the Invellop slider case for those that want a good cover bumber for their iphone and don't care about the designs or anything. My only problem is that it's a little loose on the bottom piece and slides out too easily.

I use this to mount my iPhone 6 Plus to the yoke of a Piper Arrow. I use it in conjunction with a ball clamp and short, double socket arm. I love how easy it is to snap my phone into the "claw." Even with an average case a 6 Plus fits, as well as my Wife's iPhone 6 (yes, she flies too). The nice thing is that the RAM system is so flexible, with so many mounting options that this can be used for a lot of devices with a variety of mounts, clamps or suction cups. The build quality is average as the first one we bought broke. The internal springs broke after about six months. The second one has lasted over a year. I guess it's a good thing I didn't review this immediately as I have more experience to write about.

Bought this for our cross country move. Installing it was a breeze! I really thought it would take a lot longer and more effort. It's held up well with the 2,600+ miles I've traveled so far (more to go too). My only complaint is the swivel ball that allows you to turn and rotate the phone casing has become wobbly. On bumpy highways and roads it will sort of fall or tilt down. Everything is secure though and it doesn't seem to be a case of anything needing tightening. It's just the swivel ball can't handle the super rough roads as well as I would like. Even given that, I would recommend this unit. It's served me quite well.

When I got the box in the mail (on time), I was so excited to start my screen protector installation. I opened up the packaging and started my first installation. I cleaned the screen, applied the protector and used the lint catcher. All to no avail. When I would open it up to get one piece of lint, another flew in. This happened also for the second screen protector. On the second one, I thought to myself, if I screw this up I'm not going to be able to get on my phone till they send my replacements. So I pulled the second one off, and instantly applied the third screen right behind it before there was an opportunity for any dust to come in. by far the best method. I really would like to use that lifetime guarantee though.

Let's start with the positive. ... I like how it feels in my hands, the magnetic ring is the whole reason I bought it. So I could hook to my magnetic phone up to the magnet in my car car without putting an ugly on the back of phone case. Now I'm not too happy about the color I expected it to look like the main picture, the real color with black buttons. But it's baby blue with orange side buttons. If you go threw the photos you actually see what it really looks like but the main pic is false advertising. I guess it's my fault. For not looking through the other entire photos . But other than the color I think I'll be able to live with it til I can buy to the one I really want once they make one for this phone.

I've never cracked my phone screen from normal use, but when I got a Pixel 3 I thought I should get screen protectors just in case. These were super easy to install and work perfectly. My only complaint is that they seem to be more fragile than the phone screen itself. They chip and shatter from incredibly minimal impact. The first one happened after I bumped my keys against the screen. I assumed the impact must've been harder than I realized and so I replaced the screen protector, but the same thing has happened. It wouldn't be so bad except when it breaks there are all these tiny shards of glass that feel very dangerous to be on something I hold near my face a lot. Next time I won't buy glass screen protectors :(

The brushes work, but then so does a new clean toothbrush. The only port swaps in the package that work are the pointy ones for the audio-jack. They fit in, can be swirled around, and remove some debris. The flat soft felti-ish pads that are the size of the USB-C port don't get flat enough. See, if you were to base the size of the tool you need JUST on the port dimensions, sure, they made these to spec and they hypothetically are the perfect fit. However, actual functional phones have a connector chip in the middle of that port hole. Which means for the swap to fit, it needs to be thinner. Otherwise it would bump up against that contact chip... which it does. Which means it is unable to actually perform it's intended function.

Great product, very nice fit. Company needs to have someone re-write their English. Both for their product posting, and manual. Very poor phrasing. Why is it that car manufactures put so much into the technology of a vehicle, but forget to design a spot for your phone? We have a 2018 Mazda 3 GT, and had been holding off on any type of phone holder because nothing seemed to work up until seeing this. Received the item yesterday, and just installed it. It clipped right in place with no adhesive, marring the finish, or damage to the dash. Great if longevity, or future resale value are concerns. Will follow up on review with pics. After putting some time behind the wheel with it. Update 03/09/2020 - use of the magnetic mount with a rugged or thick case does not work out. Since I own a 3d printer I can modify the mount to accept a holder that works better. Well aware other do not have that option. Would recommend 3M tape for the disk, and externally mounting the disk to the outside of the protective case.

Seller is fantastic! Product not so much. I bought the tempered glass screen protector and although I'm certain this is done on purpose to work with certain popular phone cases, the glass is not wide enough to fully cover the screen in a way I feel is satisfactory. Even if the glass is positioned as accurately in the center as possible, it does not cover the viewing area completely--there is about half a millimeter of uncovered screen on each side of the glass. This bothers me to no end. I previously purchased the tech SKIN and I find that to be far superior in terms of coverage.

I tried it on both Pixel 2 and Pixel 3 in China and only to find that I was not allowed to add Access Point Name (APN) on these phones. So I did not have phone to use for the first couple of days while in China. I still give the product 2 stars because I'm unsure if the problem lies with Google phone. In either case, it will be so much better if I was warned when I purchased the product. By the way, I later went to a mobile carrier's office in China and acquired a SIM card with my passport. For about $8, I was given 5G data and more than 100 min talk time for at least one month. If you can get around in China, this is much better and reliable deal.

**WARNING -- PHONE COMES WITH MULTIPLE AMAZON PRIME APPS YOU CAN NOT REMOVE.** A few apps you can disable, most you can not. **WARNING -- PHONE COMES WITH MULTIPLE AMAZON PRIME APPS YOU CAN NOT REMOVE.** Apps include Amazon (not removable, can disable), Amazon Alexa (not removable, can disable), Amazon Drive (not removable), Amazon Kindle (not removable), Amazon Music (not removable), Amazon Offers (not removable), Amazon Prime (not removable), Amazon Widget (not removable), Audible (not removable), Good Reads (not removable). You can disable notifications for all apps except Amazon Offers and Amazon Widget. I bought this for a gift for my husband - if he hates the App notification too much, I will have to try to return it. **WARNING -- PHONE COMES WITH MULTIPLE AMAZON PRIME APPS YOU CAN NOT REMOVE.**

I agree with the other reviewers. I bought my first one two years ago and used it for work a couple times a week. It charged up fairly quickly and the sound quality was okay. I liked the way it plugged in, since I keep my charger on my desk and I can see the blue light. I mainly used it for books/podcasts so the sound was good enough. I liked that it was in one ear because I could still hear if someone called me. After maybe 6 months the battery life declined noticeably. I didn't want to pay the full price so I waited until the price dropped slightly and ordered another one. I had hoped the first was just a fluke and that this battery would last longer. Unfortunately that's not the case. I now have both plugged in so that I can use one while the other charges and just switch them out when one dies. I do think that I will try a different brand next time to see if I have better luck.

I want to change my review to 3 stars. This one fell off after 2 months. I tried two other brands. They fell off after 2 days. That makes this a better buy. However, the others came with a warranty so they could be replaced. Give it a zero star if I could. Fell off after two months. I work inside so no great stress on the watch. The cover just fell off. Also note: this seems to be the only watch cover that the company does not give any kind of warranty so you're out of watch protection and out of money.

I had initially bought this for the Apple iPhone 12 Pro Max, but after upgrading to the Apple iPhone 13 Pro Max with a Moment Case and Lens Adapter - it became too unstable. The clamp doesn't work very well with the Moment case, so I had to remove the rubber side grips, which helped hold it. I even paid DJU $25 for their newer Magnetic Grip, which is slightly larger, but it still fails to gip the phone correctly. If you add filters or lenses to this gimbal, it is way over the payload limit, and the filter adapter hits the gimbal. I eventually sold this and upgraded to the Zhiyun Smooth 5 Gimbal (very happy with this gimbal), which also works with FiLMiC Pro.

This was an upgrade from the blu studio 5c...so far. I love this phone. Yes it works on straight talk. No it will not support a Verizon sim as it is a gsm phone. I use at&t sim with no issues. Transfer was easy as well. Camera is fantastic. Not advertised feature, hotspot. This is a huge bonus, as we have children who can now YouTube on long car rides. Also, flashlight comes pre- installed. For me, its the little things. Update...its been over a year since my purchase...the battery gets hot and causes all sorts of issues. When I initially purchased this product, I had it for just a little over a week before the clip that fastened to the air vent in my truck had broke. I considered it to be cheap. So I wrote a review stating this and gave it a one star. Several weeks later the company reached out to me and offered to replace the clip that failed and I agreed. When I received their package, I was surprised to see that I got a completely new unit to include the charger itself. I believe the charger is good, but the clip still seems to be the same. The fastener seems to be made only for horizontal air vents, and it doesn’t seem to work very well on vertical air vents, or up and down. But aside from that the product seems to be OK. I was disappointed, after the company sent me a new unit altogether, that I received an email asking me to either give them a five star rating, or remove my one star rating all together. I sent them an email back saying I would do neither, but I would give them an honest review based on my opinion.

I had the original that was made for the IPhone 6 Plus before the 7 plus came out. It was great, fit perfect, and lasted 2 years with lots of abuse. I just got this newer version and the bottom rubber piece by the head phone jack and across to the speaker fits loose and has a gap between it and the edge of phone. Secondly, the first time I deployed the kickstand, it broke. I hardly ever use the kickstand but still, that’s junk. I was really high on this case after the original was so good, but this new version barely gets 3 stars from me. I won’t be buying another one, but for $17 bucks I guess you get what you pay for.

I've bought this 3 times because the papery quality is really great. But I started noticing that after a couple weeks of use, the corners would start loosening up a little bit (like not be flushed against the screen). While it's not a big issue, since the cover isn't like falling off or anything, it's really annoying to look at. At first I thought it was my phone cases but after swapping cases multiple times and trying this product out 6 times (3 packs x 2 screen protectors each inside).. I've come to the conclusion that the adhesion just isn't that strong after a while of use. It's a shame.

Edit: The case finally broke, approximately 8 months later. The hard backing separated from the soft sides. This was based on daily use. Never dropped the phone, but went into a pocket daily. I liked the case enough to buy it again, but 8 months seems like a very short life, so dropped the rating from a 5 to 3. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I don't have any experience with other cases, but some of the key points: -The finish is nice. The molding lines are almost invisible and only ever so slightly appear in the corners of the case. -Fit is amazing. -Buttons are easy to press. No problems with the double power tap to open the camera app. -Cutouts are spot on and don't interfere with the OEM charging cables, or any of the headphone jacks that I use. -Fingerprint reader is easily accessible. -The back of the case for the most part doesn't stick to the phone, with the exception of a small area around the camera cutout within the small curve. -There is a small raised lip around the screen to keep it off of surfaces when face down. -There are tiny bumpers on the back to keep the hard back off of flat surfaces. This will prevent the back from getting scuffed up. -The case adds a small amount of grip to an otherwise fairly slippery phone. -It moves in and out of jean pockets easily. -It doesn't really show fingerprints. -The only negative I have is that there was a very very small piece of debris that was molded into the case, and is slightly noticeable. It doesn't bother me. Overall a really great blind purchase.

The Best rating I could give this is 3 stars (thought about 2). First off, the seller advertised it as an 'AT&T Unlocked' phone. When I received it and activated it, I found out it was a SPRINT phone! So, it was a huge hassle getting the AT&T network added, plus I have some background Sprint stuff that will be on the phone forever. Next, the phone will not download multimedia messages via text (i.e., when someone sends you a picture) - we have yet to get that problem resolved. Has not been a good experience with this phone yet at all, other than that it does have good battery life.

I love having a pop socket or some kind of handle on the back of my phone for support and as well as a stand. I was really hoping I'd like this one and bought it because the price was decent. As you'll see in other reviews, the ring on the back is too low and it spins easily so it's hard to hold and when putting it up as a stand, you have to mess with it a little bit before you get it just right... it's annoying. I tried to give it time to adjust but I want something more stable and in a better location. Also, I never used the mount so I can't speak on that aspect of it.

The screen protector in itself is good quality, and the accessories to help apply it properly are good. For me, the fingerprint sensor's efficacy hasn't significantly worsened, but it does affect it slightly. BUT, the cutout for the selfie camera is bizarrely miniscule. Like it may even be smaller than the sensor itself, let alone the actual cutout in the screen, which this screen protector's cutout is significantly smaller than. Wish I could say anything different. I don't take a ton of selfies, so I'll see how long I can live with this, probably not long and I may have to return this.

If this product doesn't work anymore, please do followings to fix. Any battery case could have this problem. 1. Remove your battery case from your phone. 2. Put the battery case in the drawer for one month. (depends on how many percent of charged) 3. check (push the button and if the light is on, put it back in drawer) 4. repeat number 3, and if no light is on, Put it back to your phone, and start charge. It should work now. This is not a problem. This could be happen with any battery case. Always you can fix with this manual.

Using these with well-recorded music is a dream. I am hearing accents in music that I never knew were there. I am actually EQing my music much less with these - no need to make up for defects anymore. However, they don't make highly compressed recordings sound good - if anything, they reveal the flaws even more. They look nice, and feel reasonably solid. I have no serious issues with them. I wish they were over-the-ear, but then they would be a different product. They are reasonably comfortable, but I do admit to some fatigue after a while. I do however have two minor quibbles. (1) The cable is rather flimsy (but obviously can be easily replaced, which is why I bought them in the first place). (2) They are huge. They barely fit me when fully retracted. There is no way my wife or 12 year-old could use these.

I was a little skeptical as to the claims of how much it protects your screen from shattering (being a nervous iPhone owner) However, got in a nasty bike wreck a couple weeks ago, and really put this thing to the test. Results - the screen protector shattered BUT the screen itself wasn't even scuffed. Nice job TechArmor. Screen took my full weight (240 lbs) straight into asphalt. I was impressed after pulling the protector off and seeing no damage to the screen. Unfortunately, the phone BODY bent and is now a bit U shaped.. but that's on apple. I say this product is quality, does what it's supposed to, and is a lot cheaper than inferior stuff that you get at cellular stores or best buy. Go for it. **********UPDATE 11/6/13************* So, being very please with the product, I ordered a new one for the 5s I just received. No kidding, it didn't last more than 2 days before cracking across the center of the screen, chipping at the corner, and becoming quite scratched (from a tumble out of my hands onto the bathroom floor, while inside of a Thule case). I am quite confused by this, because the very same product was used on my 5 for months without any problems whatsoever. Perhaps quality control sucks, maybe I got a particularly weak one, no way of telling. Get your stuff together TechArmor... the hardness of this screen was hardly anything to brag about. I'm going to try another brand for now, but will perhaps come back to this brand if the other

First, I want to say it is a beautiful case built with quality materials. However, after 4 months the corner of the case started to come apart. I contacted Torro regarding the matter and was told, "the camera is very close to the top of the handset, this part of the frame is very narrow and therefore there isn't a lot of room for the adhesive which attaches the leather to the frame. This part of the leather can be easily pulled going in and out of pockets etc, so I would check that this isn't happening", which indicates to me that this is a known problem. I was instructed to either send it back (with a prepaid label provided) to England from the U.S. or to fix it myself by applying adhesive. I'm a bit disappointed as I really like the case for its esthetic and the material, but cannot be without a case for a $1200 phone for an extended time. My hope was that I would be able to return and have the item replaced through Amazon. Unfortunately that is not the case.

After about four months of use, I started getting random freezing and auto reboots. I did what most other people would do, I got rid of unnecessary apps and I even resetted my phone to factory settings. None of these things helped. Upon closer examination, I discovered that my rear glass had been cracked. I decided to remove it and discovered that this battery had swelled up to the point that it cracked my rear glass. I believe that it's faulty voltage was the issue was giving me performance issues. I purchase the new battery and all the issues are gone.

Uh, this case was great until i started using it regularly. The clip broke the first day, there are 2 edges that help hold it to your belt or pants and they have broken already with out it being knocked or banged around. Additionally, the phone slides in and out of the holder and its too tight. I have to push the phone in really hard to get it in, it does stay in there well, but eventually its going to make the rubber casing loose its elasticity, I hope this case lasts 6 months until i can upgrade to an iphone 5.

I liked this pretty well (I have a Samsung Galaxy S5) until a few days ago when it just flung off my belt without me even knowing it. I was in the parking lot at work locking my car when I saw a black object on the ground and realized it was this holster with my phone in it. After that I stopped using it. I suppose there's a way to secure it better, but my confidence is low and I can't afford to lose my phone so easily. Otherwise I like the holster itself and worked well for the 3 weeks before it fell off.

Have to agree with most of the others. It is great as a speakerphone, but the FM transmitter needs work. I bought it as a bulk pack and went to the Jabra site for instructions. Had difficulty actually getting my stereo tuned in to 106.9. When using the FM option the static often breaks throught the call. Otherwise, easy to use, portable, uses the same charger as my GPS, so no big deal. Has a long battery life, so I just bring it in sometimes for an overnight charge. Worth the money vs. others. On speakerphone, call clarity is great and I like hearing "call ended" so I know the line is not still open.

I bought three packages of Mr. Shield screen protectors (2 for Samsung and 1 for HTC). The first pack was excellent. I was two for two. The second pack was not good. One protector was good, but the other was cracked. I didn't send them back because I only needed one of the two at the time, and I wanted to avoid the hassle of a return. The third pack (same product but for my Samsung) was also one for two. One of the protectors was good, but the other was actually the incorrect item. I did not find that out until I went to swap out the first protector for the second. Good product, but inconsistent in terms of packaging and item accuracy.

I have had 3 of these cases. Purchased from Verizon. ALL THREE HARD CASES BROKE. They have a very real tendency to crack at the corners when putting on and taking off the hard case. If you plan to put it on and never take it off this is a great case. Good pretectection. Nice aesthetics. I even droped the phone two times, once in my gravel driveway and once in a parkinglot. Both phone and case were fine. The problem comes with the removal and replacement of the hard case portion. If your like me and occasionally have to remove your battery or remove the case for cleaning, your gonna run into problems. I did. WITH ALL THREE CASES. I like the case, so i gave it benefit of the doubt, obviously purchasing three before giving up. The way you have to put the hard case on causes stress points at the coners. After doing it a few times the corners crack and split. EVERYTIME. I was super careful and tried different tactics to win this battle to no avail. Now i just use the silicone part of the case, which is fairly indestructible. BUY THIS BEARING IN MIND THAT IT IS PROBABLY NOT GOIN TO LAST IF YOU TAKE IT ON AND OFF.

I was extremely excited to receive this product as it met all 4+ review components. Beautiful case Beautiful packaging Screen protector ...and even a very sweet “start up” thank you note. I have not dropped my phone and thus cannot speak as to the protective nature of the case, however, what I have noticed is that this case does cause my phone to unusually overheat. Prior to this case, I had an otter box - it was great. No issues with overheating and amazing protection but the product broke on the edges. Unfortunately, I do use my phone regularly both personal and business and after about 30 minutes, the phone begins to get extremely hot enough so that I have taken the case off to allow it to breathe. I’m saddened that I will have to look at purchasing a new case that can handle the amount of usage needed.

Pros: First, this piece is very comfortable to wear. It feels better than some more expensive ones I've tried and infinitely better than some cheaper and comparably priced ones. For reception, the sound quality is loud and clear, even is noisy environments. I'm told that my voice is coming through very clearly as well. Had a call during lunch and the person I was speaking with said they couldn't tell I was eating, so a plus for noise cancellation. Battery life seems to be great. Standby mode lasts quite a while with no noticeable drain. Cons: The voice prompt and ring for incoming calls is annoying and amateurish in my opinion. While apparently the noise cancellation for me eating at lunch is excellent, the person I was speaking with said that they could hear a woman all the way across the restaurant very clearly. I personally could barely hear the woman referred to. The controls for the earpiece aren't as easily used as that of traditional style bluetooth earpieces. I'm not used to wearing behind the ear setups though, so this is a personal quirk.

I purchased 2 packages one for me and one for my mom. I watched the video to make sure I was applying correctly. I read most of the reviews so that I knew what to watch out for too. I know others mentioned that the film comes off when you are charging the Fitbit. This is the problem that my mom and I both have. This starts becoming a pain every time you charge you have to go through the process of re-applying another film. I thought the film covers would last me the amount of time we keep the Fitbits, instead I'm going through a box of them in almost 1 month.

The photo makes the colored part, in my case I chose the pink, look metallic. Nope, it's not. It's non-shiny plain pink. And the black part was not that rubbery. I often check by feel if I have my phone and I feel for the rubber. I was worried this wouldn't feel right. Returned it. But you can't beat the prime delivery, fast and free for trying these cases out. And the prices for most of the cases on Amazon are very reasonable. This one just wasn't my cup of tea. I bought a three part case instead with rubber bumpers around the edges and hard plastic on the back and front, with NO screen protector.

I really liked this armband until it broke. It fit my iPhone 7 phone perfectly. It even had a big enough hole for the headphones to go through (which is he same type of cord as the iPhone charger). It stayed on my arm for the most part, except when I adjusted it too tight. It stayed on pretty well, even with running, biking. The plastic piece that holds the strap snapped when I was trying to put it back on my arm. My arm was really sweaty because I was working out and there was too much resistance on the band around the arm. It snapped when I pulled the strap to attach to my arm. I would recommend being very careful when sweaty or get an armband that does not have plastic holding the straps (just Velcro or a metal piece). Another note, I rarely used my phone in the smaller section of the armband, the part where you can see your phone screen from the outside of the armband. My phone would get stuck because moisture would get into the armband. It was much easier to pull out my phone when placed in the larger section. The picture attached shows where it broke. It has tape on it right now.

The screen came as advertised. But now camera takes real bright pictures.. I wish I would've paid the few dollars extra and got the screen with the camera, ear speaker, etc already installed. With this screen you have to take those pieces from your old broken screen. I got it installed and everything works. But for some reason the camera takes real bright pictures now. Not sure what I did wrong... I took it back apart and didn't see anything wrong. So now I am ordering a new camera for $13... I rated 5 stars because I got what I paid for as advertised.. and it works as expected...except the camera (which didn't come with the screen)... my advice ..pay the extra for the screen with the accessories already installed

Your accessories are great but the metal band for the Fenix 5S is hard as hell to put back together after removing links. The person on your YouTube video has a hard time as well. It took me over an hour to complete. I’m generous with giving 4 stars as I have 3 of your silicone watch bands for the Fenix 5S but I’d love to see a way that you can tweak the design to make it easier to put the band back together after removing links. So this phone was listed as new. I wrote the seller to ensure that it was new and I was told "Yes, brand new.". The item I got was clearly used and I only have 30 days to be sure its working which would have been great if it was in fact brand new but there's no telling what has happened to it etc. The phone is a very basic phone and gets very hot when charging. The charger is huge and I'm not sure it is the right one for the phone. The battery does last a long time when its standing by. I don't know how good it is when in use.

This armband case fits my Driod Razr HD very well, but I found that the seams between the fabric chafe when I'm running. My girlfriend bought a sports band for her iPhone that has much more comfortable material, but cost twice the price of this band. For $8 dollars I figured that the band would have lower quality fabric, but really it's the seams that cause the discomfort. If I could do it again I might spend around $20, but with large/heavy phones like mine there still might be a lot of movement. In the end, I stopped using this armband after my third run with it, and I switched to keeping it in a cheap drawstring bag ([...] If I tie the bag in the front, my phone won't bounce at all, so it's really comfortable, but it's much less convenient to access so there's a trade off. tl;dr - If you want a band, get something higher quality, or try using a simple knapsack.

I like that this case is very slim and light but I found it very hard to hear the other person on the other end of the line; even when I turned the volume way up. It is definitely waterproof and that was the primary reason I bought it. However, when I went to use my finger print to unlock the phone, I noticed that a portion of the home key was covered up by the white material of the case and no matter what I tried, I could not get it to fit right and because of this overlap, I could not unlock the phone with my fingerprint. It was not worth returning so I used an exact-o-knife to cut the part away...now I have a slim, light case but it's no longer water proof and it's still hard to hear through. Half the time, I have to pull the cover off when I am talking to someone. Maybe the case I got was defective but the bottom line is I should have read more of the reviews before buying this case....I probably would have passed on it.

It works fine daily, but it has some things to consider before you buy it. I bought it for use in Venezuela and works perfect. The first week I installed some games to check RAM and processor and it runs great, but the battery won't last a day. The screen is ok, but it has a limited viewing angle and I can't read in it if Im not holding the phone in certain ways. The front camera is VGA (Pic1), bad for indoors pictures or videos. I don't use it very much most of all because of the viewing angle of the screen that bothers me. The 5MP rear camera can't make focus properly and the pictures have a lot of weird grains when you zoom in it (Pic2). The sound is very very low, every phone I've had sounds louder than this one. I have to put it near my ear or use earphones to hear voice notes. The internal storage is limited so if you plan to install many apps or apps with a lot of data storage, you may find installation errors because of it. I installed Clean Master to keep it optimized and free of junk files.

I had a feeling the advertised 42800 mah wasn't accurate, considering the price. I decided to completely drain the battery by charging my phone a few times on it, then when the phone would no longer charge I turned on the flashlight and left it on overnight to drain it completely. Then I added a little USB meter to the cable to see how much it would actually hold. As you can see in the photo, after nearly 21 hours of charging it topped out at a little over 18000 mah. Obviously it's still useful and the solar charging can come in handy, but don't buy it if you expect 42800 mah, or even half that.
