Doesn't seem like the case's button covers line up with the Pixel's power and volume buttons. It takes extreme force to push the power button- lesser so for volume, but still no good. Seems like this is the only waterproof case for the Pixel 4a so far, so small price to pay for a feature that should be inherent to the phone to begin with ... **contacted company and they sent another case bc they said it shouldn't be that hard to press buttons- still is. Having major problems with the touchpad sensitivity. Have almost heaved my new phone into the wall bc I have to hit things about 10 times around the edges of the screen for them to register.**

I bought this phone new at the end of 2015. It lasted me about a year and a half, but it should have been at least two years or more. Ultimately, this phone's undoing was a failed charging port. At first, it was just a loose connection. I thought maybe it was the charger. But then eventually, it was determined the the port itself was shot. I could have sent it in for repair, but it was already past warranty. Once the battery drained for good, there was no using this again. It is a shame because I liked the phone until it broke. It had a beautiful AMOLED screen, it was relatively fast, the camera was decent, and I loved the diminutive frame, thinness, and lightness of this thing. If this same phone was available for about $50 now, I might actually break down and buy another one. At this point, that's all this should be worth at this point. However, I can't justify still paying $100-$200 for this in 2018, especially if it is likely going to be a refurbished unit and might develop the same problem. Also, the other downside to this phone was that it was only 16 GB of storage with no expandability.

The small solar panel size should give you a clue as to how well the solar recharge works. Plus the 80 hours of CONTINUOUS strong sunlight to charge it is 10 days of 8 hour a day direct sunlight to charge it 100% from empty. Even for enough of a charge to recharge one cell phone you need 2 days of sunlight. Main complaints are: 1. Solar charging is impractical to the point it is false advertising. 2. The 4 blue lights to indicate percent of charge remaining on the battery pack do not work - they are all always on. There could be only 5% of a charge left and you would not know it. 3. Once the green led turns on the device will no longer charge anything. However you can still turn on the light - and leave it on so a charge is still in there. 4. There are TOO MANY warnings about leaving the device in a hot car and in the hot sun. A bit suspicious. 5. The unique USB mini port is ONLY to charge the device. Cant use that port to charge anything else. All in all - Not knowing how much power is left on the device is unacceptable at a minimum expectation. At $18 I am keeping it as it can fully charge my cell at least 4 times from a full charge camping as it is a 20,000mah battery pack for only $18! BUT - I think I should never take it traveling on a plane due to the heat issues.

There's a circle in the middle of the screen protector towards the bottom, you can see it all the time. Dont know why its there. They need to remove it and show accurate pics. Thinking about returning it Update: thinking the circle is for finger prints. This screen protector went on perfect, very easy, no bubbles and has stayed on. Along the sides have not lifted like all the other protectors I have purchased since the beginning of 2021. I'm giving it a 4 right now and I'll see how long it lasts and update again. Great screen protector. No lifting no cracking

The screen protector was fairly easy to put on. I struggle with these things so it took me 4 or 5 tries to get it positioned where I wanted it. The screen protector works well. I had no problem with bubbles or first that always seem to plague me when putting on screen protectors. My only real complaint is the size. It barely covers the active part of the screen. I understand they made it smaller because the edges of the screen on the nexus 6 are curved but they could have made it significantly bigger. If it reached the edges of my case I'd be a happy camper as it is I'm kind of disappointed, especially for the price of the product which isn't terrible but a cheap non-glass screen protector would have fit much better.

Usually I don't go back and write a delayed review, because it may not be the right time to do it, but unfortunately I have to do so now. The phone took a hard impact, near the edge of the curved infinity display, and the glass shattered. Admittedly, it did so UNDER the screen protector, so you can't really feel it. However, I've had the phone for six months and the display is slippery, easy to drop, always catching my finger movements on the side of the display as screen taps, which makes me give the phone a horrendous review. But the protector deserves justice too. Since I got it, the protector does very little to help the phone be more easily grippable. The protector doesn't even come flush on the sides of the front screen, so it isn't adequate for the job as I see it. Overall, I feel better with reusing my Motorola Droid Turbo from 6 years ago.

This lasted about 8 months of daily use. It eventually wore out right at the cross bar that attaches the band to the bezzel. It was fairly comfy for as cheap as it is. Just know that it'll break suddenly and isn't built to last. Having said that, I ordered a second until I can find a better quality band that'll last. The one your watch comes with works, but whoever thought a rubber wrist band was a good idea should get slapped. The thing sticks to your wrist, pulls hairs and is genuinely uncomfortable. I despise it in every sense of the word.

I'm kind of disappointed with this one for two main issues, but mentioned in previous reviews. 1. The rubber on the ears is very cheap, and has already started to peel off after putting the ears through the holes one time. The holes are just to tight and sharp for the sticky pads to last very long. 2. The one that I got must be a newer version, as it looks different than the pictures. Most of the customer provided pictures show the older style with just one set of holes. One picture (as of this writing, shows the model with the three holes. I purchased these lens protectors in late December 2022, as of writing this review it is april 2023, they seemed to work okay i never had any incidents but a few days ago one of the glass pieces popped off the ring that surrounds the edge of the camera leaving the lens exposed, likely due to the fact that the glass is not flush with the surrounding ring making it easier to slide off as its just a bit of sticky stuff holding it on. The screen protectors were great, and did burn through one, but the second one applied just fine (my error, not the products). It looks great and fits nicely. Let's get put the way that it's cute and it's Hello Kitty so even more cute. As for a phone holder it's ok 3 stars at best. The clamps on the sides of the holder that keep your phone in place is not big enough if you have a pop socket or ring on thr back of your phone. Taking care to clean everything, I was able to put this on my phone cleanly with zero imperfections on the front or back clear covers. Buttons work great. Touch sensitivity is unaffected. Rubber is sticky enough to do its job keeping the phone from sliding, but not so overly sticky that its hard to put in your pocket. The only reason I don't give this 5 stars is the cover flap for the USB-C port. It is a very stiff rubber tab that strongly resists being moved out of the way for a charging cable. Once you insert a charging cable, the cover flap will press against the side of the cable-end fairly strongly. I worry that the components in my charge port will become bent over time due to the pressure the flap puts on the cable.

This is the 4th and 5th of these I’ve had. All worked flawlessly. My first got soaked in the rain and the switch stopped working. The next 2 got lost. Noise cancellation could be better. I really miss my old Jaw Bone in noisy environments. Otherwise it has good battery life and great sound. I generally am on the phone all day with them. They say 8 to 10 hours talk time when fully charged. However I generally run out of juice after 6 hours and switch to a second one I have charged and waiting. They are acceptable from a comfort perspective. There are after market silicone ear pieces that make it more comfortable but I’ve been using these latest ones lately without the silicone after market ear piece.

Here are the main things that are wrong with this phone: no expandable SD card and no headphone slot. The reason for the first is laughably obvious, in that SD cards are a cheap way to greatly increase storage space but they want to rip you off by charging massive amounts to upsell you on a much more expensive phone with more storage. So I went from an S10e, a much older phone, to a Galaxy Flip and lost much storage capacity and entirely lost the headphone slot. The second problem, the lack of a 3.5mm headphone slot, is so they can upcharge you for some crappy Samsung wireless earbuds that die after 4 hours. Wired headphones never die. Or you can buy a C to 3.5mm adapter converter but then lose any ability to have a portable charger. I work 12 hour shifts and used to love to listen to audio books for 12 hours or longer. I'd use a wired headphone jack and a portable charger at the same time so my phone and headphones would never die. None of this is possible with the new Samsung phones. The screen folds which is neat but that is literally the only good point. The old phones were definitely better.

The instructions said merely to plug the cable into the charger and into a block and let it go. We did that last night. We numbers were flashing as if something was happening. This morning, the numbers were the same and still flashing. My husband then noticed it said in very small letters "Out". So, we tried another block. This time, it said "In" so we left it to go. That was at about 10am. It is now EIGHT HOURS LATER and it has only climbed up 22%. In EIGHT HOURS. So I read the small details. It recommends a block with 5v/2a or 5v/2,4A power. I checked mine. It is 5v/.3 which is waay too weak for this (but works great with our phones). I checked another block here, it is 5v./1.55 I checked another. It is 5v/1a. So not one single block in our home is the recommended size for optimal charging. You would think the manufacture would INCLUDE a block specific to its needs. Guess what we have go buy now.

Overall, I love the convenience of just putting the cable to the base and letting the magnetic piece do its thing. I have been using these exclusively for 10 weeks. 90% of the charging I do is overnight, so the slow speed of charging isn't an issue in my use case, but the problem I have is that on 3 occasions, I wake up and the phone is almost out of battery and never charged overnight. After this happened the second time, I make sure each evening I check to see that the batter has the indicator active showing that it is charging, and last night it did, but this AM my battery was at 9%. These need to work 100% of the time.

You get what you pay for. The touch sensor is definitely sensitive as it turned off on me multiple times within the first five minutes of use. Also having to turn off Bluetooth on your iPad is annoying, what if you wanna listen to music? Lastly, the biggest issue I had is that this pen cannot swipe up to get me back to the home screen on my iPad mini 6. I don’t draw, so I think I will pass on this cheap pen and wait till I find an actual Apple Pencil on sale. This thing can definitely get you buying in a pinch though. But I’m not fond of it.

This stand is BEAUTIFUL...I purchased a different one and it didn’t fit my phone right and when searching for another I found this! The only thing I would have liked differently is the color scheme of it. I like the purple/blue in the pictures but I received one that is green/yellow. Not sure just yet if I will keep it because of the colors but the stand itself is amazing. I have an iPhone 12 Pro Max and it fits perfectly even with my popsocket on my case which it the problem I had with the other item I ordered.

Nice case and sturdy. Feels great. Easy to position IPad much better than Apple's own smart cover. It holds iPad securely. It is a steal given the price. But I dropped my iPad with this case once because the hook got in the way and I failed to get a good hold of it when it was handed over to me. Fortunately, it is in my car and it only hit the surface of the console. Still, it made a big bang with ipad facing down! Couple times, the hook almost potentially tangled with my hands and caused the same problem. It is annoying. Then another problem is that it is not easy to open the iPad when it is closed. The only plus is the ease of closing. That is about it, but not worth trading for giving all the bad. I think it is good for the company to remove the hook design and replace it with something that is soft such a belt. To sum this review up, I thought it was a good product.

This is a tough case and will no doubt protect your phone. However, there are a couple of issues that led to me swapping this out for a new case after just a couple of weeks. 1. The edges around the screen intrude enough that it was difficult accessing the edges with my fingers. Inhibiting usability is a big negative in my opinion. 2. The white case looked great out of the box but quickly got scuffed around the edges after I put it in my pocket. Definitely noticeable after the second or third time. I think they should have used the black outer with the white case. In less than a week my new case looked dirty and dingy (see pictures).

It took me a little while to assemble this. Some of the cardboard pieces were difficult to align but I think I got it at the end. One of the sides don't stick well even with the provided sticker and does seem to come off every now and then. I tried viewing various youtube videos via this, the image quality doesn't seem to be good. I was using this against OnePlus Two android phone. The video quality through the lens seem more like 360p. Overall - good to try VR at low price but don't expect to be amazed by it or to view it on a continuous basis.

It goes on easier than I thought, and it looks good, but... I use screen protectors because I carry the phone in my pocket together with change, keys etc. These hard objects make dents in the surface of the TechSkin, and while it does eventually "heal" these scratches and dents to the point where they are barely visible (after 24+ hrs), they do leave the surface less than smooth in the meantime. If you don't plan on putting your phone in a place where it actually will get in contact with things that could scratch or dent this kind of screen I guess it works fine, but not for me. I am going back to the "three protectors for a buck or two" style which seem to work better for my use.

This case is VERY slippery! I have dropped my phone more with this case on than I did when it didn't have a case. And I dropped it a lot. That being said, it has protected my phone well. I read a few other reviews that said it wasn't a perfect fit for the 6S, and I have to agree with that. There is a little space between where the two pieces connect that just won't close all the way. It's not the end of the world, but it's also not my favorite thing ever. I just really don't like how slippery it is. I'll probably order a different case.

I've tried contacting this seller & was unable to b/c i was over my 30 days- I had 2 deaths in my family the past few weeks VERY close death & i was unable to contact seller before the 30 days- I was going to send an email & ask if they could work with me on replacing it due to the reason why i couldn't response before the 30 days (honestly i recieved the case & had so much going on i didnt even think about it) - That is not the seller's fault though but just saying- anyhow the case is super cute & super soft....but it isnt tight on the phone dirt gets stuck in it & the rubber wore off the first week i had it- Like it wore off to plain white like ive had the case for 1 year already- I wish i could get in contact with the seller & just get a replacement but o well :( I don't want to purchase another and it do the same thing- but maybe i just had a bad case & hope they are not all like that

UPDATE REVIEW....6/8/17 I had some trouble with my protector and contacted IQ Shield. They were great in sending me a replacement product, but unfortunately kept sending me the S8, and not the S8 Plus. When i tried to explain this to them, they insisted the regular S8 protector would fit. I will no longer argue with them about this significant size difference, so I went ahead and purchased the correct size for S8 Plus from another vendor. I hope no one else has this issue. The advice to install it before bed was great as well, because it needs time to set and dry overnight with the phone off. When I woke up the next morning and picked up my phone, I could not even tell the protector was on there. It looks that flawless, no bubbles or anything. I am very happy.

About a year ago, I purchased the red version of this very case. I LOVED it...it was very sturdy and protected my phone during some accidental falls, etc. I also liked that it wasn't bulky and it's not silcone-like, so it easily slides in and out of my pocket. After that case was showing some wear and tear, I decided to purchase this one on here instead of at my mobile carrier's store, as it was $20 cheaper. I was VERY disappointed when it came. Any time I would lock my phone, it would practically slide the bottom piece off. This did NOT happen with my first case. Why? Well, my first case had much more ample "sticky" (more siliconey) piece INSIDE the case to help keep it on. It never budged an inch. So I took this new case to the store and it turned out it's simply designed differently. I then purchased another one of the original red I bought a year ago and haven't had a problem. In closing, the look, feel, and sturdiness of this case is nice. But if you want it to stay on your phone, consider something different. Or purchase in store so you can see what it's like.

The Garmin Speak Plus is an interesting combination of functions - dash cam, navigation, and Alexa. I thought it had a lot of potential, but it turned out to be a rather frustrating device in use. The app is pretty straightforward, and I was already familiar with Alexa from devices in my home. However, certain functions (e.g. custom skills that combine basic skills) are available over Bluetooth but not using an AUX cable. Huh? That was annoying, but that was not the deal breaker for me. Luckily this happened on test routes for which I already knew where I was going. However, on multiple occasions in the middle of a route, the navigation would go away and be replaced with a notice that the software was updating. Yuck! How would you like to be navigating in an unfamiliar location and have your directions vanish on you? I could not find a way to prevent this, and for me, it made the device unusable. It very much feels like a beta release and needs some improvements before I would recommend using it.

I have & have had many UAG products. I had this Watch protector on for less than 2 full days & never got a chance to use it in any rugged way.(the entire reason for choosing this item) I believe it happened while exiting my vehicle like a normal calm human. I was so excited about this product. I really wanted to give it 5 stars. However, this case is not shock proof at all. I dropped it once and the whole side cracked, so I doubt it's water proof at all now. Essentially I wasted my money :( If you are clumsy or have kids that handle your phone and are looking for a shock proof phone case, this isn't it!

It still appears to have a very slight curve on the underside, but not enough to cause problems. I was disappointed that the charger does not charge my Apple Watch as quickly as the charger that comes with the watch. It also makes my watch feel slightly warm after it has been charging for a while. I don’t think it’s a safety concern, but this is a sign of a lower quality charger, in my opinion. The overall remote is of good build quality, the packaging is nice. However under the hood, I have problems with the software and coding that was put into this remote. First, the remote goes to sleep way to fast. Probably about 10 seconds and the remote will go to sleep. If you aren't aware of this, you will miss several (if not all) of the shots you intend to take. Second, often times the range is just super poor. I can be standing 10 feet away with the remote behind my leg and it won't take any pictures. I almost have to be pointing the remote at the camera...Then other times randomly I can be about 20 feet away and it works fine. Lastly, it just overall often leaves me frustrated. Half the time I will walk back to my phone to find that it somehow turned the screen off, or didn't take any pictures at all, or only took one photo instead of 5. Then I have to go back and re-pose or reconnect the remote...etc When it works it's great, WHEN it works. I feel this was made more for indoor use, and I mostly use mine hiking at distance outdoors.

Never having owned an Otterbox case before, I did not realize it's like armor for your phone. Great for firefighters and mountain climbers, I guess...but for me, it's overkill. My biggest complaint is that it is very difficult to text with this case. The rim is too high and obtrusive when texting. The color (Ocean/Night Blue) is nothing like it's pictured here. WHAT YOU GET This Belkin Sheer case is a topaz blue. The surface is hard and smooth and it's holes line up perfectly for 5cs. One of the things I like about the surface is that despite the fact that it's smooth, it's not super slippery. I've handled some smooth cases that were like holding ice, this case is easier to hold than that. WHO WOULD LIKE THIS This Belkin Sheer case would be good for people whose main concern was protecting their phone from scratches. People who want the least amount of bulk added to the phone. SUMMARY I know from the experience of family members that different people want different things from their phone case. This phone cover is a thin sheath that is rigid and doesn't provide protection against drops. It's lightweight design and smooth surface means that it won't add bulk to your phone, so that you'll easily be able to slip phone-with-case into your back pocket without any grabby surfaces making it a struggle. Great price.

I just finished comparing the BTX270 to the Oontz Angle Plus - side by side. I received the Kinivo for Christmas but had my eye on the Oontz. I wanted to compare the two and was prepared to return either one. The Kinivo outperforms the Angle Plus acoustically, except that the Angle Plus is louder at max volume, and I would say the bass response is indistinguishable between the two: The Kinivo is brighter and more realistic (less boxy & tinny, less radio-like), through the highs and upper mid range. Neither speaker is big on bass (nor could one expect them to be, given their size), and the lower mid-ranges were very, very similar. Bass on both speakers was present, but weak. All in all, both speakers are respectable for their size, but I chose the BTX270 as being more realistic. The BTX270 produces sufficient volume to fill a 10 x 15 foot room well above speaking level and the Angle Plus is probably 15% louder. I would recommend the BTX270 over the Angle Plus, unless you are after bigger volume. I did not evaluate the moisture resistance of the Angle Plus. Both units seem very well made.

The Incipio Feather Iphone 5 case does not disappoint. It fits well, does not add much bulk to the phone and offers great protection. The shoulders on the sides are raised a hair's width over the front screen surface. This is good feature, it keeps the screen from coming into contact with the surface of the table when the phone is placed upside down. The only issue I have is the knife's edge at the bottom headphone/speaker/lightning connector area. It makes the phone uncomfortable to hold. I am sure Incipio is already aware of this and would not be at all surprised to see this corrected at some point. I was really surprised with the elaborate retail packaging. It almost seems like more design effort and expense went into the packaging than the actual product itself. Overall the Incipio Feather Iphone 5 case is a great buy. I highly recommend it. Update: because of the nature of snap-on cases the top and bottom end of the phone is exposed. It did not take long before my phone accumulated a number of scratches along the exposed sides. Combine that with a couple of 3ft. Drops and my phone looked like it was 3 yrs. old. Got the Incipio Frequency case now which is MUCH better. Wish I had it from day one.

I owned a few Lifeproofs in the past and I would choose them over this Ghostek case. I am guessing it has good waterproofing, I haven't tested it out. The sound quality while talking on the phone and listening to music is diminished. I tried to do a return but I guess I waited too long, and the product they offered to exchange it with, was half the price I paid for this case. Not a fair exchange nor are they fair in backing up their product.

Its a beautiful phone. Calls, texts, speaker is wonderful. Down side... Mose badic google apps are loaded on the phone but the apps do not show up. To get to messages, I have to go through contacts. I give this product 3 stars because it works. Its almost exactly like the lifeproof case, except comes apart much easier. I find myself snap'n it back together a few times a day, but for the price so far it has been much better than expected! My wife has one as well and she has the same issue. I wouldnt trust this case in a downpour or a puddle of water, but for your basic everyday abuse and moisture control i think its great. The ringer on/off switch worked better on this case than the Lifeprf case. I would refer this case to anyone looking for an alternitive to the expensive ones!

I really like the durability and build on the cases themselves, but the holster portion is lacking. The case really protects my phone and makes it very easy to hold the phone even with wet hands. I try to be very careful, but phones get dropped on occasion and it has made it through all of the knocks and bumps with no issue on the phone. The only real problem I have experienced is I only get about 6 to 8 months out of the holster/clip as the belt clip breaks off of the holster back..It would have been a much better design if the clip and holster were metal or at least the clip and its attached area. I have purchased a few at a time when the go on sale for this reason.

It isn’t horrible. I mean, you do get two of them and it is a phone stand as well as Qi charger for under $30 (if you have the iphone 12 -14 though, you probably wish it was magnetic which it is not.) … but it is so primitive looking. It looks like the device they used to have in shoe stores to measure your feet! (If you are old enough to remember shoe stores, you will see what I mean.) It does not look particularly attractive. That is definitely not a game changer if it works well, but sadly this does not. It just isn’t very fast. It took a very long time to charge my iphone 12. I am going to have to give this a pass.

The Lifeproof LifeActiv Quickmount Adapter is a very flexible mounting system for your phone. Essentially it is a small magnetic that glues on to the back of your existing case. This magnet then works with the lineup of existing Lifeproof adapters to let you mount your case. I have the bikemount which works fairly well. I have a rather large phone (A Galaxy Note 4) but this does a pretty good job of keeping it securely attached (just make sure you follow the directions on how to clean and mount the magnet on the back of your case). The one major downside is that the magnets and teh adapters are fairly expensive. While this is a nice setup it is hard to justify a magnet that costs over $15 and then accessories that cost over $30. Another flaw is that while the magnet is secure I would not really test it with a delicate device such as a phone in very challenging environments. The photos show people playing watersports but I would restrict this to mild activities so you don't risk losing or damaging your device.

When I first got this phone case I really loved it! I love the pattern and the clear case looks awesome on my white phone. My only issue is that it must not allow the phone to cook itself down very well because I constantly feel my phone getting extremely hot while this case Is on it and I frequently have to remove the case to prevent my phone from overheating. This is a big issue for me as I really need a case on my phone as much as possible to avoid cracking it. If I didn’t have this issue I would have given 5 stars because so far it seems durable! I’ve had it for about a month or so.

The specs seem to indicate that this device will supply power to devices WHILE being charged, but it only does that with the wireless charger. When you plug this unit into the wall to charge, it will stop supplying power to devices connected via the USB. And if you unplug the wall outlet, you sill have to press a button to start charging the connected devices again. I was hoping to use this as an in-line uninterruptible power supply for my grandfather's iPad in the hospital, but it won't work. He is not capable of finding and pressing the button to restart charges, and understanding that when the power is plugged into the wall, and the iPad is plugged into the battery pack, it isn't actually charging, and will die. I specifically rush-ordered this device because it says "Charge while Recharging" but I failed to catch that it only does this wirelessly for some reason. I'm giving it 3 stars because that's sloppy product design, and sloppy messaging. There are cheaper devices from other manufacturers that include pass-through charging.

I must admit, the style of this case is quite nice! The picture doesn't do it justice in my opinion. It takes the dinky little iPhone 6 and turns it into something I can really keep my hands around, while still keeping a relatively small form-factor, and it looks awesome! However, it doesn't grip the phone all too well. There is very little gripping on to the front of the phone and I would have preferred it if the edges went a little bit closer to the phone. The phone has NEVER popped out of its case on any kind of impact though, but every time I take it out of my pocket, I have to push one of the corners back into the case, which is rather easy to do and isn't really a big deal, but I can see someone dropping it as they take it out of their pocket with that corner exposed, it could easily hit the ground phone first -- but I've never had this happen. If having to pop the phone back into its case every once in a while when you take it out of your pocket (has become second nature to me) then you can consider this a four star review, and I'd recommend the case! If that's an issue for you, or you commonly drop your phone directly out of your pocket, I recommend looking for a case with a bit more grip.

This is a case 3 for my Samsung Tab Pro. The previous one had rotating parts and was very slick. I have decided to buy this one based on feedback. Wrong decision! Ordered 4 months ago. Love the look and feel of the case, but now its cracking around the edges and coming apart. This case looks awesome on the phone. I really really wanted to love this case. All the cutouts on the screen are in the right position. Unfortunately this case has one big downfall for me. Otherwise buttons on the side are perfectly placed and the charger, s pen, and earphones are very well accessible.

I really wanted a case like this one, but if I have to keep buying replacements within 2 weeks, it's not worth it to spend $6 plus shipping cause this wasn't eligible for Prime membership free shipping.

so, for a headset that is supposed to be designed for job site conditions, this one is waaaaay too quiet. i replaced the Steel with the Stealth which is much louder. also, not having a "real" on/off switch is a bother. Stealth has sliding on/off that you can use without looking. the Steel on/off swith is a button you have to press and wait for something to happen. also, it's advertised to have "large" buttons that can be used with gloves... yeah. maybe with thin latex gloves. the talk button is a small bump that is often hard to locate with bare hands. otherwise, it connected rapidly to my phone each time, never dropped calls, and does feel rugged... but since you are probably not going to be using it where it is windy or dusty or raining because you'll be moving inside to hear anything, you may as well get the Stealth.

I guess you get what you pay for. I originally purchased my first case around the middle of Nov 2020 and that only lasted me for about six months (May 2021). At the time, the upper right-hand corner of the hard plastic frame broke. After a failed attempt at gluing it back together, I decided to buy a 2nd case thinking that maybe it was just a one-off and that the 2nd case would be better. The 2nd case did last longer this time around (up until recently). However, it broke in the same exact place again! Therefore, I am cutting my losses and getting an Otterbox Defender Series instead.

Not the best design, speaker hole molded in wrong place and covered mouth speaker completely. Had to cut out hole to see speaker. Case is slim, but tends to come off easy as there is only the back plastic holding, the front rubber corners come off under normal use. On the plus side, it does look nice. However by looking at the pictures I assumed there would be more rubber instead of plastic molded to look like rubber, hence the phone is very slippery, which was the main reason I purchased the case in the first place, I thought the main case was rube riled at least. Overall, if the shipping would have been free, it would be worth the $8 cost.

Well, it's a stylus, and it works MOST of the time. You have to wear this weird glove to use it, it isn't pinpoint accurate per se. It writes. Amazon never posts my reviews because I'm too honest for them, especially considering the first thing I saw when opening the package. Soon as i opened it, there's this card with the word SORRY written across the top, I'll all caps. I'm already thinking the pen is gonna be so bad, they were apologizing before I opened it. So I read on. What is said, was that if I gave them a 5 star review, they'd give me 20 bucks Amazon credit. Here's the kicker. On the bottom of the card, they offer you a another 5 bucks if you don't mention the card in the rating btw. Think about that a minute. They wanted to give me 25 bucks to rate a 20 dollar item? I'm want born yesterday. Please don't fall for this.

The rubber armor is noticeably loose-fitting & doesn't wrap around the front of the phone very much (to protect where the screen meets the phone's body)... other than that, it seems to work fine. The "free" clear screen protector (the flexible plastic type) was not the best... no matter how carefully I tried to place it on the screen, I ended up with lots of bubbles (which I could not get rid of) & the lower right corner of the protector just wouldn't stick to the phone's screen at all. Very frustrating. I ended up buying a Dmax Armor tempered glass screen protector. See my separate review of that product.

PRO: This is a thin strong very durable case. CON: The kick stand is hard to flip out;especially, if wearing mechanic gloves. Even with gloves off, the stand is hard to flex out. Use the stand for supporting the phone in hand, but the stand is curved which causes the fingers to slip up & out. Also, to wireless charge you need to pop off/out the kick stand. Other than the NEGs, it does not feel like phone is in a case. Wish the back side had a more rubber grip or continue to weaved gripping on the side of case to be included on the back where the case is just as slippery as the phone not having a case. To use the magnet, you must remove the kick stand which is cumberson going in and out of car using dash magnet wireless charging. You can drive a Mack truck over the case, since work in off highway construction will keep case for work only.

I have been using this phone for more than 2 months and, although I do not like the Android operating system and the unnecessary permissions in many of the apps, I like the phone. It has excellent battery life and the large size makes it easy to browse the internet and read the screen. The negative side of the large size is that it is difficult to handle with one hand and that makes it only average as a phone. I now grudgingly use the Bluetooth feature in my vehicle and that is probably safer. The one feature that prevents me from giving a 5 star rating is the anemic alarm. Perhaps it is just my particular handset or the pitiful alarm clock app that can not be removed, but at maximum volume set for all profiles I can barely hear the alarm when I am awake and near the phone. I do not have a problem with alarms on other phones and the jog dial turning on my clock radio will usually wake me before the first note is played. I have tried many other alarm clock apps on this phone with similar results. I would still recommend the phone because it is a good value and the volume of the phone ringing and notifications other than the alarm is sufficient.

Cons: I’ve had this case for almost 3 months and I’m not disappointed by the purchase but definitely going to be a back up case. The ring holder was stiff to start which was great because I could half heartedly prop it and it would stay in place. After 3 months the ring has become pretty loose and you’ll have to set up at the perfect angle for it to stay in place. Something else that I grew to appreciate less was the cover for the camera. Only because it was slick so if you don’t use the grooves it would take a lot more effort than I’d like for it to move. Maybe putting a rubber piece on top to make it easier to slide? Lastly if you try to lay the case flat and text it will move/tilt but if you avoid pressing too hard or typing fast then should be fine. Pros: the case feels super sturdy despite being thin that I would not worry if I dropped my phone. The sides provide enough grip so it doesn’t feel like the phone would fly out of your hand if you don’t use the ring 24/7. The back camera protection is appreciated just wish it was easier to slide over for a quick snap but at least you’ve got it covered just in case.

well i got this for around 120$. not bad. really good actually. definetly isnt perfect though. however i see how the repacking at the amazon lab could have missed these details... sim card tray was stuck so i had to google the problem and do surgery on the phone to get my sim card in. involved a screwdriver and a pin. not rocket science but lame. then after turning the phone on ( i noticed the speakers were full of dirt- it had had full a life before me), i noticed the 2nd hangup- the home button does not work. makes navigating difficult. googled that and managed to resensitize it for a few minutes but then lost its responsiveness again. I Ended up using it is assistive mode with a touchscreen floating home button. does the trick, though lets face it its not as it should be, however, the phone was 120$ instead of 500$. So if your ok with a few tech repairs and character building glitches go with the cheaper then average but still operable restocked iphone 4 :)

The pictures in the ad clearly show the case should be 0.3" I measured the thinnest part of the case (in the middle) with my digital calipers and it measures at just over 0.4". It's even thicker where camera and bottom edge bulges are. It does provide good protection though, as even with a glass screen protector the case edge is still just a hair taller than it. The back is protected well with hard crystal clear plastic but it will definitely scratch. The lightning port hole is more than big enough for the largest cables. Also, the raised button covers click very well. They click just as well if not better than the silicone Apple case so I was pleased about that. Cheaper cases sometimes make it hard to click the buttons. The sleep button slot is large enough for easy muting/unmuting, but is set in a bit deep though nothing out of the ordinary for a case of this size. Overall, for the money, a good case.

By and large this is a really good case. Very thing and I think it has a great chance to protect the phone but the lip around the screen doesn't seem like its enough. there is no screen protector and i fear that it would be close to impossible to install a really good one. If you are super careful and have no fear of cracking your screen this would be a perfect case for you. I can tell you this case will survive a pocket level dropto the solid ground and to the carpet. its a reliable and sturdy case.

Worked excellently for my Note 3 for a long time. I feel like it could have been a bit prettier with cables everywhere and such, but the price is right and it works great. Ended up getting a new phone that it simply doesn't work with; Samsung 6 edge+. I understood going into it that the HDMI bit wasn't going to work because of the phone, and the curved edge of the phone causes the lip in the dock to be unable to hold the phone up in landscape (and its not really a portrait dock) and I think I can forgive those two things, but the usb Cable can't plug into the phone at all. There is a tiny tiny metal tab on the connector that keeps me from plugging it into the device. I suspect there is a reason for this so I'm not going to force it in or modify the plug. I guess I'll just retire the thing along with the phone :\

I am in love with this phone ring. I've owned it for one week. It is still as stiff as it was when i first got it. I believe it's easier to hold than the popsockets. I like that it can be turned and twisted any way, and it can hold the phone up at any angle. the sticker is VERY sticky and the ring does not budge. The two complaints I have are that it only came with one sticker, and the description stated two. The second complaint is the surface has already been scratched up quite a bit, and I've had the product for one week.

The case does what it's supposed to do which is why I gave it 3 stars. I took off 1 star because the magnet is not strong enough to hold on my car mount. I took off another star because there is a very disturbing chirping sound coming from the case when it charges on the wireless charger. I have used 4 different wireless chargers hoping that the chirping would go away but it wont stop and I can confirm its coming from the case because of this. The noise gets very disturbing at night when I am trying to sleep and I wake up constantly to this irritating noise.

I purchased this case because it holds the s-pen for the S21 Ultra. My son has had Spigen before and he said it was a good case. I had my phone 3 weeks and I accidentally dropped it and now there is something loose in the phone that rattles. I have always owned otterboxes for my phones, that protect phones so well, even when dropped. Now I'm stuck with a phone that I'm sure something will stop working soon because of the rattling part. All because I wanted a case that would hold the S-pen and purchased this Spigen. I guess I should feel blessed that the screen didn't shatter!

Purchases two renewed iPhones, one for my son and the other for myself and within six weeks experienced problems. On one phone the touch screen was not working in the center as shown in picture. This problem keeps going and coming. We use it as is. On the other phone after attempting to do an update, the phone would not reboot with an error message 4013. Tried everything recommended online by the apple site. Had the phone assessed by an apple approved technician who said that it had a hard drive problem and paid $36 to repair. It works now but not the Face ID. For both phones I reached out to the supplier and on each occasion I was given the opportunity to return the phones and get replacements or a full refund. However, because I live outside the US the costs of getting the phones on US soil was too much. So be wary if you live outside the US

Easy to install — AFTER TAKING ABOUT 20 MINUTES TO REMOVE THE BACKING FILM. I didn’t even realize there was a film, initially. There were no instructions. I assumed it was a simple click on to install. Tried using my fingernails, but that was futile. So, I resorted to trying to grab ahold of the edge of the film where a small bubble had formed, but I was afraid I’d scratch the very surface the ridiculously-stuck-on film was protecting. I finally managed to peel back a corner using my pointy tweezers, then switched to blunt tweezers to peel it back more, but the adhesive seal was so strong, the film was trying to tear. So, back to fingernails. Wouldn’t a bad product for its intended use — “IF” — they used a less sticky backing film, and included an instruction card.

Bought this when it was billed as fitting the LG 305C - which it does, sort of. The cutout for the camera lens on the back is square and the 305C has a round lens opening, so that's a little off. There are NO side cutouts for the on/off or the volume control, which is a pain. It fits a bit loose. But the worst thing about this one for me was that it picks up everything but men and money! I put the phone with the cover on into my sweatshirt pocket and it came out covered with lint and bits of whatever there was in my pocket previously - I think peanut shell fragments and/or sand from fishing at the beach. I've now removed it from the phone and will look for a better solution. On the plus side, it was ordered on 1/11/15 and arrived on 1/16/15 so that was good. I like the color too. Sorry that it's not a good solution for my phone and me.

likes 1. light weight 2. the knobs fits perfectly to access volume and pen etc dislikes 1. the protective plastic that you peel of on the front of the case was more responsive to the touch screen than the plastic for the case so the manufacturers can consider making it with that built in 2. the plastic at the back at the finger print area working well so far (2 months) but i find it can be punctured easily so i am very careful when pressing my finger against it i have not tried the waterproof capabilities so no review on that.

Was very excited for this product because of the color and the double compartment. I thought it was really nifty cause you had two different pockets, one to store cash and the other cards. That's important because for my last one which only had one pocket when I put a lot of cash and spent it the pocket would be stretched out and the cards would fall out more readily. The reason it's getting three stars out of five is the back isn't sticking very well to my phone. (I will note I have an iPhone 5s with an otter box case). It peals off a little bit and I have to push it back down. I would still recommend this product!

Update: When it first came out of the box it appeared to be of flimsy construction but it worked. Not long after, I have trouble with the plugs. They won't stay in charge mode. I have to jiggle and jiggle the cords and plugs to get them to turn on. Maddening. When it works, it's great but otherwise, it is bad for my blood pressure. Buy something more durable. The unit at first seemed of flimsy plastic. Was easy to assemble. Once assembled, I realized it was sturdy enough to hold my tablet. Glad someone mentioned something about the plugs, that you pull the caps off to get usb. It worked just as described and shut off when my tablet was charged. Now I don't have to choose whether to charge my phone or my tablet. They charged quickly. I am very pleased.

I bought this product about a week ago. The first day I had zero issues. About three days into it, I started to notice that I had some bubbles. Then today happened when I just pulled my phone out of my pocket and discovered this crack. I have not dropped my phone or mishandled it in any way but I have a web all across my "screen protector". I have never had this issue with a screen protector before with my iPhone 6s or X so I'm just going to see if a different company may have a better quality one.

I will be reaching out to the seller.... nothing about the packaging or labels on the packaging indicate this is an environmentally friendly product or is made from recycled or compostable materials as stated in the listing. Also, there's a ton of extra plastic as part of the packaging! Plastic film so you can see the case and a plastic shell the case sits in. All would go into a landfill. :-/ Update... I messaged Moko on Facebook and they provided their customer service email address. Their customer service was quite responsive and thorough about how they realize they have some more things to change to make this truly environmentally friendly. It is apparently their first eco product so I support their efforts! They did confirm the case itself is compostable and will have their product team address my suggestions of recycled packaging, no plastic in the packaging, have the packaging indicate the case is compostable and the materials used, etc.

I have to say this is the easiest, cleanest and clearest screen protector product I have ever used. The installation was a breeze with no need for any sprays or liquids that other "shield" products require. It took less than 5 seconds to install, and there were absolutely no bubbles under the film after putting it on. The film looks crystal clear and shiny! In fact, it's so shiny that it turns the screen into a mirror in sunlight and negates the camera screen's anti-glare coating. I had a very hard time using my camera outdoors with this protector on the screen. So, I've removed the protector, and I am now looking for an alternative product with better anti-glare properties.

UPDATE: I will say after writing this review, the company followed up 4 times to send me a new product which I thought was nice. I ended up not reaching out because 1) I don't use it that much and 2) I was lazy but the company is great and that warrants one more star in my book for trying to make it right. INITIAL REVIEW: I am actually a little unimpressed. It works half the time but I feel like I have issues with it the remainder of the time. I feel like the unit losses the charge if it just sits there for a week. It takes a long time to charge. Also, it will sometimes shut off randomly and doesn't charge my phone to the percentage it said it would. If you have a phone with a removable battery, I would suggest just getting a extra battery so you can take that as a backup.

Was a 5 star until it broke. I really liked this case until it broke today almost 10 months after I bought it. There is a clip, all plastic that has a spring loading. This clip holds it in the holster. It snapped and not the phone will not stay in the holster. I really liked this holster. The inner case is excellent and protect my phone from a dozen or more drops. On day 3, my phone started to get a bend, but with this case, there is no way the phone can bend. I am really bummed it broke and now must decide if I risk a second one (the devil I know) or risk a different one (the devil I don't know). :-(

I love the idea of this device - it is a great design which charges, provides audio out, holds my Galaxy S3 with a fairly bulky case, and folds up into a compact size for travel.That's why the inability to sync is heartbreaking. You can get others that do sync and charge, but they're bulky compared to this one. Some of them won't take a case and some will though it might be a very tight fit. I guess the problem is that this is designed as a Universal dock for many Samsung devices. Samsung doesn't make a dock just for their Premier and monster selling smartphone? Without a case, your S3 will rock and be unstable. However, if you don't need data transfer, this works well, with a case like the Puregear-Utilitarian-Silicone-Kickstand-Protector.

The case looks quite capable to protect the phone. The built in screen protector seems to work well (i.e. the phone responds by touch with it in the way). My main complaint is that the buttons (on/off, up & down volume) are very stiff. I don't think it would be possible to increase/decrease the volume of a call while you are holding it to your ear with a thumb click. You almost have to hold the phone in one hand and press to the point of pain with one of your fingers on your other hand. I don't think it will "loosen up" over time.

Update: The newer versions of this case no longer have magnets in the phone protector so I cannot recommend this purchase any longer and this is now like all the other wallet cases. Mediocre. TL:DR: This phone case has protected my phone flawlessly for 4 years and the wallet is absurdly bulky (so I don't even use it). But the magnetic case alone is worth it. Super strong magnet and extremely durable case. Originally I bought this wallet case to replace a previous one I had for my S6. One complaint I had about that one was that it was pretty bulky to have in my pockets, but I used to wear baggy clothes so it wasn't so bad. As I got older I wanted more fitted clothing so this became an issue, which is why having the detachable magnetic phone case was great. Eventually I found myself not even using the wallet and only using the magnetic case. I drop my phone all the time and this case has protected it flawlessly, but after 4 years I have no idea where the wallet is finally starting to degrade... so I'm gonna buy another one.

I was so excited when this band finally came. Unfortunately, I wasn’t as happy once I tried it on. It was easy to put on and easy to secure around my wrist. The bigger size was too big and the smaller it was too small so I ended up moving the knots a little bit to make it fit perfectly. I did end up sending it back though, because the beads would end up under the watch and the watch would lock thinking I wasn't wearing it so I wouldn't get notification. So I tried loosening it and then tightening it back up again hoping it would fix the problem, but it didn’t.

The product arrived on time and as described. The case fit my iPhone 4S perfectly. The screen cover was applied as the instructions indicated and fit perfectly. However, when removing the second sticker, the paper from the sticker separated from the adhesive, leaving a sticky residue on the screen saver. An adhesive remover was required to remove the residue. Despite attempts to keep the adhesive remover from wicking under the cover and onto the phone, the adhesive remover did just that. This required the cover to be lifted so that the screen could be cleaned. While cleaning the screen, tiny dust particles from the cleaning cloth transferred onto the screen cover, making it impossible to apply and use. I'll be asking for a replacement.

Ok, maybe it's my fault but it wasn't totally clear to me that the "fine ball pen for iPhone etc" was a REAL PEN. I spent ten minutes trying to write with it on my ipad... Thank god I didn't scratch it because I noticed something was obviously wrong before I could do any damages.... But still, I thought it was a little misleading. The other end is to thick. I'm gonna keep it because my fingers get tired of writing but my handwriting looks much prettier when I use my index finger instead.... And WHY ON EARTH do I need a real pen attached on the opposite end of the stylus? I've removed the ink and the pen ball already.... Lame!

Works just 'ok' in a 2013 Subaru Outback with an iPhone 6. I tried every combination with the three add on pads and with the unit right side up and then up side down. No matter what I choose, a small to medium tug would pull out the Koomus. One thing that I did not see what other reviews said was that the instructions said to "not have a CD" in the drive. This is no big deal to me as I hardly listen to the CD and normally listen to the radio or sometimes bluetooth pod casts to my radio.

I gave this a 4 because of some major flaws which are if you are a person like me who has short nails it's not such a good idea to get this case because the charger port takes some pretty long nails to open. Another flaw is you can't have your screen protector on. They give you a zagg optional screen protector but if you mess up it would probably be another 20$ for a new one. But all in all it has good signs like if you are not like me who likes to have screen protection then it's just perfect touching the glass on your phone. Also I got it in white on my gold 5s it look really nice because you can see the color.

I wanted to save the expense of buying a new phone, plus I really liked my 4 year old I phone 7, so I decided to replace the battery. Installation procedure was explained well, but it took me about 6 hours. I am 72, well educated, but my fingers are not nimble and the parts are small and fragile. The screws are super small and I needed a dish to keep them from getting lost and I needed a magnifier to see them. I used the magnifier througout the entire process. The hardest part was the removal of the old battery. The tool kit provided was not adequate because the plastic parts break easily. I was super careful and took my time and I didn't break anything in the process. It works well and holds a charge. After installation the battery health setting on my phone read 100%, which is great; however, I am not happy with the time I can use it per charge. I bought the high capacity and thought it would last longer. It didn't meet my expectations. I lowered the brightness to about 20%, and always closed the apps I wasn't using. I am not a gamer and use the phone primarily for a phone, text and news and I found I had to charge it at least twice, sometime 3 times per day.

I love everything about this case, the feel, the look, and the protection but have to dock off a few stars because it’s not that long lasting. I’ve had it for less than a month and the edges and corners are already yellow .. even the edges around the camera on the back as well .. so I’m super disappointed .. if it didn’t yellow so quickly this would’ve easily been a 5 stars review. now my phone case just looks dirty and old and I’ve had it for a year when I’ve had it for less than a month .

EDIT: The listing said "LTE bands 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 20, 28, 38, 40, 41 (120 MHz); (LATAM) 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 28". I trusted this and brought the phone to India, where it does not work on 4G. I then looked up the version number of this phone and it says TA-1391. I looked it up, and the only 4G bands supported are 2,4,5,7 and 41. Original review: This is a strange beast. It is not just the bezel; the USB connector is micro-USB, and new phones haven't used those in years. The back can be opened and the battery replaced---a good thing in principle, but also adds to the impression that this is an old phone. The listing currently says the OS is Android 11, but in fact it is Android 11 Go, a lite version designed for phones with only 2GB of RAM. This also indicates an old design, what new phone has only 2GB RAM? Another 2GB would cost, what, $5 more? Incidentally, it is an import from Latin America somewhere and does not have a warranty.

This was easy to install and had great anti glare and touch capability. The first sheet was on my phone for over 2 years with just minor surface scratches. I was giving my phone to someone else, so I was putting on new glass. The new piece of glass was horrible - nothing like my first experience. It installed easily but the touch capability was off - I felt like I was punching the screen to get it to respond. For the first time ever, I dropped my phone - but it was on the carpet and it bounced onto the tile - the entire glass protection screen shattered. So thankful it wasn't the phone screen - but there was no way this should have shattered with the tiny hit on the tile - it was like it rolled onto the tile - not a 5 foot drop direct hit. Very disappointed. I bought a new one but haven't needed it - so I don't know if the second sheet was just defective or if the product quality has declined.

The case fits fine on the phone and seems more like a style choice than a durable phone protection case. That's ok because I sort of knew that this case was more about looks than protection from dings or drops. It's the color of the case that is the problem. The description and photo shows a red color case but when I received the item it looks way more pink than red. The rubber like edges are light colored all around the outline of the case and the art work it's self has a mix between pink and light red tones. Just a heads up to anyone planning to purchase this case. If your looking for a pink looking case then this one is for you.

I like the case, it covers my new Nexus 5X phone very well. Have full access to all of the buttons and plugins. Like the raised sides and battleship corners that allow you to place the phone face-side down without harming the screen. Like the dimples on the inside of case which avoid the 'oily' look exhibited by other clear plastic cases without this feature. My only issue with the case is that the clear plastic backside has cloudy spots..mainly around the cut-outs. I tried washing the case with a mild soap and water to no avail.I tried rubbing the cloudy spots with my fingers and it helped a little but still there. I wrote to the Ballistic company support about the problem but got no response. So I'm deducting one star, perhaps it's a one-off defective product since no one else is complaining. I will continue to use the case until I find something I like better.

Just purchased this to try in my 2003 Tundra with a Pioneer Avic700 head unit. Bottom line - the device fits into the cd slot but has absolutely zero holding-strength. It readily, and with almost no force, pulls directly out of the cd slot, and it utterly useless in my particular application. I'm giving this device 2-stars, because it is certainly possibly that my configuration just won't work with this device, and it may work fine with other vehicles/configurations. That being said, I will be "gifting" this thing to a friend to try in her car - I will post the results here.

The case was good, I would not complain but some people do count on the stand and the stand wasn't so good. So for them I'm giving 4 stars in case they are going to be relying on the stand. The phone is held in the case with an adhesive strip about half the size of the phone, you put the rubbery case on the phone and stick the case on the adhesive, that's where the problem comes in with the stand. If you try using the stand it is flimsy and the adhesive begins to pull, if left there long it may have dropped the phone off. I wasn't going to be using the stand as I have a device that I put the phone case in to hold it. I have to turn this case where the back meets the front then it sits in my stand well, that's why I was reasonably satisfied with the case. Thé color was a nice bright pink, I was impressed with that as that is favorite color and the case felt rather sturdy, the magnets held well, the case and the phone lined up perfectly for the controls on the phone. What I did was reinforced the phone on to the case by laying a strip of two faced tape on the back of the rubbery case and stuck it down on the pink case for better hold, then I had no problems at all, if I was to need another one I wouldn't hesitate to order one.

It's OK. Lots of thick TPU on the back and top/bottom. That should provide good protection there, but it makes the phone a bit heavy. Not much protection on the edges; makes me think the phone might not survive a drop there. The case is easy to grip, but that's only due to lots of sharp edges and the 4 feet on the corners. I prefer a more contoured feel with grippy material. My biggest complaint is despite the extra weight and bulk, it does not seem to add much protection on the sides. I might have to look at Otterbox.

So I've had Solar chargers before and I though hey that's a great price for these, I recently went camping had them fully charged before I left used one per night just to charge my phone (I ordered two) next day I put the one that was already dead from charging my phone out in the sun it sat there all day in direct sun did not charge at all, I continue to let it sit there all night and the next day because I had to so then I put the second one out there and figured OK this one should be charged now at least a little bit didn't charge at all, very disappointed in the product like I said I've had solar chargers before never had an issue

I ordered these for my son's and my phone. We have used SuperSheilds before for our previous phones Samsung J3 and liked them. These, however, have popped off, 2x on my son's phone and once with mine. Not sure if that's because they have the curved edges. Now there is fine particles underneath, so my screen never looks clean. My son's cracked and shattered just a month after putting it on. Which I know is what it's supposed to do, instead of your phone screen. There is a micro grid pattern within the glass, not sure what the purpose of it is, but when the light shines on it just right it is hard to see the screen because of this. Not thrilled with these. Will be looking for something else to replace my son's .

The cover is good. It does what it is supposed to do, protect the phone. Instructions would be helpful, there are none with the phone. The belt clip was snug, which I assumed was good. I really didn't want the phone to detach. I got the case on Thursday and Saturday was the first chance I had to use it. I worked fine until the end of the day when the phone seemed a little loose in the clip. I then realized that the plastic snap that holds the phone in the clip had broken. Not very strong. I am now using a leather belt holder with the cover. That works

Pros: Overall this is a sturdy item, though the bezel around the screen protector on mine has come apart. Cons: 1) The screen protector is cheap plastic that isn't fully transparent nor does it adequately convey touches to the phone touch screen. I replaced the plastic with a glass protector. 2) In order to lock or unlock the phone, you have to either unclip the outer shield from the inner shield, taking several seconds, or cut a hole in the outer shield. 3) the button for the volume control isn't very sensitive. 4) In order to remove the micro SD card, you have to either remove both the outer and inner cases, or cut another hole. (I haven't tried the last one yet, so I'm not sure it will work).

I purchased this to power the Garmin 705 on events that last over 8 hours. It is a shame that the Garmin battery is SO WEAK! On the first event a 400K rondo I used velcro to strap this to the bars next to the Garmin. This is shiped with a VERY short cable so I lost a lot of handelbar space. With just one battery the garmin kept running however it did not have enought power to charge the Garmin while it was in use. For my next event a 600K rondo I purchased the Enegizer with two batteries. This did a little better at leting the Garmin run and get charged at the same time. The Energizer also had a short cable so I need to get something else worked out to handle the short cable issue. It is a shame that Garmin can not come up with a product to deal with this issue. I have see one other person with a dynmo front hub do a power take off and run this through some type of converter and into the Garmin and NEVER lose power even when they are runing the night lights.

I liked the SUPCASE for the 5S. I'm not a fan of the case they have come up with for the 6S. My complaints: 1) No raised buttons for power and volume make it very hard to know if you are pressing in the right location. You have to run your thumb or fingernail along the case to detect the groove that demarcates the beginning of the button area. 2) The rubber is very hard and thick over the buttons, making them hard to press when you do find them. The location of the power button on the 6S, directly across from the VOL ^ button, means that as you squeeze the phone to turn it on or off, more often than not you raise the volume instead. 3) The hole over the headphone jack is too small to fit most headphone plugs. Only my Sennheiser headphones have a long, skinny plug that will work in this port. 4) The clear back is an interesting idea, but dirt and lint make their way inside and show up against the light color of the phone.

I truly love the look but there is a major problem with this case and all other cases that are being made for the Surface Duos through third parties and that is you can not fold your surface duo in phone mode due to the cases Even if you took one off and try and fold your phone all the way around it will not allow it, Cases for the Surface Duos needs to be re made so that it stops at least 1 inch before reaching the end of the phone and not right on the bevels that way you can fully FOLD the phone.

I'm actually impressed. I expected something pretty cheap for the price. It's actually pretty similar to my husband's otterbox. It even feels the same. It doesn't have the tempered glass front that the otterbox did but that's okay by me as we even popped that out of my husband's because it made typing horrible on his phone. This case does at some weight to the phone and took a tiny bit of patience putting it together but all in all I'm impressed. The screen sits back from the case enough to protect it in a fall but it doesn't bother the edge feature on my s7 edge. UPDATE: ABOUT TWO MONTHS LATER! The rubber casing is coming off way too easily. It almost always comes off when I take it off the belt clip now and actually prevented my phone from buckling into the clip well a few days ago. Causing it to fall off the clip. Luckily no damage. The rubber is also ripping in the area around where the clip holds. I also had an issue with the case bothering my screen. I had to remove the case when my phone started hanging up on calls without me doing anything. Quickly realized it was the case causing the problem. Hasn't happened since I removed the case, cleaned it and the phone then put it back together. The biggest reason I lowered the rating is the rubber piece has made it where my buttons are near impossible to press. I have to fiddle and adjust the case just to turn my volume up and down. I've ordered a new case and am kicking this one to the curb. It was decent for a short time but didn't get the life out of it that I wanted.

--Updated Review-- After 2 days, many of the bubbles and "cloudy" appearance have gone away. So, I've upped my review to 3 stars from one because now I won't be ripping this thing off my phone as soon as my new screen protector arrives. It looks much better now and seems as good as any "normal non-liquid installed screen protector". However, I still believe that whatever the benefits of this screen protector may be, they are not at all worth the complex, messy, liquid spray based install process, nor the lengthy wait time to have the screen become clear and bubble free. --Original Review-- The fact that you have to spray liquid on this to install it is insane. I've forgotten this (they don't mention the overly complicated liquid based install procedure on the box) and bought more than one of these only to find that when I open the box it has a spray bottle and 5 step process to install, and when done it looks bubbly and terrible. I've used so many screen protectors over the years and this is the only one that requires you to spray it down with magic "adhesive" liquid to install. SUUUUUCKS!!

The lighting and whatnot is cool, even if you can't change the logo or pattern, but the case itself is not really protective. The accessories I have fit fine with it on (twinview dock and aircooler). The right side is very vunerable, however. You definitely should have a screen protector if you want to use it. Fortunately, I had one. It also randomly came off once when it was in my pocket; Not sure what that was about. I am purchasing another full plexi case for daily use, and will just have to remove it to use accessories as needed until something better comes along. If you don't have large hands and can't easily grip it with one hand securely whilst still being able to use it, I'd suggest something more protective.

While I originally really liked the way this stand worked, but over the past six months it has become less and less useful. I've cleaned both the stand and the phone (iPhone 5S) multiple times, and pressed the phone hard against the stand to get it to stick, but haven't had any luck. The phone will always detatch and either drop off the stand or slide slightly forward on the base. I've had to rely on leaning it on the base, but even that doesn't work all that well as the plastic on the foot simply allows the bottom of the phone to slide forward, possibly allowing the phone to slip off the base altogether. Perhaps if they had put a rubberized bumper there it would be more useful. Needless to say, the stand sticks to my desk without question, but since I never move it, the suction has not weakened. I appreciate the design, asthetic, and concept, but have been less than impressed with the product in use.

I have had the blackberry passport for about 3-1/2 weeks. I Decided to give Blackberry a try coming from a iPhone 4s and tired of iPhone and android phones there all the same plus I used to love my curve back in 2010-11. I loved the design of this phone it's different than anything else on the market and it definitely turned some heads. But I'm speaking in past tense because I am returning the phone to Amazon due to a few issues that I can't live with. 1 and this is the biggest problem I don't have access to most of the apps that I need for my everyday life like It doesn't have a app for my bank, my credit card, or my brokerage firm. These are things that I check numerous times throughout the day and without the app it's a real pain. I wasn't even bothered about the lack of gaming apps because I knew that before I bought it plus I don't even play games 2. For some reason I can't watch videos on the Internet not even YouTube or Instagram videos. I found myself still using my iPhone 4 everyday. I just feel like i would be comprising too much just to have a different looking phone not to mention having to switch to AT&T from Verizon and them messing my plan up and not having internet outside of wifi even though it was in my plan. So today I went back to Verizon and bought a iPhone 6 plus and I was instantly relieved. This would be a great phone if it weren't for these few issues.

First of all this is a very very heavy charger. It is not one that you would want to carry in your purse or bag. It is mainly for keeping at home I may be in your car but not for carrying around because of its weight. Once it’s fully charged it does charge your items very well. I took my iPhone from 10% to 100% in about 45 minutes. And still had two bars of charging left on the charger. Good things about this charger is that it has a built-in flashlight it has two regular USB ports and it also has ports for a fast charger an android type charger. The bad thing about this is once you let this charger get down to one bar or to the point where it needs to be recharged. It takes 8 to 10 hours to recharge it which is crazy.

It’s rather disappointing that a lot of the screen replacements are for the wrong phone—this one luckily was the correct replacement (this had the correct number of cables, the other is for 6S and only has two cables, do a quick search and see how many are incorrectly labeled! My complaint is that seller states you can simply change out the home button with your Touch ID button from the previous screen. I’m here to say that the Touch ID will still not work. Otherwise the button works, but you get a message that Touch ID can not be initialized after reboot. That was disappointing, especially when the seller states it should work.

I really needed to keep a better eye on my air pressure. It was 62 overnight and 105 today so being able to not only keep an eye on my pressure but also the temperature of my tires is critical. These do both. And alert me when my pressure is off by too much. Money well spent. Only thing is I wish they came in chrome. Like most Harley owners, I'm pretty fastidious about what I put on my bike and how it looks. But until they come out with chrome, the silver ones look fine and may just save my butt someday. UPDATE: After 6 months one sensor died. We'll see how they're customer support is
