Doesn't cover the phone completely flush so it wouldn't register touches on the side where the screen curves. Kickstand broke as the plastic piece that keeps it from opening completely is too thin including the nubs that keep it in place. Should have gone with the supcase as the one I used for my S7 worked flawlessly. I just had to cut the cheap plastic screen protector out.

You get what you pay for. These are very flimsy and break often. It has always protected my screen but I actually haven’t saved money buying these. They are cheap flemones wise but produce wise as well. For nearly all 7 times I have had to replace these, it’s simply because my keys and phone are in the same pocket and some sort of pressure is applied over the pocket. They break that easily. I’m going to buy a more expensive protector in the hopes it will last longer than these do and hopefully save money *over time* and not have to replace every 2 months. Remember: buying cheap things is often more expensive in the long term. This is a lesson that I have re-learned buying this brand.

This screen protector is great, it cover the screen quite well, and is case friendly. The only problem is that is not a hybrid, it's just a thick normal screen protector. I say this due to my experience from my vacation. Someone was taking pictures with my phone near a beach, the person had multiple phones and hands somewhat dirty. This person scratch and bubbled the screen protector. That's why I said is not a hybrid glass, it just got scratch like a regular plastic screen protector. A glass protector wouldn't scratch that easy. Had to reorder this product. Anyway, the installation of the screen protector is quite easy due to a plastic handle that goes into the charging port, making the screen stay on the right places. The only downside is that when you lift the second plastic, lifts the screen protector and it bubbles again - so I suggest taking it off first, then the first plastic and place it on the screen. Again, great screen protector - better than other brands, but still misleading. Just take care of the screen protector.

It's not terrible, it's not great, either. I wouldn't feel bad if this thing was knocked around while I was at work, but that's only because it feels like it's made out of cheap plastic. there's no way that this battery is 24000 mAh, it's more around 10,000. that's still decent, but if that's what I was looking for then i'd go with something else. I've got a few portable chargers, and this one is my least favorite. the light that it comes with is basically useless. mine also buzzes when I charge it via micro USB, but not when I use a lightning cable. I'll probably return this.

I purchased these headsets since I am working remotely. The first day I got them, they paired and worked great. Then after a few days I started having problems with the sound and mic on the headsets working with my Skype client. I uninstalled and paired multiple times along with rebooting laptop and trying any and every configuration on my laptop and Skype client as far as sound and audio settings. Nothing worked. One thing I noticed when you pair this headset is that you get two Bluetooth accounts/options--one for stereo and one without. Depending on which one you choose will yield different settings and experiences. After trying to work with this headset for three days, I finally gave up and will be returning them for a refund. Too frustrating to continue on so I'm throwing in the towel. Pros to this headset is that it's very cute, but does have a little weight to it since all the controls are on the headset as well. It does pair nicely with two devices at the same time and the sound quality is spot on. Other than that, you may experience some technical difficulties like I did so just be prepared. Lastly the instructions for the headset is basically one page paragraph with no additional help for technical difficulties.

Over all, this is a pretty great product. The QR code for the warranty does not work but given the price, it would be better to buy a new one if you have problems like the one below. The only complaint I have is that I wish the ball joint holding the magnet was a bit stronger. I noticed that my phone started to hang lower than normal after several months of use. I'm sure that is due to the Florida temperature being well over the 100 degree index over the summer but this is still a issue that needs to be addressed and could be improved.

My daughter has destroyed two Otterbox Commuters because she can't stop fiddling with the headphone and charger covers and eventually the rubber rips clean off. We're trying this one out as an alternative. The buttons are easier to press than when the phone is in the Otterbox and there is no rubber covering the headphone jack or the charger port, but I haven't found that to be a problem. It's not like the Commuter case was at all waterproof. She tends to drop her phone a lot and so far this one has held up well. We'll see how it lasts over time.

Shout out to those who got through with the adjustments. The directions are so bad. Not enough details for people who are doing this the first time. They give a lot of replacement screws because the screws will get bent because the arrows on the directions are confusing..and you end up screwing a pin through the wrong side. Get the directions right and you wouldn’t need spares. I ended up figuring it out but I went through all the spares and punctured my index as well…don’t ask. The design looks good but i can already tell the paint won’t last long. I already have some small chips that came off.

The headset is comfortable and easily fits everything from a small child to a large adult head. The microphone piece appears durable and sturdy. However, the headset only syncs with our phones for call audio. The description and photos lead one to belive that the headset will work with media audio but on 2 Android phones that is not the case. Perhaps it's just an error on the website but without media audio I have no desire for such a product. The packaging and unboxing were very good quality as are the laminated instructions. Another disappointing issue though is that the description says it charges via micro USB but the included cable and receptacle are mini USB, which is discouraging since most devices use micro USB.

I wanted to love it. It’s bright, slim, shows the back of the iPhone through the clear back. The texture of the plastic rubberized sides is pleasant and doesn’t feel cheap. But the feel of the side button is just light years behind that of the volume buttons. The volume buttons are pleasantly clicky. The side button doesn’t click, has a super shallow travel range, and requires way too much force to actuate. I removed and reinserted the phone a few times to see if I could “clear the error”. It improved slightly sometimes, but was bad other times. Something about the fit on the right just isn’t correct vs. the fit on the left. It’s my first Otterbox case, and given the brand reputation I was hoping for better.

The Plantronics Voyager Legend Wireless Bluetooth Headset is a great headset for anyone who is looking to enjoy a wireless, hands-free phone experience. This headset offers excellent sound quality both in my ear and from talking to people on the other end of the phone conversation. It also blocks wind noise out of a conversation better than the phone itself does. But that is not all it does. This headset allows music to be played through it as well, allowing for hands-free music enjoyment for hours on end. The battery life for this headset is around five hours of constant use, but it only takes about thirty minutes for a full recharge. This makes it easy to use, easily allowing for full use of this product all day long with issue or constraint. The headset sits comfortably on the ear. It so comfortably on my ear, that I have forgotten that I even had it on until someone called me and it announced the caller through the headset. This is yet another one of the awesome features that come with this headset. My only complaint is that my Bluetooth headset will randomly disconnect from my phone without warning at times which can be incredibly frustrating while in the middle of a conversation. It does not happen very often but it does happen, which is worrisome. Otherwise a great product.

can't hear even with volume up, sounds fades. Getting to the net is so expensive and time consuming it is really useless, so can the one feature I spent extra for. I got it for $27 so it is OK for a low level cell, but I wish I did not lose my cheap little $20 clamshell. BTW, Tracfone is notorious for really poor customer support, the kind you just want to reach though the phone line and slap the Cust Support person. Well, it has gotten worse. This phone replaces a phone that I got to replace clammy. The second phone never actually successfully made more that 4 calls - rather than trying to understand what I was asking, customer support suggested I throw it out and get a new phone. Several times in a row, like a robot. Before I actually turned it on. Tracfone is cheap and reliable, but this will be my last trac phone, just based on the customer support.

I have this phone. The GPS is terrible. Some people think it's a 1920x1080 (also known as 1080p) screen. It isn't. It's a 1280x720 (also known as 720p) screen. This isn't a problem for me though. I don't use it for movies, TV shows, YouTube, etc. The wi-fi will turn on automatically and take over your screen even if you manually shut it off. The sound output from the headphone jack is terribly low even if you use a volume booster app. I can't drown out the cheesy "Top 40" dance music when I'm at the gym, which means bringing my old school chocolate-colored 30GB Microsoft Zune (first gen - what?!) to the gym instead. That thing will drown out a tornado with the right earbuds.

I read the reviews that the instructions weren't good so I was prepared for that. YouTube provided all the instructions needed but this was still not something I would recommend doing on your own. Getting the glue off of your lcd is a very difficult and delicate process and the kit doesn't come with adequate glue removal supplies. Once we finally got the glue off, the lcd was ruined in a few spots. We went ahead and put it all together anyways until we could get a new lcd and the glass cracked with the slightest pressure. It's only $8 but in the process we wrecked my lcd so we ended up paying to get it all replaced anyways. At least the screwdrivers fit.

Very sturdy case. It looks just like it's pictured. I got the gold one to go with my gold note 5 answer it looks great. A little difficult to put on but if you keep both pieces together than it will go on easier. It doesn't muffle calls and definitely makes your phone feel more protected. The texture on the case makes it easier to hold do. Adds a tiny bit of bulk to the phone, but not anything like an otter box case. Camera is protected as well and the case doesn't attract finger prints. Definitely worth buying. It came quickly and was an easy purchas. Thank you 2/26 update After using this case for a few days, I've noticed a spot on the corner over the spen that is sharp and I can't seem to make it go away without damaging the case. It hurts my hand when I have to put it over that spot. I'm looking into buying a backup case for when I can't handle it anymore.

I liked the phone case EXCEPT I requested pink but they gave my purple and blue color. The texture of the phone case that I received seemed to be entirely different than what the phone case looked in the pictures (I thought that it would have a soft texture but what I got was a phone cover that had a bumpy and rough texture). If I had to be extremely finicky, another contrasting online phone case appearance from what I had received is that line you see on the front of the phone case (the one where there's supposed to be a hole so you can hear your calls). What I got instead were these horizontal holes that looked a bit cheaply punched through by a bit smaller-than-average hole puncher. The only redeeming quality is that it does its job as in it works as a phone cover that can fit my phone and has been designed so I can conveniently place cards and money in it.

I'm wondering what Samsung Galaxy S2 was used in coming up with the design for this case because it must be a different one from the S2 my sister has! The cut-outs for the keys & ports around the phone are only SOMEWHAT aligned with the keys they're supposed to allow access to. I gave it 2 stars because the case itself is very pretty & served its aesthetic purpose well. She's 11 & LOVED being able to bling out her phone with this case. However half of her power button & volume keys are blocked & the hole for the earphones jack is too much to the right. I suggest that the manufacturers revisit their calculations & make the small tweaks required to put out what would otherwise be a really decent product (I have no quality complaints otherwise).

The case is in two pieces: one hard plastic and one rubber. I found that it works best to install the flexible rubber one first, then work one side of the hard plastic on and then the other. Not easy to do. The two-part case makes the phone bulkier, but the advantage is that the phone then becomes less slippery and not as prone to dropping. As far as the static cling screen protector is concerned, getting it on without bubbles or air spaces is near impossible. You only get one good shot at it and if it is not absolutely perfect, you have wasted the screen protector. The glass on the phone is quite hard, so a protector may not even be necessary. One more note after using the case for awhile: The rubber buttons covering the on/off and the volume control switches protrude more, making it very easy to hit either button by mistake. Very annoying!

I saw reviews about these cases getting dirty fast and ignored it, because I thought it wouldn't be that bad. I was wrong. I even got the pinky/orange because I was hoping it would hide dirt better, but it doesn't. I've had this for a month and a half and it is already dirty and looks awful. Magic erasers, which I think can clean almost anything, didn't do a thing here. It's also surprisingly slippery. Sometimes I'll set it on the arm of my couch, and like 2 minutes later it slips off onto the floor. I was surprised because I thought my last case was this material, but I compared the two and this is definitely different. My old one feels much more grippy like silicone, and this one feels closer to plastic. I get that this isn't that expensive, but I'd recommend looking elsewhere if you don't want your phone case looking old after like a month.

UPDATED ---- I think this is one of the best phone protectors. Highly improved since Galaxy Note9 version that I also own. Very sturdy and great inside shock protection. - BUT they did not implement three IMPORTAN features: 1- NO Camera protection via a Sliding Door (which is GREAT and EXTREMELY useful in other phone cases that I also own, giving you peace of mind) 2- No SIM Tray cut out, especially useful for Dual-Sim phones (I requested that 4 years ago...) 3- No hole to attach a lanyard. VERY helpful for many users. This would help preventing drops, theft, etc. I worked around this doing myself, but should be considered by manufacturers! Especially for such expendio smartphone. IF manufacturers implement the Sliding Door to protect the (extremely expensive) cameras on this phone, then it would be almost PERFECT.

Update- Not even a month later and the screen protector cracked. I didn't expect it to last long but I expected more than a few weeks out of it. Had it not cracked I would have taken it off soon anyway. So much dirt got underneath it and would have scratched the screen. It is a 2 pack but I didn't even put the second one on. Pros- This is a thick screen protector so I think it would be difficult for scratches to reach the screen. It is truly clear and doesn't make the screen look blurry. Also, there are 2 protectors and they fit the phone perfectly. Cons- You have to tap the screen harder than normal for the phone to recognize the touches. Also, the adhesive that holds it on is only around the edges. This is common on new screen protectors but causes it not to adhere as soon. Dirt gets trapped in between the phone and the protector. I can tell I will have to change it within a few months as there is no way to clean this area. I cleaned the area before applying it and the phone was new out of the box. This is just dirt that gets trapped. In addition, the alchohol pads it came with were dry. I just poured a little rubbing alcohol on them. Overall, they are a good price and work well. If you plan to have one long term without changing it, this likely wouldn't be the best one. If you need something good at a great price but don't mind changing it after a few months, this will work.

Bought for my "senior" monther-in-law - her first Smartphone. Was able to root very easily and so far she likes the phone. Even though it is Tracfone you do get Verizon signal and coverage. One note - you will be in a world of hurt if you activate the phone, play with it, and then transfer a number over from another carrier. I was on with Tracfone for 3 hours trying to get the number ported over. You should instead activate and port at the same time - but that can be a gamble if you're using this as a way of saving money by switching from another carrier and want to make sure the phone is "right" before taking the plunge.

I give these little guys three stars because they do protect your screen from all kinds of danger. These selfless warriors, however, are themselves as weak as young barley. My first stalwart soldier bit the dust protecting my phone from a paperback cookbook as it careened recklessly from a height of two inches, striking my oblivious phone without mercy. The second perished as I was in the heat of a peekaboo war with a four month old ninja when my wedding band dealt my phone a half-hearted backhand as it passed. In summation, three stars to these little fighters for going above and beyond their call of duty and keeping my phone pristine, but minus two stars for their fanatical propensity for self sacrifice.

So this thing sounds pretty good, despite the issue of them only including one ear pad that is so small I doubt it would fit into a baby's ear. That's probably my biggest gripe with this earpiece. It doesn't fit normal earpads, so there's nothing you can do about this. I believe this earpiece would be mind-blowingly good if it fit properly. Here are some quick pros and cons about this earpiece... CONS: - the battery is borked. It can only ever charge up to 90% no matter what.. - It doesn't come with a USB charger so having to put it in its battery case all the time is really lame. - Alert prompts are SUPER LOUD. This thing is terrifying when you're using it to listen to stuff while falling asleep. I would recommend powering this thing on BEFORE you put it in your ear. And be conscious of when the power is low or it'll scream at you. - the lights are super bright when they flash. It doesn't happen constantly, but is very visible, even when you're wearing it! - They really REALLY need to give you different sized pads. The one that comes with is so small that it just falls out of my ear in most cases. It would also help with sound. PROS: - Its sounds is pretty decent, even with the ill-fitting earpad. I can only assume it would sound fan-freakin-tastic if they included pads that actually fit. - the battery, although being crap, lasts a really really long time on a single charge. Somewhere in the range of 5-7 hours depending on use. The charger itself can hold enough power for about 3-1/2 full charges.

I actually bought 2 of these one red and one blue. I had one previously had one and loved it! The quality on the new ones don't compare. I bought the blue one for my Mom and the red one for me. I can't understand most if what she says its muffled and she has to pair it 4-6 times a week because it unpairs itself. It does not stay on, on standby it shuts itself off. So everytime she gets a phone call you have to go back through the connecting mode and half of the time you have to re-pair it. At first I thought she was having these issues because she's getting older, but I switched hers and mine out. Then I started trying to use mine and am having the same problems so its been very frustrating and quite frankly a real waste of money and time. Like I stated I had one that I lost that I loved and it worked great for about 4 years. I lost it once in October and in July of the next year my Dad had found it in the garden, we charged it and turned it on and it was still paired to my phone! I used it for another year before losing it on a motorcycle trip. I was readjusting it in my helmet and it flipped out of my hand on the highway doing about 65 miles an hour. I never got the chance to find it again! So sad that these 2 don't work.

The wallet flap is the stand and doesn’t hold phone for long. Need to use my tablet stand instead. Wallet has lots of slots but with my limited hand strength it’s very hard to pull cards in and out and I only have 2 cards in it. I do like having my DL and Credit Card with me and manage. Cards are definitely held tight for safety. Leather, magnet and snap work well. When I drop my phone it’s safe and cards stay in. Overall I like it and would recommend so long as you don’t want to use their so called stand feature that doesn’t support the weight of the phone.

I originally got this so I could keep my phone, room key, and ID together and it did just that. I love how I can choose to either have my phone in the wallet or just in my pocket without having to physically take it out of the case. The magnets are really strong and reliable. The only reason this doesn't have 5 stats is because the gold detail on the phone case wore off and the spine of the wallet is cracked and worn. This would be understandable if my wallet ever got full but aside from a few cards and receipts there's barley anything ever in it.

I liked the program after I figured out how to download the section of the map into my Garmin. There is no instruction manual with the program!!! I guess they think everyone is a geek. I had to call Garmin to get help. After going through about 10 levels of Voice Mail, I got a LIVE VOICE. I have gone hiking twice. It is difficult to show the area that we are walking and to make the trails with breadcrumbs so we can get back home. The main reason I purchased the program was to able to walk trails and NOT get lost and to justify my Garmin 60CSx which is about $350!! I can use an automobile GPS with about as much accuracy. Anyone help? E-Mail is gene_cline .net

This kit is what you need to fix your iPhone. But please use caution and be ready to take some time (up to 3 hours). The parts in an iPhone are super small, so please have a large area to work and safe place to keep the screws while you are working. A magnetic pad or double-sided tape will work to hold the screws and keep track of what you are doing and what screws go with each step, as they vary in size. You can save some money doing it yourself, but if you are not 100% committed, let a professional do it, you'll just screw up your iPhone even worse and be forced to buy a new one.

I have a contract with Sprint and got the Pal Pixi. I have gone through 5 of these phones(screen won't scroll, 2 times the plastice backing melted tot he phone, volumn control button got stuck, and it's won't connect to my bluebooth), each time I have trouble I take it back to Sprint and they replace it with the same phone. This phone dails on its on, the screen scrolls w/o touching it, it get too hot, it'll dail back the last number called w/o me touching the phone, if I dare to watch TV or any program, it drains the battery, and let's not even talk about what listening to music does to the battery. Recently during less than normal usage only phn calls), I went to a dance class came out and the battery was drained, thank goodness I had the car charger handy. I positively hate this phone, and so does my sister who got the same phone when we activated our plans with Sprint, so much so that she eventually went back to a blackberry.

I like this item for protecting my phones screen. It is not scratch proof like the glass one I had on my LG G4, but apparently there are no glass ones for this phone. This DOES protect the phone from scratches. I am also frequently dropping my phone so I need to protect it as much as possible. So far it has done that. While the glass screen protector never scratched, it did crack when I dropped my phone once, it kept the screen from cracking though so I was so glad I had it on. 12/4/16 Update: This DID NOT protect my screen from breaking when I dropped my phone. The one I had on my LGG4 DID protect my screen from breaking when dropped. That one was glass and seemed to make the difference.

I loved this case when I first got it but like many of the other reviewers, one drop and the hard plastic sides cracked. Once those crack, the overall rigidity of the case is compromised and at this point it's just on as a courtesy. These cases are great. If you absolutely never whoopsies your phone you'll be fine. But if you even drop it once it's highly likely the side will crack. Stinks, I really liked this case. Due to the squared edges my ProClip phone mount really grips the phone even when I'm off road bouncing on rocks it doesn't fall out like a lot of cases, especially with rounded edges.

Edit: After 2 months, the kickstand broke. The kickstand was only used 8-10 times in that period. The issue with it is that the kickstand 'pins' are plastic and the opening the stand after ~10 times or so broke those pins that hold it in place. If you do not use the kickstand, this case is still good. However, if you need a kickstand for the phone this one will not last. :( Original Review: Overall, this is a really nice case! Only issue is that there is no protection on the front top and bottom areas. It fits tightly into the "holster" enclosure and that enclosure swivels when on the belt, making adjusting it nice and comfortable. The back is non-slippery but has too much of a "nail file" feel to it, but it is still better than the slippery S7 on its own. Overall, this is a good price for a good item.

Loved the old version with the solid back. Not a fan of the "kick stand" that lets dirt in. It NEEDS a glass screen protector, or the case needs to be sized so I can get a "case friendly" glass screen protector that fits. I've ordered 3 and had to send them back since they don't fit with the case. OR the screen protector that is available on the Galaxy s21 and the ultra, needs to be available for the plus. I want a case that also protects the screen and this doesn't seem to be it. The vinyl screen protector that comes on the phone, does not stay on with this case. The company doesn't seem to care that there is no screen protector for this case.

Very good while it lasts, but ports are unfortunately fragile. Tiny brittle plastic bits support the cable ports and they break with little warning and render the otherwise quality device completely useless. Don't let the solid weight and feel fool you into thinking it's high quality or that it will tolerate any amount of careless handling. As long as you baby the device and treat every plug-in event like a careful process, it might be worth it. I might still get another one if I can't find another product worth trying in the same price range. It worked as advertised and for a low cost. It just rankles that I only used it for infrequent backup charges, so I got maybe three charges out of it before it broke. It would hurt more if it weren't so cheap. Edit: Attached photo of the failed part. The bit that should go into the micro USB cable had no support behind it and only two tiny legs beneath it holding it to the board. The first time it doesn't align correctly, it'll snap with normal pressure from trying to plug in the cable.

I've owned the Strada case for the Galaxy S7 Edge and the S9+. Each generation seems to get a little worse. Past cases were made of multiple materials to improve drop protection including a hard plastic frame/back with soft plastic edges. The current version seems to be just TPU. Also, the amount that the front edge of the case rises above the surface of the screen is minimal proving less protection than previous versions. Another problem is that the back of the case is essentially flush with the camera bump. The leather wrapping does increase the thickness of the back a little so that the camera will not touch when placed on a flat surface. However, I am suspicious of the drop protection that would be provided to the camera bump and the potential for scratching when placed on anything that isn't perfectly flat. Finally, as others have said, the small tab with a magnet that was used to keep the cover closed has been replaced with a flush cover using a stronger magnet. It is therefore harder to open (no tab to grab), does not stay closed as well (no magnet to metal contact), and is much too hard to close when the cover is folded back (due very strong magnet in the middle of the cover adhering to metal in the back of the case). I understand that Otterbox is trying to cut costs and limit thickness of the case. I think that it will still provide adequate protection but they are obviously cutting quality, and this version seems clearly inferior to the previous versions.

I had forgotten how lost the sound quality on this phone was. And the touch screen is almost non responsive with no way to adjust the sensitivity. But I do like that it has an unlocked bootloader so rooting took literally less than 5 minutes. So I am sure I can just research some scripts to run to adjust the two abovementioned problems. Love my Skyrocket. Wish Samsung didn't have to go all "prude" and lock down their bootloader with the new s5 Lollipop update. BOO!! Oh well, i'll just wait for another to crack the next one. Til then, duck you Samsung from my s5

Well, I have had this case a week and I am already buying another one. The red "gloss" is not really that glossy and the back cover design is barely noticeable. Moreover, the case looks cheap and the mirror cover gets fingerprints all over it as well as becomes impossible to ready in the sunlight! Now, the case does a pretty good job of protecting everything as well as provides a smooth fit. I decided I should just get a clear case to show off the zen appeal of the iPhone rather than have my phone be called a "cheap prostitute" again.

This does not work for messages--neither SMS nor What's App. Not at all!...because it does not vibrate long enough to trigger it, even when choosing the longest ringers. But it works GREAT for being a loud ringer that I can hear everywhere in the house--which is mostly what I wanted it for. And it is SUPER easy to use and keep on using. You can adjust the sound from off to low to high. High is super loud! Only problem is that I want it on the kitchen counter near the sink, but the vibration of the garbage disposal sets it off like crazy!!!!!

This case is has been one I've been debating getting for awhile, while I was on iOS 6 I got to the point where it was having considerably shorter battery life (usually got down to 30% by the time I was leaving work even on some 6 hour days and this wasn't even if I made calls... This got somewhat better when I got a clean install with iOS 7, so it probably was some location intensive apps and push apps but still I was looking for a way to extend the life some more of the battery, after installing this case I noticed right away how it put the phone into charging mode when switched on, I find the case itself hasn't even really been fully used at work so far. its a little heavy but not too bad, it feels solid, my biggest gripe is it requires a screen protector as it does nothing to protect that except offer a little bit of extra space

I bought the Amazon renewed premium phone. I am not happy as they advertised something that weren't true or misleading 1. Its mentioned as dual sim phone but it does not have two physical slots. There is an option to add an e-sim. 2. It is mentioned under special features that it has "expandable memory" but there is no slot. I belive its false unless they mean customizing the RAM as expandable memory. 3. No USB connector was provided. 4. Charging the phone is super slow. Phone is not bad for the price. It does not show any bugs or irregularities or weird activities so far.

Two tempered glass screen protectors are included for the Samsung S20 Ultra but neither would allow "reading" of fingerprints to log in. I removed all fingerprints from the log-in memory, applied the screen protector each time, then tried to re-enter my fingerprints into the reader, but neither screen protector allowed re-entry of fingerprints. On the positive side, however, the tempered glass application with the enclosed installation frame makes applying the glass the easiest of any I have ever used. The company just needs to manufacture the screen protector without the sticky substance in the fingerprint circle that seems to be blocking re-entry of fingerprint. By the way, the Samsung S20 ships with a screen protector already applied. But it apparently is not tempered glass. It had no problem accepting fingerprints until I applied these two tempered glass screens from Foval. Their product description clearly states that the screen is "Compatible with Fingerprint Scanner," but what they sent me was clearly not compatible.

I'll start with the pros. I like that it was sleek and seemless on the edges and sat flush with the case. Super easy to install. Privacy function was good. I like how the lens protector doesn't protrude passed the case. Cons. It will not read fingerprints, it's a finger print magnet, screen protector came right off 2 day after I installed it, I can't use the flash because it sets off a hazy glare. I've followed the direction as it said on the instruction guide. But that too was needs editing. It is an okay screen protector if you do not use the biometric finger print security. But

I thought these glass covers looked pretty nice, but I’ve been kind of underwhelmed. Firstly, on both of them you can see a line through the top and left hand side, a line that no amount of cleaning will get rid of. It’s always there, and is really distracting. You can see it in the attached photo. Also, I have a black watch, and chose to use the black cover first. Within a week, the black covering had started to scrape away from the metal underneath. I’ve since switched to the clear one, and it’s working well enough, but I hate that flaw along half of the outside.

Recieved package in a timely manner. The case itself was a little too chunky for my tastes and it looked to me like it would be the kind of soft plastic & rubber you'd get with an otterbox but it was the very slick plastic. The case didnt fit my Edge exactly. It took me a few tries to get the case on and when i finally did I couldnt properly press in the sleep/volume buttons on either side of the phone. The kickstand was really hard to extend, I almost had to pry it out of the back of the case to get it open. Pretty decent design but not my cup of tea.

This case is probably one of the prettiest being offered right now but unfortunately it doesn't offer me the protection I'm looking for. The part of the case surrounding the screen seems to come up higher than the screen and I may have given it a chance until I saw that the case doesn't offer protection around the S pen area. This is a deal breaker for me after having an LG stylo that had a pen slot that I dropped. It hit the ground on the pen slot part and jammed the pen in the slot so hard that it got ejected and I couldn't put the pin back in. I definitely don't want to take this kind of risk with my s23 Ultra. Sad to see it go but it's a must . 3 stars for possibly being protective on the edges.

I have always wanted to try one of these and so when I got it I was excited. My work phone which is a Android Samsung S20 went onto it first, when I pulled it off the next morning it was a ting very weird, never has done that since I've had the phone. I then placed my Samsung S21 and it had to be positioned just right to pick up the charge bit it did and charged fairly fast. Overall I am happy with the product wish it was easier to find the charging point where they would marry up perfectly.

I got the case with a white, purple and bluish flower design for the back of the phone. The print of the flowers is pretty but some of the white flowers printed out very light and looks like it did not print out correctly. Not pretty. I don't know if that was how they were suppose to be or not but I think it would of looked nicer if they all were the same print. The print seems to be lasting and is colorful. The case itself seems to be durable and has not changed colors. I had other clear cases that turned yellowish over time. It was easy to install and is easy to get on and off and fits my iphone 11 nicely. There is no space and does not slip. All of the buttons on the phone are easy to use when the case is on it. The back of the case has the slot for the two lens. Over all I like the case but would not buy the same flower design I got - there was many other designs to pick from.

In terms of protection, this case is great. However, in ease of use, not so much. The points of connection, i.e., the power and the headphone jack are a major disappointment. With the case on the only type of cord that will work are the ones designed to go with apple products. So good bye car charger, goodbye my Bose noise canceling headphones, and goodbye to the ear protector headphones I use when working with loud machinery. So the times my phone is most vulnerable when working out doors on the mower, etc. are the times that I cannot use the case. My previous Lifeproof case allowed Non-apple products to be used with the case on. This is a real deal breaker for me and I will not be buying another.

This plug sits nice and neatly, flush against the wall, but when I plugged it in, I got a pretty large spray of sparks one time, and one of the normal USB plugs doesn't appear to work for me at all. The other two work well, and because I'm not too comfortable leaving it plugged in all the time, I use this as backup while I'm out and about. As it offers little in terms of flexibility, requiring the user to potentially carry an extra wall adaptor piece that can fall off in traveling, and not having a simple rotating wall plug, I can't imagine that too much thought or quality control went into this product. The flexibility of potentially fast-charging up to three devices at once, in a neat little package is tempting, especially at this price, but I think you can probably find something much more reliable with a little research.

I got these for my 6yo's Ace 3 Fitbit. He can't put the wristband on so he has an elastic band. The elastic is fabulous, but it leaves the face of the fitbit exposed. This fits wonderfully, however it gets even more scratched than the fitbit. He's worn it less than a week, and you can no longer see the time or step count, or anything else. The dirt/dust seems to get between this protector and the fitbit too, and makes it even worse. I had high hopes for this and the concept, fit, and clarity are wonderful. After wearing it even a couple days, it's so scratched that you can't see the fitbit display. Disappointing.

This Case is huge, I have big hands, unless you're a lumber Jack, you're probably not going to like this Case. Imagine an OtterBox but not, I came fom a G7 to the OnePlus 8. The G7 is slightly larger , but with this case the one+ beats it by a Mile. Imagine the note 3 with an otter box that's what this phone now feels like. I have to stretch to reach the otherside of my phone..not good. However, if you like having a small house around your phone, this is a nice Case. I'll try it for a week, see if I can get used to. Maybe the buttons will losen up a bit by then. Update: it's been a week, and this case still isn't nice, I've since discovered it's kind of slippery, I like to hold my phone on my shoulder to my ear when I need both hands, doesn't work with this case, there's no texture on the back, missed the mark on that one..I suppose you could sand it a bit. But probably just buy a better Case

I've had this phone for about a week so that is my disclaimer but here is what I've found as the pros and cons of this phone: Pros: -Does get 4G on At&t network. -Screen size is large and design is sleek. -Android formating for easy use for previous Android users. -Comes with screen protector and case. Cons: -Not enough personalized features (able to select different text tones for different contacts with S4) -Screen is not very scratch resistant (buy screen protectors you'll need them) -No text preview options. -Standard email app is a joke. (downloaded mymail app) I'm still finding my way around this phone but overall it's a decent phone for the price. It doesn't have every bell and whistle, but has enough to get the job done. I bought a 32gb sd card when I purchased the phone and I'm still able to have all the same apps and media that I had on my S4.

It feels somewhat cheap but it looks good. This is also for the larger Apple Watch 5s I believe. My girlfriend got me my watch as a gift and said she got the smaller one because the bigger one was only 4mm bigger. I think this band was meant for the bigger model because you'll see a little bit of metal sticking out on each side once you slide it into place but it's not too noticeable and could be mistaken as fashionable? It also comes with a thing to remove links and instructions so it's pretty simple to make adjustments.

The fingerprint reader with this screen protector works great. But that's because it has a small outlined circle on the protector where the fingerprint should go. I'm not sure if it's thinner glass there, but it's very noticeable when you apply the protector to your phone. That was never mentioned in the description. Also, for whatever reason, the touch screen didn't work consistently. Sometimes, I had to press relatively hard, or multiples times to get an app to respond...which can be annoying. The fingerprint reader part worked great, but the rest of it struggled to read my finger consistently (maybe it was too thick). Also, it was difficult to apply it without any air bubbles and I always had a rainbow prism effect streak across my screen...which is also annoying. Anyways, I had to return it because the fingerprint circle silhouette ruined the beautiful screen of my phone, and the touch sensitivity just wasn't up to par (And yes, I turned my touch sensitivity on my phone to max)

Eh, better than most products out there, and what a great price! But the little shortcomings of quality really makes a big difference. The arm: Everything about it is great, but towards the base (towards the clamp), either the screw is not set tightly enough (for all i can tell it is tight), and there is huge motion, OR the joints towards the clamp are weaker. Either way, it results in large swings of motion instead of staying rigid. I'm not talking about inevitable small vibrations, but large, 30 degree range of position because of this one issue. So much of it is good, but it's like a chain with a weak joint that makes the entire chain much worse. The mount: It comes sticky, and there is a very clever suction mechanism. But it doesn't stay. at least not on my car deck. Maybe on a very smooth, even surface it might, but not on my car's somewhat textured panel. I hoped the stickiness would make up for it, but it only stuck on for a day. I didn't even have the phone on it. I really hope the base of my arm is an individual defect, rather than something plaguing all units. What a disappointment.

Great case, but they should have made the hole on the bottom where you charge the phone larger. I got this case right at the time of my 4s purchase and noticed most of my charging cables weren't staying in good - they didn't quite make a latch therefore too easy to pull out (ie. picking up the phone to talk on it would pull charging cable out of phone). After a while I figured out this was because the cables weren't quite going in all the way because the opening for them wasn't big enough, therefore no secure latch. If all you use are OEM iPhone charging cables, no worries. If you use 3rd party cables, this case is a pain only for that reason.

I bought this screen protector when I first got my iphone 12 pro three years ago. It's worked great the past three years, and the only reason I replaced it was I finally managed to crack the screen protector. It saved my phone's screen. Three years ago, installation was simple, no air bubbles, and the protector fit the screen perfectly. After installing it today, I can't say I recommend the product anymore. I see a lot of reviews with what I dealt with today: a ton of tiny air bubbles, and the screen protector does not encompass the phone screen entirely as it is too small. I used all three screen protectors provided, and only on the last one was it decent enough to use. I know I bought the right size advertised for my phone. Not sure what has changed over the past three years, but spend the extra couple dollars elsewhere for better quality and less headache.

Works well with iphone4 and it was easy to set up out of the box. However, the manual needs more information, or maybe the website should host the info since the device has improved since its release--that is to say, now, there are apps (namely Vlingo, free) that can allow you to speak a text message (or facebook update) using the S4 speakerphone. But getting the S4, Vlingo and the Iphone to all cooperate and do that is not straightforward the first time around. Also, Vlingo does some things for free and others you have to pay for. So I updated my facebook status using the S4 from the car (free) but theres a one time fee to send text messages, and I havent subscribed yet.

At first I loved this case. The color matches exactly the color of my iPhone 5C. Seems waterproof. Protects my phone from drops and spills. But one big problem. The MUTE switch on the side does not work. It turns the ringer OFF and I am not able to turn it back on. I have to take the case completely off, switch the ringer back on, then put the case back together. Then, every couple days I notice that my phone isn't ringing anymore and it's because the little slider-switch on the side has turned the ringer off again and I can't turn it back on unless I open the case back up. Sigh...I wish these knock-off companies would test their products better before putting them on the market.

This case is a standard TPU case, but what bothers me a bit is that the cutouts in the case are not aligned very well with the ports and holes on the Moto E5 Play. No ports or holes are completely covered, but for example, the cutout at the top of the case isn't centered on the microphone (?) hole, so the microphone hole is at the very edge of the cutout instead of centered in it (see the picture I uploaded). The same is true for the microphone hole at the bottom of the phone; it's also off-center from the cutout in the case. Also, the cutout for the micro-USB port is too small for the standard charging cord that's included with the Moto E5 Play. The fit of the actual micro-USB metal plug is fine, but the shoulders of plug (the black plastic surrounding the actual metal plug) are too large to fit into the cutout of the case. Thus when you plug in the charging cord, the shoulders of the plug push on the case, and the plug doesn't sit flush with the bottom edge of the device. To fix this, I had to enlarge the micro-USB cutout in the case with scissors so that the plug would sit flush with the device. This was a lot of work for a $7 case, and I had to do this twice for 2 cases.

I bought the Otter Box Commuter case and loved it. The only problem was I needed a case that had a belt clip so I purchased this one. The case itself is great. Excellent protection. My problem is the belt clip/holster is the worst design I have had since I bought my first cell phone back in 1992. This "holster" does not lock the phone in properly and allows the phone to fall out at any time without any provocation. I have not dropped a phone since 2005 and have never broken a cell phone. I started using this holster/clip yesterday and so far my phone has fallen SEVEN times. If it were not for the great design of the case itself my phone would have been broken. For the price of this case and the good reputation of Otter Box this thing should be built like a tank. There is no excuse for the bad design of this unit. I gave this three stars for the case design and took two off for the terrible belt clip design.

Looks good but not very comfortable. Had the urge to move it often. Large channels on side that makes contact with skin Im guessing to allow moisture to move. Very thick because of the rubber material they used and the aforementioned channels. The leather is actually laid in to the rubber strap and set by adhesive. This isn’t a very expensive band so don’t expect superb craftsmanship. The leather is already starting to come up in spots and adhesive is coming out, I’ve only had this for a few weeks and worn it a few times. There is also some excessive play where the band inserts into the sides of the Apple Watch. Again it was a pretty inexpensive band but maybe save your money and go for something that’s a little better built.

wanted to ditch having 3 different chords on my bed side table so i got this and the idea is great but it only charges my watch fully. it’s never consistent with how much it charges my phone (iphone 11). it usually charges it up to around 50-60% and no further, it charged it up to 100% once? forget about the airpods, it just flashes blue and won’t charge them. if this worked the way it’s supposed to i’d give 5 stars but it’s proved to be a a hassle given i need to find a way to charge my phone by noon.

Aftet a couple of weeks of use, I do like this phone handle, it's far sturdier than the stretchy elastic ones. The plastic isn't quite silicone, but is soft enough to form around your finger to give a firm grip when you tighten it. The metal grommets are a little bulky, and make a bit of an irritating sound when put on hard surfaces. The one big issue I have that may lead to me giving it up is the edges, they're quite thin and have been causing my cuticles to peel due to small cuts. I'm hoping the edges with soften up/dull over time, but it is quite uncomfortable at the moment.

Only gave 3 stars because it works sometimes but it falls out at least 3 times a day for me and as someone who is constantly driving for a living it gets frustrating when you’re trying to use your GPS and your phone falls on the floor while you’re trying to drive. If you have an iPhone XR or similar sized phone with a case on it (I have a lifeproof case on mine) I wouldn’t recommend it. It’s hard to stretch the device enough for it to fit the phone to begin with and when it does fit it’ll only hold for so long. It’s very hard to get it to grip properly on a phone that size. The description should not say it’s a universal device. There is a size limit.

This case is a great bright color of true red but it fits so loosely on the Galaxy Reverb 950 that it falls off and causes one to lose grip on the phone. If it were to fit, the case would have a good rubber feel that should help you hold onto the phone. I tried placing it over top of a hard case thinking it might then add the rubbery grip, yet, even though it's such a loose-fitting case it's not loose enough to go over a close-fitting plain hard plastic one. Openings align well at least, but I'd go for a more expensive jelly skin that is better fitted for your Galaxy Reverb.

About standard for a leather phone wallet. Doesn't seem to block reception and fits perfectly in the shell. Some people were complaining about this but it actually fits right and more importantly it doesn't disturb the touch area of the screen whatsoever. The pictures for this item are wrong and show a different type of shell casing. Maybe for the non-pro model of pixel 6? However, there are two significant concerns of mine regarding this case. The first and most importantly is there's hardly any room for credit cards or money in the wallet portion of this case. I should always be careful with it so that I don't bend the cover closed when it's in my pocket because there is a significant bulge from all the cards and money. My other leather case was able to handle this quite well. The second concern I have is that the name of this item is absolutely ridiculous. Seems that someone was just making up random words when they decided to apply this name to the product itself. It's very cheap sounding. Feel like this wallet should be priced closer to the $20 range. Maybe $25 at most. Edit: And yes the case certainly does smell terrible and it's very noticeable and the smell gets all over your hands and does not go away. Other people have complained about this and it certainly is true, I can confirm it. It's a very strong smell of some kind of leather product. It's not a bad smell necessarily, but it's very intrusive. I don't want this smell all over my hands constantly all over everything It touches.

Got this for 11 pro when the phone was brand new. Nice looking case. But the phone would sleep, drop calls all the time. I’d be in the middle of writing a text and phone would shut down. I thought for sure I had a lemon phone or serious software issues. I was about to reset phone to factory when a friend suggested I take it out of the case first. I did...No more issues. Phone works perfectly. After realizing it was the case, I played with it a little and it appears that when the flap is open and against the back of the phone, that’s where I have issues. I can only conclude it’s got something to do with the magnet. Pity, because I really do like case very much.

Don’t get me wrong, I love Spigen’s products, I’ve used their cases and screen protectors before. When I was installing the screen protector, I followed each step carefully, even waiting longer than 30 seconds to take off the hole sticker, but upon removing the protective film on the screen protector, I noticed multiple air bubbles, some small ones around the lower middle of the screen, and two large ones on the ends of the white bar. I used the included squeegee to try and remove them, but to no avail. I thought to myself “oh, I must have done something wrong, let me try again”. So I used the other screen protector and tried again, but the same thing happened. I know it may look small, but it doesn’t look good to me, it just looks ugly in my eyes.

So I bought this case and it was like described I had it for about a month and it's fallen apart. I only dropped my phone on a hard surface one time and the plastic got bent, the rubber part is now incredibly faded and falling off. That might be in part of I had to take it out of the case everytime I used it in my car for the radio. I don't reccomend this case if your going to spend this kind of money on a case you might as well just buy an otterbox. Definitely not buying a Speck case in the future.

Look ska great, Had to put scotch tape on side of phone and on the bottom to hold the screen protector on the phone in place so the phone would not get marked up. Put oil on the sides a bit and pushed the phone in. The tape is still on the sides of the phone and I pulled the tape off just a bit on the bottom of the iPhone so I could hear calls. Someone else may have a better way of putting the phone in the case so keep reading but this is how I did it.

Good: Good Looks Decent Battery Backup Bad: Sleep Tracking is way off Pedometer is way off too I was surprised that it consumed 22% battery while I slept for 7 hours. The sleep tracking is also all wrong. Though I am sleeping at 11 PM for two consecutive nights it had recorded me sleeping from 2:30 AM. The pedometer is also very poor. It over calculates the number of steps by at least a factor of 1.5. I am OK with the smartwatch not having NFC, GPS and Heart Rate Sensor as I bought it knowing fully well what it has and what not. It is very disappointing that the pedometer and sleep tracking is not even as good as the mi-fit 1 band. I hope there will be software fix for this.

So I got this case maybe a month ago. It's soo cute and I like that the melting part looks more realistic compared to other melting cases. It provides pretty good protection as well. The reason I didn't give it a 5 was because when the case is on I get little to no wifi and my signal going from 5 bars to maybe 3. The material interferes with the antenna going around the phone. Not sure if it affects ALL carriers though. I' with AT&T by the way. So now that case is just there collecting dust; currently waiting for my new case made of TPU to come in.

The product I purchased is an Iphone 7plus rose gold marble case. I purchased this product 4 months ago. This is a really good phone case. It protects the back, sides and partially the front of the phone. It holds tight to the phone so the phone does not fall out. My biggest issue with the case is that the back is very smooth which makes is prone to slipping out of your hand. When the phone falls the case protects it from any possible damage. The front of the phone case is transparent and so are the volume and power buttons. Long term use makes this part of the case dirty. The marble design is very pretty and it matched with the outfit needed for a specific event. This case makes the Iphone 7plus look smaller which I do not appreciate. The phone case has not been damaged due to falling nor has it lost its shape. The designs on the back of the phone case also hasn’t worn away. The headphone jack/charging port slot is a little too small. The headphones and charger fit but it is a very tight fit.

Within a few days to a week the strength of the lock on the spin of the spinner ring and the close of the camera lense cover dropped significantly. Nothing that made it useless, but wildly disappointed at how quickly the quality depreciated. I just went to pick up my phone and flipped the ring up and it broke clean off. I bought this case in May and it's September now. Didn't even last 6 months! I appreciate this case's features and want it to last. I've accidentally dropped my phone a couple of times and the case kept it safe every time. I'm bummed that I feel like I need to buy a new case already. When I first bought this case I was also driving deliveries and using maps on my phone regularly. Had a magnetic car mount, but the phone was too heavy/big for the magnet to keep a good hold on the parts of this case that are supposed to be for that purpose. UPDATE: mere days after writing this update the company reached out and offered to send a replacement. The replacement has been sent. However, I live overseas now and I will wait a little longer for its arrival.

I purchased two of these. After opening the box I went to install the screen protector and the glue used on the tags was so good it would not peel without tearing and leaving half on the protector. Wouldn't have thought much to it but the second one did the same thing. See my original review below; my opinion on this product has improved after having it for a few months now. Overall, I'd give it 4.25 stars or so as a product and given the low price, it gets 5 stars now. I've had about 10 charging cases for various iPhone models that were similar in design to this one. I started out liking this one the least, but now I like it the best. With the others, invariably, the lightning male connector would break. Also, if you insert a headphone into the lightning female port, then it would break easily with the result that you couldn't use headphones. Both lightning ports are going strong and it charges my phone consistently well. I have no complaints. Some advice: 1. Take your phone in and out of the charging case only when necessary. Each time you do, you have a chance of breaking the connection between them when you reinsert the phone. 2. Be super careful when putting the phone into the case. 3. Be really careful when putting headphones into the charging case. For example, don't have headphones and run with your phone bouncing everywhere as you'll be more prone to break the headphone insert. == The connection of the battery case with the iPhone is not good. You have to insert it just right. The slot for the phone to connect with the battery case is a little tricky to get to line up correctly. However, once it's properly inserted into the phone, it works ok.

The color of the case matches the pictures on Amazon. I like that it has a small lip to wrap around the screen -- I need that extra room since I don't have a screen protector! The case fits my iPhone SE really well, and is a good material to grip. I like the rubbery texture, which prevents my phone from sliding around if put on an uneven surface. It does not block the speaker, charging ports, or any part of the screen. The one downfall to this case is durability. I have had the case get easily scratched when dropped on pavement or when rock scrambling. I spend a lot of time hiking with my phone in my pocket - this case does not hold up well when rubbed against hard jagged surfaces like rock. It protects the phone, as the plastic layer underneath takes no damage, but the rubber portion has started to peel. I imagine not everyone is as rough with their phone as I am, so if you are not often putting your phone on or near hard jagged surfaces, this case should have no issues!

As for the functionality- the case has protected my iPad well. The hand strap fits my hand comfortably and has been very convenient. The rotatable kickstand was a big selling point for me, but isn’t exactly like I had hoped. It works great while propping up my iPad in the horizontal position, but not so great vertically. Vertically, it lays back too much and the kickstand tends to close/ collapse on its own. Also, the screen protector will protect my iPad screen from getting scratch, but it is very thin and flimsy. As for appearance- it’s not exactly pretty or “nice” looking, but I do like the silicone around the outside.
